title: Improve large-board interaction latency
description: Caches primitive and trace lookups instead of rescanning the full Circuit JSON during hover and navigation. Camera updates are also limited to one React update per animation frame. The spatial index preserves original primitive order, so overlapping same-layer hits keep their existing selection priority. Median of six fixed-build runs, compared with the three-run baseline, on the 100,548-element TMDS62LEVM fixture:  Interaction  Before  After  Speedup   ---  ---:  ---:  ---:   Hover  489 ms  58 ms  8.5   20 zoom events  1,366 ms  699 ms  2.0   20 drag steps  1,766 ms  384 ms  4.6   React render time during navigation  1,997 ms  90 ms  22.3
body:
Caches primitive and trace lookups instead of rescanning the full Circuit JSON during hover and navigation. Camera updates are also limited to one React update per animation frame.

The spatial index preserves original primitive order, so overlapping same-layer hits keep their existing selection priority.

Median of six fixed-build runs, compared with the three-run baseline, on the 100,548-element TMDS62LEVM fixture:

| Interaction | Before | After | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Hover | 489 ms | 58 ms | 8.5× |
| 20 zoom events | 1,366 ms | 699 ms | 2.0× |
| 20 drag steps | 1,766 ms | 384 ms | 4.6× |
| React render time during navigation | 1,997 ms | 90 ms | 22.3× |

- [Fixed Sitara preview](https://pcb-viewer-git-perf-reduce-sitara-interaction-latency-tscircuit.vercel.app/?fixture=%7B%22path%22%3A%22src%2Fexamples%2F2026%2Fwebgpu-tmds62levm.fixture.tsx%22%7D)
- [Original repro preview](https://pcb-viewer-git-repro-sitara-interaction-latency-tscircuit.vercel.app/?fixture=%7B%22path%22%3A%22src%2Fexamples%2F2026%2Fwebgpu-tmds62levm.fixture.tsx%22%7D)

title: Add pcb_stackup element for fabricator stackup and material data
description: Adds a new pcb_stackup element to Circuit JSON for carrying resolved physical layer data alongside the board, allowing consumers to access material properties without needing to re-resolve templates or read side files.
body:
## Why

Downstream projects such as `0hmX/am3352-ddr-eye` keep board construction and material properties in a separate `board-construction.json` / `simulation.json`. This PR adds `pcb_stackup`, so Circuit JSON can carry the resolved physical layer data alongside the board. A follow-up in core/props will resolve a fabricator template code, such as JLCPCB `JLC04161H-3313`, and emit the full stackup. Consumers can then use those values without re-resolving the template or reading a side file.

## Schema

- Identifiers: `pcb_stackup_id`, `pcb_board_id`, optional `subcircuit_id`.
- Optional `plated_hole_copper_thickness`: the copper thickness of plated hole and via barrel walls.
- Required `layers`, ordered top to bottom, discriminated by `layer_type`:
  - `soldermask`: `thickness`, `relative_permittivity`
  - `copper`: `layer` (`top`, `inner1`, …, `bottom`), `thickness`, `electrical_conductivity_s_per_m`, `rms_surface_roughness`
  - `dielectric`: `dielectric_type` (`core` | `prepreg`), `material_name`, `thickness`, `relative_permittivity`, `loss_tangent`, `dielectric_properties_frequency_hz`

Lengths accept existing unit strings and are normalized to mm. Physical values must be finite and positive. Roughness and loss tangent may also be zero. When `electrical_conductivity_s_per_m` is omitted, consumers may assume 5.8e7 S/m (annealed copper).

Board thickness and copper weight are not duplicated here: `pcb_board.thickness` already holds the board thickness, and each copper layer's `thickness` holds its resolved value.

## Example

Two-layer board, top to bottom, lengths in mm:

```json
{
  "type": "pcb_stackup",
  "pcb_stackup_id": "pcb_stackup_1",
  "pcb_board_id": "pcb_board_1",
  "plated_hole_copper_thickness": 0.02,
  "layers": [
    { "layer_type": "soldermask", "thickness": 0.01, "relative_permittivity": 3.5 },
    { "layer_type": "copper", "layer": "top", "thickness": 0.035, "electrical_conductivity_s_per_m": 58000000 },
    {
      "layer_type": "dielectric",
      "dielectric_type": "core",
      "material_name": "FR-4",
      "thickness": 1.51,
      "relative_permittivity": 4.3,
      "loss_tangent": 0.02,
      "dielectric_properties_frequency_hz": 1000000000
    },
    { "layer_type": "copper", "layer": "bottom", "thickness": 0.035, "electrical_conductivity_s_per_m": 58000000 },
    { "layer_type": "soldermask", "thickness": 0.01, "relative_permittivity": 3.5 }
  ]
}
```

## Tests

Each file contains a single test:

- `pcb_stackup_jlc_template`: a JLC04161H-3313 fixture parses through `any_circuit_element`, units normalize to mm, and the JSON round trip is stable.
- `pcb_stackup_optional_material_properties`: optional properties are retained, and zero roughness and zero loss tangent are accepted.
- `pcb_stackup_required_fields`, `pcb_stackup_invalid_layers`, `pcb_stackup_invalid_physical_values`: missing fields, unknown layer types or refs, and zero, negative or non-finite values are rejected.

The README has a new `PcbStackup` section, generated with `bun run generate-docs`. Only the stackup section is committed, without unrelated regeneration drift.

## Validation

`bun test` (475 pass), `tsc --noEmit`, `lint:zod`, `check-snake-case`, `build`, `format`: all pass.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: feat: retain the footprint origin independently of copper bounds
description: Adds optional footprint origin to PCB components, allowing for independent placement from copper bounds while maintaining backward compatibility with older records.
body:
Supports tscircuit/core#4628.

Add optional `pcb_component.footprint_origin`: the footprint-local (0, 0) point after placement, expressed in board-world mm (+X right, +Y top, +Z above; right-handed). Keep `center` as the copper bounds center and keep placement-anchor semantics unchanged. Older records omit the field and remain valid.

Core will emit the point, circuit-json-util will transform it with its component, and KiCad will use it as the footprint origin. Those consumer changes are separate PRs and must wait for this schema to be published.

Validation: the new parse regression fails before the fix and passes afterward; all 495 tests, TypeScript and build pass. Regenerated only the affected PCB component documentation section to avoid unrelated generated-doc changes.

title: feat: add isRouteViaCoveredByPhysicalVia geometry helper
description: Add isRouteViaCoveredByPhysicalVia to check whether a physical via covers a traces layer transition at the same coordinates and with compatible diameters.
body:
Add `isRouteViaCoveredByPhysicalVia` to check whether a physical via covers a trace's layer transition at the same coordinates and with compatible diameters. For example, a top-to-bottom via can cover a top-to-inner1 route transition. The helper uses Circuit JSON layer names and supports either transition direction; missing or unknown spans do not establish coverage.

Electrical connectivity remains a separate caller check. The helper has no KiCad types or dependencies.

Extracted for [the review on circuit-json-to-kicad #697](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-kicad/pull/697#discussion_r4335446786). The converter will consume the exported helper after release through a separate tscircuit dependency upgrade.

Validation: all 162 tests pass locally, including geometry mismatches, reversed direction, and partial-span coverage. Typecheck, build, formatting of changed files, and diff checks pass. The repository-wide formatting check fails on the unchanged `package.json` `files` array formatting, which is identical on `main`.

title: Reproduce missing pin 1 orientation for slightly skewed two-pad footprints
description: Reproduces a bug where the analyzer fails to determine pin 1 orientation for slightly skewed two-pad LED and diode footprints due to small coordinate differences, without changing the analyzers functionality.
body:
## Motivation
Imported two-pad LED and diode footprints can contain tiny coordinate differences between pad centers, even when the pads are intended to form a horizontal or vertical row. analyzePcbPin1Location currently treats these footprints as diagonal and returns null.


Core therefore cannot populate pin1_location, leaving downstream assembly and pick-and-place tools unable to verify or adjust the orientation of polarized components. The analyzer should tolerate small import rounding errors while continuing to reject genuinely diagonal footprints.

This PR only reproduces the issue. It does not change the analyzer.

- Uses the exact imported LED and diode pad geometry.
- Generates SVG snapshots directly from those fixtures and the analyzer's current output.
- Uses `test.failing` to document the expected `topside_left` result without treating the current `null` result as correct.

### LED rectangular pads

![LED pad-center skew](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GokulPandi-M/circuit-json-util/feac5eb2e9419d7e1b73e4c803313a4f1fdd210e/tests/__snapshots__/repro-imported-two-pad-pin1-skew-led.snap.svg)

### Diode polygon pads

![Diode pad-center skew](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GokulPandi-M/circuit-json-util/feac5eb2e9419d7e1b73e4c803313a4f1fdd210e/tests/__snapshots__/repro-imported-two-pad-pin1-skew-diode.snap.svg)

Validation:
- `bun test` — 150 pass, 0 fail
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`
- `bun run format:check`

`package.json` only contains the formatting required by the repository-wide format check. The same formatting-only change was included in the recently merged reproduction PR #222; the current `main` formatting workflow otherwise fails on this file.

title: fix: transform the footprint origin with its component
description: Applies the existing PCB transformation matrix to the footprint origin of PCB components, ensuring it remains attached during transformations.
body:
Supports tscircuit/core#4628. Depends on tscircuit/circuit-json#913.

Apply the existing PCB transformation matrix to `pcb_component.footprint_origin`, exactly as for its other board-world points. This keeps the authored origin attached to the footprint under rotation, reflection, packing and group repositioning. No separate transform is reconstructed in core.

Validation: all 157 tests (4 snapshots, 3,099 assertions), TypeScript and build pass. The new regression fails without the implementation. Uses the #913 schema preview only for development; replace it with the published version after #913 merges. Keep this PR draft until then.

title: Add autorouterThreads to platform configuration
description: Platforms can now specify a local autorouting thread request with platformConfig:  autorouterThreads: 4 . The optional value must be a positive safe integer: 1 requests inline solving, and omission preserves the host default. Parsed values are preserved alongside cloudautorouter settings; browsers remain single-threaded. This PR defines the config contract; supporting hosts must consume it to activate workers. Includes input validation coverage and regenerated READMEprops overview documentation. Ran all four required generation scripts; full suite: 712 passed, 0 failed. Type checking, formatting, and package build pass.
body:
Platforms can now specify a local autorouting thread request with `platformConfig: { autorouterThreads: 4 }`. The optional value must be a positive safe integer: `1` requests inline solving, and omission preserves the host default. Parsed values are preserved alongside cloud/autorouter settings; browsers remain single-threaded. This PR defines the config contract; supporting hosts must consume it to activate workers.

Includes input validation coverage and regenerated README/props overview documentation. Ran all four required generation scripts; full suite: 712 passed, 0 failed. Type checking, formatting, and package build pass.

title: Explain required bounds for invalid symbol viewboxes
description: Adds validation for symbol viewboxes to ensure they contain required bounds, improving error diagnostics for malformed inputs.
body:
Stacked on #947, the malformed symbol viewbox repro.

Malformed viewboxes now produce one error at `viewbox`: `viewbox requires { minX, maxX, minY, maxY } bounds in the local symbol coordinate space.` A typed shape check runs before the existing distance and increasing-bounds validation. Valid input types, unit parsing, fit modes, and defaults stay the same. All generated documentation is included.

Validation:
- The repro fails on unchanged main and passes with this fix.
- All 712 props tests, full props typecheck, package/declaration build, formatting, and all four generation scripts pass.
- An isolated core integration emits the new message in its existing `source_failed_to_create_component_error`. All eight existing custom-symbol sizing/rotation tests pass with the built props package.
- This improves diagnostics for invalid input; it does not add `{ x, y, width, height }` aliases or change valid symbol geometry.

The rotation-field follow-up is separate: `schematic_component` has no supported `rotation` property in Circuit JSON; rotation is already applied to custom-symbol geometry and ports. No unsupported field is added.

title: Add props for external IBIS transient simulations
description: Add typed ibismodel, analog.digitalstimulus, and analog.eyediagram declarations plus per-experiment IBIS pin states on analog.transientsimulation.
body:
Add typed ibismodel, analog.digitalstimulus, and analog.eyediagram declarations plus per-experiment IBIS pin states on analog.transientsimulation.

Models use the shared ibisModelAsset object, explicit vendor component/pin/model names, modelValueCorner, and includePackageParasitics. Pin states use isOutput and output-only isOutputEnabled booleans. The existing spiceEngine="pcb_spice" selects the separately invoked PCB extraction/SPICE backend; no executionMode prop is added. Existing native transient defaults remain unchanged. Rendering does not fetch assets, install tools, or execute simulation.

Companions: https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/pull/908 and https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4765. Publish the props release before updating core's dependency pin.

Validation: all 687 tests pass, plus TypeScript and package build. New tests cover Asset shape, explicit model settings, Boolean pin states, backend selection, digital timing, and eye gates.

title: Add polarized option to generic capacitor footprints
description: Adds a polarized option to generic capacitor footprints, allowing for a positive pin marking and specific silkscreen placement without altering existing pad geometry.
body:
Adds `.polarized()` / `_polarized` to generic `cap` footprints. Opting in draws a 0.15 mm silkscreen + beside pin 1, with at least 0.25 mm clearance from copper and body paths. Default/disabled capacitors retain their existing output and pad geometry.

```ts
fp().cap().imperial("0603").polarized().circuitJson()
fp.string("cap0603_polarized").circuitJson()
```

A standalone, smaller alternative to #927: this PR includes only the generic-capacitor flag and its positive-pin-1 marking. It adds no positive/negative pin remapping and changes no radial/electrolytic generators. The cap builder exposes the flag, and the passive definition schema retains it. Contradictory polarized/nonpolarized selections are rejected. Existing origin/rotation and `nosilkscreen` options apply to the new mark.

Validation: **646 tests pass**, production build and changed-file format check pass. New SVG snapshots cover four sizes, opt-in/default/disabled behavior, through-hole holes, transforms, and disabled silkscreen. No new documentation files.

title: Fix nonparallel flex tails in the 3D viewer
description: Fixes rendering issues in the 3D viewer for flex PCB tails with nonparallel bend axes by updating flex-utils and restoring Float32 boundary precision.
body:
Separate encoder and connector tails with nonparallel bend axes fail in the live viewer because it does not supply the board outline needed to resolve independent moving regions. Update bundled flex-utils to 0.0.8 and pass the board-local outline to its existing folding implementation.

Restore Float32 boundary precision when adapting native Three.js meshes so rounded tail edges are classified on the correct moving region instead of remaining flat and forming spikes. This adapter handles Three.js storage precision and mesh transforms; bend-region selection, fold ordering, deformation and CAD transforms remain in flex-utils.

The **Flex PCB → Independent Tails** fixture has a 180° encoder return, a separate 90° connector bend, component markers and stiffeners. Its fractional tail edge reproduces the precision bug. Open [Folded](https://3d-viewer-git-fix-nonparallel-flex-preview-tscircuit.vercel.app/?path=/story/flex-pcb-independent-tails--folded) or [Flat](https://3d-viewer-git-fix-nonparallel-flex-preview-tscircuit.vercel.app/?path=/story/flex-pcb-independent-tails--flat); right-click **Fold PCBs** to switch states. Regression tests share the fixture and check tail positions, CAD fold/unfold, textures and edge precision.

Apply the repository formatter to the four existing workflow/documentation files reported by CI, including CRLF normalization; workflow behavior is unchanged.

Dependency publication: flex-utils 0.0.8 currently publishes only to GitHub Packages. The public npm registry returns 404, GitHub Packages requires authentication, and jscdn serves tarballs rather than npm registry metadata. Keep the working versioned CDN dependency until flex-utils is published to public npm; replacing it with a bare version now would break clean installs.

Validation: CI passes Format Check, Type Check and Test Node Bundle Load (including the flex regression tests). Repository-wide formatting and the production build also pass locally.

title: repro: PCB note rectangle ignores parent chip rotation
description: Reproduces a bug where the PCB note rectangle does not rotate with its parent chip, demonstrating the issue with a test case and snapshot.
body:
Rotating a chip by 90° rotates its pads, but its `<pcbnoterect>` stays horizontal. The snapshot shows the unrotated rectangle on the left, the bug in the middle, and an equivalent `<pcbnotepath>` rotating correctly on the right.

title: fix: preserve polygon pad offsets in PCB flex layout
description: Fixes polygon-pad overlap in PCB flex layout by accurately calculating bounds for nonrectangular polygons and circular primitives, ensuring proper spacing between pads.
body:
Fixes the polygon-pad overlap reproduced in #4671, found while building [Done Dot](https://tscircuit.com/Devesh36/done-dot). With `pcbFlexGap={0.8}`, the imported TVS parts overlapped by **0.6224 mm** instead of leaving a **0.8 mm gap**.

Layout was rebuilding bounds from centered pad dimensions, bypassing the existing polygon-bounds method. It now asks each primitive for its board-space bounds. The existing corner transform moves into the default primitive implementation; polygon pads reuse their existing calculation from transformed vertices. This removes duplicated code and also gives accurate bounds for nonrectangular polygons at arbitrary angles. Circular primitives transform only their center, preserving diameter-based bounds under rotation and bottom-layer reflection.

### Before
![Imported polygon pads overlap](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/core/f0a5872fdf24ce15c366c1747574b7b77d4e5829/tests/repros/__snapshots__/repro-imported-tvs-polygon-flex-overlap-pcb.snap.svg)

### After
![Both pad representations keep the requested gap](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Devesh36/core/fb19f207f0d050728e8dbbed08b34371a0cccf80/tests/repros/__snapshots__/repro-imported-tvs-polygon-flex-overlap-pcb.snap.svg)

The existing polygon example snapshot is updated because the corrected bounds also correct its centering; restoring the old SVG causes its test to fail. The additional regression uses offset triangular pads at 0°, 45°, 90°, 180°, and 270° on both layers and compares component bounds with emitted copper. The previous implementation fails this test by 0.707 mm at 45°.

The circular-bounds regression covers SMT pads, plated holes, unplated holes, and vias at 0°, 45°, 90°, 180°, and 270° on both layers. It reproduces the review finding: a 2 mm pad at 45° previously reported 2.828 mm bounds. It also checks that a neighboring pad separated by 0.2 mm is not falsely considered overlapping during port matching.

Validation: the circular-bounds regression, existing polygon-layout tests, and rectangular/polygon pad-rotation tests pass. TypeScript and formatting pass. The broader primitive suite had 290 passes, one skip, and one schematic-title test exceeding the default 5-second timeout; that test passes when rerun with a 30-second limit.

Related work: draft #4806 addresses the same polygon-bounds bug within a larger CAD-origin change. This PR fixes it independently using the existing world-space bounds method; reconcile the overlap if either PR lands first.

title: fix: rotate LED silkscreen rectangles with their footprints

Fixes the LED outline rotation reproduced in #4622. Rotating C540985 or C540986 by 45° now rotates the silkscreen rectangle together with its pads.

This PR records the current behavior and passes without the fix. It contains only TSX tests and generated snapshots. Chips and both jumper implementations also emit the point because they override normal component rendering.

Use actual polygon vertices for local pad bounds so circle and polygon versions of the contact report the same copper extent. Preserve the bounding-box `center` used by placement checks. No hand-written layout transforms or renderer compensation.

body:
Add native TSX declarations for IBIS models, binary traffic, and eye requests, exporting them as Circuit JSON for the local PCB extraction/SPICE runner. Existing spiceEngine="pcb_spice" selects that backend; no executionMode prop or execution_mode record field is introduced. The built-in render phase skips that backend while native experiments continue to execute.

Models use the shared Asset object and explicit vendor component/pin/model names. Core maps port labels to physical source_port_id values, translates Boolean direction/output-enable states, and preserves the requested IBIS data column and package parasitics choice. Reference roles identify physical supply/clamp ports. Duplicate physical pin mappings, unmapped reference/model keys, stimuli without an enabled output, and pin states without exactly one model binding are rejected. Model binding validation runs after all declarations render, so JSX order does not matter.

Dependencies / merge order: https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/pull/908, https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/945, then this PR. The verified preview pins must be replaced with published versions before merging. The repository dependency guard remains unchanged.

Validation: all 43 targeted simulation tests pass, including eight IBIS integration tests and a PCB snapshot. Schema/props suites pass (479 and 687 tests). Independent Opus review confirmed the schema review changes and both additional pin-binding fixes. TypeScript and the package build (ESM and declarations) pass. GitHub build, smoke-test, type-check, and all ten test shards pass. No new enums, ternaries, docs, or README edits are included.

Rendering does not fetch assets, install tools, or execute external solvers. CLI/local-runner wiring and CSV/HTML result commands remain follow-ups. No Python or solver binaries are added; the prototype backend's three-selected-trace limit is unchanged.

title: fix: rotate polygon plated holes in PCB SVGs
description: Fixes the issue where rotating polygon plated holes in PCB SVGs does not rotate their copper outlines and offset drills, ensuring they move together with the pad group during rotation.
body:
Rotating polygon plated holes currently leaves their copper outlines and offset drills unrotated in PCB SVGs, even when Circuit JSON supplies `ccw_rotation`.

Apply the rotation to the enclosing pad group so the copper, drill offset, and drill orientation move together. Use the same negative SVG angle and pad-center pivot as existing pad and hole renderers. Update polygon bounds and pin-number placement to follow the same rotation.

This PR builds on repro #868 in GitHub Stack #870. It updates the existing single snapshot from the buggy output to the correct 90° rotation, and removes `test.failing` so the rotation assertions pass as a normal regression test.

Validation: the focused snapshot test and formatting checks pass. The full suite passed with 466 tests (1 todo), along with TypeScript and build checks.

Rotation compatibility review: 20 related tests passed. An additional local audit passed 176 cases across all four drill shapes, covering omitted/zero, positive, negative, and full-turn rotations, offset drills, pin-label positions, and bounds. Its 22 comparisons with the existing rotated SMT rectangle and plated pill renderers also passed.

Fixes #709. Companion to tscircuit/core#4804, which supplies the rotation metadata.

The snapshot records the current bug: both pads render horizontally even though the second pad specifies `ccw_rotation: 90`. The test also asserts the expected rotated bounds and is marked `test.failing` because those rotation assertions fail with the current implementation. title: fix: check trace thickness against its own routed copper
description: Fixes incorrect warnings when traces sharing a net request different widths by ensuring checks are made against their own routed segments.
body:
Fixes #456.

Two correctly routed traces sharing a net may request different widths. Previously a 0.8 mm request was checked against another branch’s 0.2 mm copper and incorrectly warned. Match copper through `pcb_trace.source_trace_id` so each request checks only its own routed segments. Existing neck-down and interpolated-width calculations remain unchanged. Three older fixtures now declare their intended owner; no IDs are inferred or manipulated (Seve’s #132 review).

TSX-derived regressions cover correctly routed mixed-width branches, a genuinely undersized 0.4 mm control, and legal 0.2 mm pad neck-downs on a nominal 0.8 mm trace. Both constant-width and tapered neck-downs pass the width checker and aggregate routing checks. A zero escape budget control still warns on the owning trace.

All four SVG snapshots use the shared circuit-to-svg board renderer, including board outline, components, pads, copper, and width labels. Warning centers are mapped from board-world mm (+X right, +Y up) into SVG pixels (+Y down) using a composed `boardToSvgTransform` and `applyToPoint` from `transformation-matrix`, following handbook rule 7. The four snapshots were visually inspected and refreshed for the font change already merged in #455; copper geometry and warning locations are unchanged. No dependency declarations are changed by this PR.

Validation against current main: all 675 tests pass (8,232 assertions); TypeScript and formatting pass locally. The complete PR is checked by CI. Both original regressions fail before the ownership fix.

Repro: 7bdfc7b. Fix: #458, merged into this branch. **Review this complete PR against main.**

title: fix: accept independent Flatten instances in copper contact checks
description: Fixes copper-contact DRC crashes when checks and a geometry producer load independent Flatten instances by reconstructing foreign polygons with the local Polygon constructor through Flattens supported JSON representation.
body:
Copper-contact DRC crashes at `edge.distanceTo(candidate.shape)[0]` when checks and a geometry producer load independent Flatten instances. Reconstruct foreign polygons with the local `Polygon` constructor through Flatten’s supported JSON representation inside the existing per-pass cache. Containment, spatial indexing and distance checks then use compatible shapes. Local polygons retain the existing path, and inputs remain unchanged.

Stacked on #459. Its TSX fixture is reduced from the actual RP2040 BLDC motor-controller board: the original bottom GND trace, two vias, and surrounding filled copper-pour contour. The trace coordinates, width, and generated outer/inner contours match the board export. This PR changes the assertion from the exact core-generated routing crash to zero errors for that same circuit. Native before/after PCB snapshots show the DRC result for the retained geometry.

Existing contact tests cover local, mixed and foreign polygon pairs, reversed arguments, repeated calls, tangent arcs, gaps, holes, multiple faces and empty polygons. No dependencies or DRC rules change.

- Type checking and changed-file formatting pass.

title: fix: include child schematic sheets in KiCad project downloads
description: Fixes the issue where downloading a hierarchical KiCad project only included the root schematic file, ensuring all child schematic sheets are included in the download.
body:
## Before

Downloading a hierarchical KiCad project included only the root `.kicad_sch` file. A project with seven child sheets therefore contained just 1 of the 8 required schematic files, leaving the child-sheet references unresolved.

## After

The ZIP includes the root schematic and every child schematic returned by `getOutputFiles()`. The root filename is passed to the converter so child-sheet references and any renamed child files stay consistent.

## Implementation

- Add all converter-generated schematic files directly to the existing ZIP download function.
- Update `@tscircuit/internal-dynamic-import` from `^0.0.15` to `^0.0.20`, which includes the KiCad declarations published after [internal-dynamic-import#42](https://github.com/tscircuit/internal-dynamic-import/pull/42) merged.
- Use `SupportedModuleMap["circuit-json-to-kicad"]` for the loader's KiCad module type.

## Validation

- Full Bun suite: 417 passed, 5 skipped, 0 failed.
- Typecheck, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- GitHub test, formatting, and typecheck checks passed; Vercel deployment succeeded for `0243fbc`.
- Downloaded `Smartwatch` v1.0.14 through **Download → KiCad → Project** on the [Vercel preview for `0243fbc`](https://tscircuit-hcmzm1r6c-tscircuit.vercel.app/anil08607/Smartwatch#files). The actual browser-downloaded ZIP passed its CRC check and contains all 8 schematics (root + 7 child sheets), with all 7 child-sheet references resolving to files in the archive. PCB/project files and 21 3D-model files are also present.
- KiCad CLI successfully exported all 8 sheets from the downloaded project to SVG.
- External-model limitation observed during the preview download: `C51927172.step` could not be fetched. The ZIP still downloaded successfully; this check confirms schematic completeness, not completeness of external 3D assets.

description: Add project-configured iframe tabs to dev and static sites, allowing external pages to be configured as RunFrame views and refreshed automatically during development.
body:
External pages currently cannot be configured as RunFrame views or refreshed automatically during development. Add project-configured iframe tabs to dev and static sites, and a generic dev feed that delivers changed URLs without reloading the parent page.

- Configure tabName, iframeUrl and optional mainComponentPath in project configuration.
- Poll validated tab descriptors once per second with sequential requests, no caching, navigation cancellation and recovery after a cached-page restore.
- Report failed refreshes visibly while keeping the last valid descriptors; recover automatically. Serve only tab descriptors, never the rest of the configuration.
- Keep static site output fixed and honor --ignore-config. Preserve current standalone/offline bootstrap behavior.

Reuses and extends the work from closed #5352 on current main. Source conversion and URL creation belong to a separate project-specific producer; the CLI has no SysConfig, private viewer or TI dependency.

Validation: 52 focused tests pass, covering existing runtime configuration flows, static-site builds, injection/escaping, live updates/removal, invalid configuration and error recovery, sequential requests and browser lifecycle races. TypeScript, repository formatting and the CLI build pass. Real-browser testing confirms an edited pedometer pin changes Output → Input in the embedded viewer without refreshing the parent or reselecting the tab. Rapid edits discard superseded producer results; failed source generation preserves the successful URL.

Rollout prerequisite: RunFrame PR https://github.com/tscircuit/runframe/pull/5788 is merged. Its release workflow published 0.0.3031, but that exact version is still unavailable from npm as of the merge check on 2026-10-20. Version 0.0.3030 does not include the extra-tab feature. Keep this PR draft until 0.0.3031 is installable, update the RunFrame dependency and selected tscircuit browser bundle, and validate against those released artifacts. Local acceptance uses the documented RUNFRAME_STANDALONE_FILE_PATH option, without committing local package links or an invented version.

title: Add Pipeline9 high-density solveAsync using SolverRuntime
description: Pipeline9 can route independent high-density batches through a host-owned SolverRuntime while retaining its existing synchronous solvestep behavior.
body:
Pipeline9 can route independent high-density batches through a host-owned SolverRuntime while retaining its existing synchronous solve/step behavior.

**Merge #3155 first.** It contains only the two Bun version upgrades, pinned to 1.4.3. This branch is based on that prerequisite, with separate commits for the runtime implementation and the complex-board parity test.

The new default-effort dataset18 sample01 test covers 115 connections, 279 obstacles, and 205 routed traces. It runs a fresh synchronous solver and a second solver with **four native Bun workers**, with caches disabled. Strict worker mode rejects unavailable registrations/startup failures; 146 dispatched batches prove the test exercises worker execution.

The checks require:
- Byte-identical complete routed SRJ, with no coordinate rounding, ID normalization, sorting, or tolerance.
- Exact high-density routes before downstream phases can hide differences.
- Identical high-density statistics and phase/pipeline logical iteration counts.
- Successful routing, unchanged source input, and a sufficiently complex board.

Both complete outputs have the same SHA-256 hash, printed in the test log. The checked-in snapshot renders both independently produced boards with the standard relaxed-DRC overlay: **UNTHREADED on the left, 4 THREADS on the right**. Both show zero relaxed-DRC errors.

![Dataset18 sample01: UNTHREADED versus 4 THREADS](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/7e27c8e680d68feb239ce2b191d1b15d65f2e7df/tests/features/__snapshots__/pipeline9-srj18-sample01-thread-parity.snap.svg)

Run it with:
```sh
bun test tests/features/pipeline9-srj18-sample01-thread-parity.test.ts --timeout 300000
```

A subprocess fixture bypasses the test suite's SVG preload, which replaces global Worker with Node's adapter, so this test exercises Bun's actual native worker pool. The visual snapshot is separate from the exact data comparisons.

Runtime behavior: registered four-node tasks commit in serial node-pop order; budget-crossing tasks replay the exact remaining prefix. Preloaded-copper dependencies remain serial. Bun/Node factories embed generated worker bundles; default/browser imports remain inline and exclude worker payloads. The host owns runtime disposal, and worker errors reject.

Validation: seven focused test files / 105 assertions pass locally on Bun 1.4.2; the final complex snapshot also passes without snapshot-update mode. Build/DTS passes. Local full typecheck retains the same 67 pre-existing dependency diagnostics as the Bun-only baseline, with none added. The snapshot was rendered and visually inspected. CI uses Bun 1.4.3 via #3155.

The repro uses a checked-in Circuit JSON fixture generated from a real bottom-mounted SOIC-8 board. Its original JSX is included as a comment in the test. The test creates a small STEP model locally and snapshots the exported board using the repo's existing dependencies. No `tscircuit` dependency or production-code changes are needed.

Biome is pinned to `2.5.15` because CI otherwise fails to load its Linux binary before checking formatting.

### Expected vs actual

The orange body should occupy Z = −3.8 to −0.8 mm. The export places it at Z = −0.8 to +2.2 mm on a 1.6 mm board.

![Expected bottom placement versus actual STEP export](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Devesh36/circuit-json-to-step/02bbfcc876176f2362491121be35c14b8e7b62b7/bottom-mounted-step-component.png)

Left: an independent reference render checked against the existing 3D converter's geometry. Right: the actual STEP export. This is a repro, not a fixed exporter.

![Current exported STEP snapshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Devesh36/circuit-json-to-step/18a99c7bb48fc60b22eb99784452275edfd093b7/test/repros/bottom-mounted-step-component/__snapshots__/bottom-mounted-step-component.snap.png)

description: Fixes inline label attachment points on routed traces to ensure accurate alignment and attachment, preventing misplacement when labels span jogs in the traces.
body:
Inline labels spanning a short bend can have an `anchorPoint` outside their routed wire. Keep the collision-checked text box, test center/left/right attachment positions against the same trace using the existing `tracePathContainsPoint` helper, and return the matching `textAnchor`. Continue the existing placement search if none fit.

This supports cleaning up [the inline-label converter PR #658](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-kicad/pull/658). Together with [the core change](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4811), it supplies an exact wire attachment and alignment so the converter can remove nearest-wire detection and attachment-point guessing.

Stacked on the repro PR #1344. In Files changed, open `repro-core-tb67s579ftg-inline-label-attachments-detail.snap.svg`: the blue points move onto the wires while the dashed text boxes and routed paths stay unchanged. Both OUT_A_P and OUT_B_P were 0.1 mm off-wire before this fix. The fixture is core's existing TB67 breakout with only J4 moved through normal layout props.

The existing bent-route snapshots use the same guide rendering before and after. This PR adds on-wire and alignment assertions and updates those snapshots. A separate straight-wire close-up uses the same captured input to check that ordinary vertical connections keep their centered attachment.

Vertical coverage: open `repro-core-tb67s579ftg-vertical-inline-label-attachments-detail.snap.svg` in Files changed. It comes from a vertical layout of core's existing TB67 circuit using normal schematic props, with the same components and connections. OUT_A_P attaches at the lower end of its text and OUT_B_P at the upper end. The solver's dashed text boxes and routes stay unchanged; both blue dots move onto their wires. `left`/`right` are alignments in the text's reading direction, so they become lower/upper ends for vertical text.

Straight vertical wire coverage: `repro-core-tb67s579ftg-vertical-inline-label-attachments-straight-detail.snap.svg` is added directly in this PR's Files changed. It shows STOP_DET_VTH and NFHYS from the same TB67 input, with dashed text bounds and blue attachment points on the straight wires. The test checks two-point vertical paths and centered, on-wire attachments.

Validation:
- Local follow-up: `bun run format:check` (installed Biome 2.5.15), both TB67 attachment tests, the updated-base gimbal test (63 assertions total), and `bunx tsc --noEmit` pass. The repository's original `^2.2.2` Biome dependency range is unchanged.
- Full `bun test`: 721 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` and `bun run build` passed.
- Restoring the original implementation makes the new on-wire assertion fail at 0.1 mm; restoring the fix passes.
- Snapshot geometry comparison confirms identical wire paths and text positions in the close-up; only attachment points move.

Merge the repro first, then this fix. Core PR https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4811 consumes the attachment/alignment after the solver is released. No Circuit JSON schema change is needed.

Straight vertical stub coverage: `repro-core-tb67s579ftg-vertical-inline-label-attachments-straight-stub.snap.svg` shows the real AGC_OUT terminal from the same TB67 input. The test checks its two-point vertical path and on-wire attachment. This solver anchor was already correct before the fix, so its before/after stub snapshots are intentionally identical.

Main-branch cross-check: the same input was run against solver main `b4dbf4f`. All inline text centers and dimensions match the fix; the bent-route attachment points change. Core main `f0a5872` produces an identical SVG with either solver version. The OUT_B_P overlap seen in core's PNG rendering also exists with both main versions; it is not introduced by this solver fix. Vertical examples remain in this solver stack.

title: Fix automatic release version-bump PRs
description: Fixes the automatic release version-bump process to ensure proper versioning and publication of releases without errors.
body:
Unblocks publication of #126, which fixes tscircuit/core#4703 (existing solver repro: #127).

Normal releases check out `github.sha`, leaving detached HEAD. After pver commits the release version, create-pull-request treats that release commit as its working base and creates no version-bump PR. The [0.0.67 release run](https://github.com/tscircuit/copper-pour-solver/actions/runs/37087843368) published successfully but logged that its bump branch was not ahead of main.

Check out the attached `main` branch for normal releases so the bot preserves the version commit. Explicit recovery tags still take precedence, retaining #83’s recovery path. This follows the existing branch checkout → pver release --no-push-main → bot PR/auto-merge flow used by the shared plop template, CLI, and circuit-json.

Align package.json once from 0.0.56 to the already published 0.0.67 so pver can select 0.0.68; otherwise the existing ten-tag collision limit [stops publishing before PR creation](https://github.com/tscircuit/copper-pour-solver/actions/runs/39170393887). Subsequent bumps use the existing bot workflow. No tags are deleted or republished.

Validation: the actual pver 0.0.43 and create-pull-request v5 branch code were exercised against temporary local Git remotes. Detached checkout produces no PR diff; attached main creates a branch containing 0.0.68, with remote main unchanged. No npm package was published during validation. After removing the checkout test requested in review, all 106 repository tests pass (4,131 assertions), and formatting passes. The previous TypeScript and ESM/DTS build checks passed.

Fix #129 is merged into this branch. **Review this complete PR against main.** Production publication and bot auto-merge still need verification after main merge. No eval dependencies were changed.

title: fix: deduplicate route transitions covered by physical vias
description: Fixes duplicate route transitions by ensuring that only unique physical vias are exported, reducing the number of exported vias from 10 to 6 when they overlap at the same positions.
body:
Fixes #676. Stacked on #696; merge the repro first, then retarget this PR to `main`.

A physical via and the route transition using it could both become KiCad vias. With `tscircuit@0.0.2984`, the repro has 6 physical vias, but the original converter exports 10 entries at 6 positions. This fix exports 6.

Preserve every `pcb_via` and omit its route copy only when the electrical connection matches and `isRouteViaCoveredByPhysicalVia` confirms matching position, compatible dimensions, and layer coverage. The geometry helper comes from `@tscircuit/circuit-json-util@0.0.125`, supplied by the existing `tscircuit` dependency after #723. The converter-local geometry method is removed. Physical vias use `layers`; route transitions use their `from_layer`/`to_layer` span.

`AddNetsStage` uses `getFullConnectivityMapFromCircuitJson` to index existing KiCad nets by Circuit JSON element ID without changing their names or numbers. `AddViasStage` reads that shared map after net initialization. Route-only duplicates must match their full span, connection, and exported dimensions, including the existing defaults.

The repro imports the main `tscircuit` package. Dependencies and refreshed snapshots are inherited from `main` through #696; this PR adds no direct utility dependency.

Validation:
- The repro passes on both branches: 6 physical / 10 exported vias on #696, and 6 physical / 6 exported vias here, at 6 distinct positions.
- All 5 focused via regressions pass, covering connectivity, distinct nets and dimensions, and omitted versus explicit defaults.
- Typecheck, build, formatting of tracked source files, and diff checks pass.
- The full local suite ran 228 tests: 224 passed; four generated-system schematic SVG comparisons failed. The same four failures reproduce on the updated base converter without this fix. No schematic snapshots were changed for this PR.

body:
Standalone `pcb_note_text` disappears during KiCad PCB export. This TSX-generated board places `BOARD NOTE` directly on the board and `FOOTPRINT NOTE` inside U1's footprint. Both notes exist in Circuit JSON, but the serialized and parsed KiCad board contains only `FOOTPRINT NOTE`. The converter implementation is unchanged.

Motive: Preserve board-level notes when exporting a PCB to KiCad.

| Note | Expected | Actual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `BOARD NOTE`, without `pcb_component_id` | Text remains in the exported PCB | Missing |
| `FOOTPRINT NOTE`, owned by U1 | Text remains in the exported footprint | Preserved |

The data-only test checks the serialized PCB using the repository's `test.failing` convention. It accepts either board graphics or footprint text, so a future fix is free to choose its representation. The passing visual test checks that both source notes exist with the intended ownership, verifies the supported footprint-note control, and compares Circuit JSON with the native KiCad render. bun test tests/pcb/repros/repro35-standalone-pcb-note-text.test.ts tests/pcb/repros/repro35-standalone-pcb-note-text-snapshot.test.ts

To expose the defect directly, temporarily replace `test.failing` with `test` in the data-only test. It fails at `expect(texts).toContain("BOARD NOTE")`, receiving only `["FOOTPRINT NOTE"]`. Restore the marker after checking the failure.

Validation: both tests pass with the expected-failure marker (7 assertions total); the snapshot matches on a second run and was visually inspected with KiCad 10.0.5. title: fix: preserve filled copper footprint polygons
description: Fixes the issue of missing filled copper footprint polygons during import, ensuring all antenna copper polygons are preserved.
body: Preserves filled copper footprint polygons dropped during import, fixing the issue reproduced in #259. **Before:** antenna copper is missing; only the two pads remain. **After:** all 12 antenna copper polygons and both pads are preserved. Copper layers use the existing `getLayerRefsFromLayers` mapper. The shared polygon path reads typed `Xy`/`PtsArc` nodes and approximates arcs for copper and annotations while preserving placement order. title: Detect transistor LED misalignment
description: Detects misalignment between a transistor and LED in a rail-to-rail indicator branch, ensuring proper alignment for electrical connections.
body:
Q2 and LED4 in the ESP32 GPS tracker's NETLIGHT indicator are separated with perpendicular connected terminals. `TransistorLedAlignmentSolver` emits `TransistorLedNotAligned` when a typed LED and transistor in a rail-to-rail indicator branch cannot read as a straight facing connection.

Stack: #335 (TSX repro) → this solver PR. Merge the repro first. This stack is independent of the fuse/connector stack.

![Tracker indicator before and after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/28d4e1f4337530a8fd835abc40a9a542e91266a8/tests/cases/__snapshots__/transistor-led-alignment-correction-comparison.snap.svg)

The proof comes from [pixalynx/esp32-gps-cellular-tracker v1.1.0](https://tscircuit.com/pixalynx/esp32-gps-cellular-tracker?version=1.1.0#schematic). The corrected TSX rotates Q2 and LED4 into a direct vertical branch, aligns R20 with its transistor terminal, and turns/repositions R16 so its supply terminal is above it. Component values, native symbols and all source electrical records are preserved. Tests also verify visible wire continuity. The complete four-part extract reports **zero findings from all analyzers** after correction.

The committed comparison includes all three original findings, with the original and corrected circuits at equal scale, a divider, red markers and diagnostics below. The original repro and a separate complete corrected-network snapshot are retained. This is an extracted network; the full published board has other findings.

The rule requires native `simple_led`, NPN/PNP `simple_transistor`, and a series `simple_resistor` between opposite declared power/ground rails. It uses typed metadata, connectivity and drawn terminal directions; names, labels, hints and pin numbers do not establish roles. It accepts horizontal or vertical straight connections and compact local bends. Separation must exceed the larger of 2 schematic units or twice the LED's largest dimension, with 0.15 units of lateral tolerance for facing pins. Ambiguous/branched connections, feedback, DNP/DNC, conflicting rails, overlapping bodies, separate scopes and incomplete geometry are skipped.

Existing coverage is demonstrated explicitly: fixing only the R20/Q2 alignment and R16 orientation leaves this LED/transistor finding. The low-side-load solver requires a different chip-load/clamp network, and #282's single-pin extension requires already-horizontal facing terminals. [SIM800 Hardware Design v1.09, page 47, Figure 43](https://simcom.ee/documents/SIM800/SIM800_Hardware%20Design_V1.09.pdf#page=47) illustrates a vertical LED/resistor/transistor branch; its resistor is on the other side of the LED, so the proof retains the published board's own connections rather than copying that circuit.

Validation: **273 tests pass**, plus typecheck, build and formatting. Guards cover renamed names/hints/pin numbers, rail flags, branched/feedback connections, missing/duplicate geometry, DNP/DNC, scope, rotation/reflection, compact bends and alignment tolerance. Both corrected SVGs were rendered and visually inspected. Existing unrelated snapshots, dependencies and timeouts are unchanged.

title: Detect fuse connector misalignment
description: Detects misalignment of fuse connectors and ensures proper alignment with grounded two-pin headers in schematic designs.
body:
F_QI is left of J_QI on the phone-stand board, but both connected terminals face right. `FuseConnectorAlignmentSolver` emits `FuseConnectorNotAligned` for a separated fuse and grounded two-pin header whose private connection cannot read as a straight facing wire.

Stack: #337 (TSX repro) → this solver PR. Merge the repro first. This stack is independent of #335 → #336.

![Fuse and connector before and after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/3024cc40fbc491b1519a0b756fa22c0d7529399c/tests/cases/__snapshots__/fuse-connector-alignment-correction-comparison.snap.svg)

The TSX proof comes from [Devesh36/usb-c-phone-stand-light v0.0.6](https://tscircuit.com/Devesh36/usb-c-phone-stand-light?version=0.0.6#schematic). The correction uses the existing `schFacingDirection="left"` prop on J_QI and moves F_QI onto the terminal axis. Its original symbol, footprint, pin order, fuse ratings and source electrical records are preserved. Tests verify continuous drawn wiring as well as connectivity. Full analysis of the complete two-part extract reports **zero findings** after correction.

The committed before/after comparison uses equal scale, a divider, red markers and diagnostics underneath. The snapshot helper accepts an optional panel height to keep this shallow network compact; existing callers retain their original height. The original repro and a separate complete corrected-network snapshot are retained. This is an extract, not a claim that the entire published board is clean.

Detection uses `simple_fuse`, `simple_pin_header`, private connectivity, an explicitly grounded second connector terminal and drawn pin directions. No names, labels, hints or pin numbers establish electrical roles. The rule accepts horizontal or vertical straight connections and compact bends. Separation must exceed the larger of 2 schematic units or twice the fuse's largest dimension; facing pins allow 0.15 units of lateral tolerance. It skips branches, ground-path fuses, conflicting rails, larger headers, DNP/DNC, overlapping bodies, separate scopes and ambiguous geometry.

Current analysis reports zero findings on the original extract. The existing connector-detour rule requires multiple signal connections, and #282's single-pin extension requires already-facing horizontal terminals. The fuse/diode rule handles a different component pair. [TI DRV8701EVM User's Guide, page 8, Figure 8](https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/slvuag3/slvuag3.pdf#page=8) shows the supporting convention in the upper-left USB–UART block: H9's power pin and F1 share a straight horizontal wire. The convention is facing terminal alignment, not a mandatory left/right direction.

Validation: **269 tests pass**, plus typecheck, build and formatting. Guard tests cover renamed names/hints/pin numbers, rail metadata, branched connections, missing/duplicate geometry, DNP/DNC, scope, rotation/reflection, compact bends and tolerance. Both corrected SVGs were rendered and visually inspected. Existing unrelated snapshots, dependencies and timeouts are unchanged.

The shared helper intersects physical/global/all owning-bus restrictions. The pipeline uses an inferred surface restriction only in its private routing view; public input, constructor parameters, output declarations and supplied copper are preserved. Uncovered signals, empty domains and inner-carrier inputs keep their existing paths. The pipeline diff primarily moves internal reads to that private view.

Both reproduction assertions pass. title: Reproduce per-bus surface layer domains and AM3352 DDR dispatch mismatch
description: Reproduces a bug related to per-bus surface layer restrictions and AM3352 DDR dispatch mismatch without claiming a routing fix.
body:
Stacked fix: #67.

Per-bus surface restrictions are handled differently from equivalent global restrictions. A TOP-only native connection gets no candidate carrier from `signalLayers`; the exact 46-signal AM3352 DDR input selects generic routing with 800k iterations, while redundant global TOP/BOTTOM selects shared-surface routing with 8m iterations.

Adds a minimal reproduction, a hash-verified unchanged native CLI capture, and a dispatch reproduction. Both scripts support `--assert-equivalent` and intentionally exit 1 on this baseline. The test records current behavior so the reproduction PR stays green; the stacked fix will replace it with the corrected expectation.

Validation: minimal test, TypeScript and formatting pass. Production routing is unchanged. The capture's native run exhausted its budget after 22m35s; the explicit-surface controls also did not produce a complete solution. This is not a claim that normalizing layers finishes DDR. No failed or partial copper images are included; existing successful legacy snapshots/proof remain untouched.

body:
Imports the pcb-spice-pipeline implementation (previously developed in `0hmX/pcb-spice-pipeline`) into the tscircuit org, with its full commit history.

## What it does
Native tscircuit TSX → routed PCB geometry → FastHenry/FasterCap extraction → `@tscircuit/ibis-to-spice` → ngspice → measured waveforms and eye diagrams. Runtime is plain code, no LLM.

- `src/` — geometry extraction, RLGC matrices, SPICE assembly, native IBIS consumption, eye-diagram metrics, CLI (`pcb-spice-pipeline`), `--repeat` determinism check
- `scripts/` — pinned native toolchain setup (`setup-tools.py`), plotting, `prove`/`audit-eye` repeatability proofs, `reproduce.sh`
- `examples/` — straight trace, routed AM3352 JSON, and the real AM3352 DDR TSX eye example
- `tests/` — unit tests plus native/real-board integration tests
- `vendor/` — experimental `@tscircuit/core`/`props` IBIS builds and `ibis-to-spice` tarball
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — Linux CI (not yet exercised; the proof was run on Darwin arm64)

## Usage
```sh
pnpm exec pcb-spice-pipeline --setup
pnpm exec pcb-spice-pipeline index.circuit.tsx
pnpm exec pcb-spice-pipeline --repeat index.circuit.tsx
```
Runnable board project: https://github.com/0hmX/am3352-ddr-eye

## Testing
```sh
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm typecheck && pnpm test && pnpm test:native
```

The filter uses a plain `"layer" in element` check and explicit top/bottom layer matching, with no `Extract` type predicate or type assertions.

Fabrication notes remain **off by default**, addressing the review. Enable them with **View → Show Fabrication Notes**; explicit and saved visibility choices are preserved.

Reproduction: open `/tests/fabrication-note-visibility/` in Vite and enable fabrication notes. It contains a board, two pads, a body outline, polarity text/path, and a top-only dimension. Before the fix, the bottom FAB canvas contains painted pixels even though no bottom FAB records exist. After the fix it contains zero. Add `?layer=bottom` for the reverse case. The top fixture has “TOP FAB +”, a 6 mm dimension, a wide body, and a triangle; the bottom fixture has “BOTTOM FAB 1”, a 4 mm dimension, a tall body, and a diamond. The snapshots intentionally use different artwork so the two sides are easy to distinguish. The Chromium regression checks both sides, default-off behavior, toggling, and persistence after reload.

| Top FAB component | Bottom FAB component |
| --- | --- |
| ![Top FAB board](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/pcb-viewer/a86189c/tests/__snapshots__/fabrication-note-top.snap.svg) | ![Bottom FAB board](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/pcb-viewer/a86189c/tests/__snapshots__/fabrication-note-bottom.snap.svg) |

Validation:
- `bun test`: 76 passed, 0 failed, 475 assertions; snapshot updates disabled.
- `bun run build`, `tsc --noEmit`, changed-file Biome formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Browser regression failed before the filter change and passes afterward. Snapshots include board/component artwork and were visually inspected.
- Separate local integration checks used the actual Runframe and tscircuit.com wrapper components with text, stroked/filled paths, rectangles, and dimensions. All six Canvas cases (three wrappers × two sides) show zero FAB pixels while disabled, 11,677 on the assigned side while enabled, and zero on the opposite side. Both wrappers forward FAB circuit data; no wrapper fix is needed for Canvas. These checks do not verify live deployments.
- WebGPU visual verification is inconclusive in this headless environment: it reports `Device was destroyed` even for a control board with no fabrication records. The existing WebGPU fabrication geometry regression passes; this PR changes Canvas filtering only.

Developed and reviewed with AI assistance.

title: Infer pin 1 orientation for slightly skewed two-pad footprints
description: Allows the analyzer to infer pin 1 orientation for two-pad footprints with slight coordinate differences, improving compatibility with polarized components.
body:
## Motivation

Imported two-pad LED and diode footprints can contain tiny coordinate differences between pad centers, even when the pads are intended to form a horizontal or vertical row. `analyzePcbPin1Location` currently treats these footprints as diagonal and returns `null`.

Core therefore cannot populate `pin1_location`, leaving downstream assembly and pick-and-place tools unable to verify or adjust the orientation of polarized components. The analyzer should tolerate small import rounding errors while continuing to reject genuinely diagonal footprints.

Repro : https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-util/pull/221
## Changes

- allow exactly two pads numbered 1 and 2 to have centerline skew up to 1% of their pitch
- retain the stricter existing behavior for multi-pad rows and genuinely diagonal footprints
- convert the merged MuseGrow reproduction into passing regression tests
- update its LED and diode snapshots to show the inferred `topside_left` orientation

title: fix: transform footprint origins with PCB placement
description: Transforms footprint origins of PCB components through the existing PCB matrix to align with physical pads during translation, rotation, and reflection, while keeping older records unchanged.
body:
Supports tscircuit/core#4628. Uses the published circuit-json@^0.0.531 release containing the merged schema change tscircuit/circuit-json#913; no preview or tarball URL remains.

Transform pcb_component.footprint_origin through the existing PCB matrix so it follows the physical pads through translation, rotation, reflection and repositioning. Older records stay unchanged. Core can emit its authored origin once without reconstructing layout transforms.

Repro: #256’s first commit. Fix: #257, merged into this branch. **Review this complete PR against main.**

Validation with the published schema: all 157 tests pass (4 snapshots, 3,099 assertions); TypeScript and the ESM/declaration build pass locally. Hosted tests, typecheck and formatting pass on the updated main-targeting head. The regression fails before the fix and covers all four quarter-turns on both faces.

Ready for review. Merge and publish this utility change before updating the dependent core origin PR to its published release. No peer or runtime dependency declarations were changed.

title: Add assembly drawing pages, part views, and title blocks
description: Adds assembly.drawing.page, assembly.drawing.partview, and optional assembly.drawing.titleblock schemas for creating assembly drawings with specified dimensions and layout.
body:
Adds `<assembly.drawing.page>`, `<assembly.drawing.partview>`, and optional `<assembly.drawing.titleblock>` schemas. Pages accept standard ISO A0–A4 / ANSI A–E sizes with landscape or portrait orientation, or explicit unit-aware custom dimensions. Named sizes resolve to mm; conflicting dimensions and invalid sheet numbering are rejected.

Part views independently select geometry via `partRef`, with explicit direction, viewport placement using `centerX`/`centerY`, hidden edges and hatched section-plane configuration. `leftOfRef`, `rightOfRef`, `aboveRef`, and `belowRef` describe inferred placement relative to sibling part views. References are nonempty selector strings; opposing references and explicit centers on the same axis conflict. Inferred axes remain undefined in parsed output; unconstrained axes default to zero. The documented layout contract places viewport edges adjacent with no implicit gap. Page-aware reference resolution, cycle detection, and position calculation remain core/exporter follow-up work.

Views automatically fit the selected geometry to their viewport; there is no `scale` prop. These are unreleased components, with no aliases for the previous `target`/`x`/`y` names. No style enum or image/artifact inputs. Enum modes use snake_case; signed-axis TSX direction notation remains unchanged.

Title-block metadata references ISO 7200:2004; sheet references are ISO 5457 and ASME Y14.1, with dimensions cross-checked against Autodesk's sheet-size documentation. Links and interoperability limits are documented. This does not claim full standards-template compliance. Core TSX registration/emission remains follow-up work.

Validation: 724 tests (7 snapshots), typecheck, build, format, and all four required documentation generators pass. Tests cover reference validation and conflicts, inferred axes, center defaults and unit conversion, required partRef, and removal of the old prop names and scale.

Related: https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/pull/918 and https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-drawing/pull/1.

title: Assembly Explosion Stage and Move Elements
description: Adds props for assembly.explosion.stage and assembly.explosion.move to enable staged disassembly and movement of subassemblies in TSX.
body:
Adds props for `<assembly.explosion.stage>` and `<assembly.explosion.move>` so TSX authors can describe staged disassembly, including moving a subassembly intact before exploding its children at the displaced pose.

Stages accept `name`, optional `nextStageRef` / `prevStageRef`, and preserved children. Moves accept `targetRefs` as a comma-separated string or an array, plus signed, unit-aware `offX` / `offY` / `offZ` normalized to finite millimeters. References are trimmed and parsed to `targetRefs: string[]`. The existing `targetRef` remains a single-target compatibility alias; supply exactly one selector prop. Empty lists and blank members fail validation. Validators and input types are exported individually and through `assemblyProps.explosion`.

The proposal documents document-order fallback, cross-assembly ordering references, accumulated motion, and automatic swept-path collision checks. This PR supplies props and validation; namespaced JSX components, stage scheduling, and collision checking require corresponding core support. No explosion container or run, detach, translate, or collision-check elements are introduced.

Validation:
- `bun test`: 676 passed, 0 failed.
- `tsc --noEmit`: passed.
- `biome format .`: passed.
- All four required documentation generation scripts completed; generated props overview included.

Approval tracking: this PR remains **draft and awaiting API approval**. Related speculative drafts are [core#4631](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4631) for constrained explosion views and PoppyGL renders, and [poppygl#49](https://github.com/tscircuit/poppygl/pull/49) for guide lines. The props/core changes remain draft pending approval; PoppyGL #49 has merged. Core uses pinned previews until the upstream packages are approved and released.

## Multiple targets

Both inputs describe one move, applying the same displacement to all targets:

```tsx
<assembly.explosion.move targetRefs="shade, collar" offZ="60mm" />
<assembly.explosion.move targetRefs={["shade", "collar"]} offZ="60mm" />
```

Core moves the union of the selected subtrees so duplicate references or parent/child overlaps do not translate a part twice. Parsed references preserve authored order; each distinct selected target can have its own guide. The proposal documents normalization, compatibility, conflicts, and grouped motion.

body:
Package previews currently rebuild the board and fetch individual component models before showing a scene. Add `glbUrl` and `glbData` inputs to `CadViewer` so callers can display a self-contained, pre-rendered circuit-json-to-gltf GLB directly:

```tsx
<CadViewer glbUrl="/previews/board.glb" />
```

This path bypasses board generation and individual model loading, restores the exporter's coordinate frame, fits the camera, and retains orbit/camera controls. Component node `extras.tscircuit` provides name tooltips, per-instance hiding, and schematic navigation without Circuit JSON. Existing GLBs without metadata still render. Geometry engine, board layer, and fold controls are omitted for baked scenes.

Source changes abort pending downloads and dispose owned geometry/materials/textures. Downloads time out after 30 seconds, failures display errors, and A-to-B-to-A source changes cannot reuse disposed scenes.

Companion exporter change: https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gltf/pull/261. No new exporter version is required to render an existing GLB; component identity features require metadata-enabled exports.

Validation:
- 12 focused tests pass for actual GLB parsing, coordinate placement, shared-mesh instance selection, schematic identity, one-request loading, load errors/cancellation, source replacement, and resource disposal, plus existing picking regressions.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` and `bun run build` pass.
- Browser-verified hover names and hiding with a regenerated rushabhcodes/fidget-counter assembly. The bundled GLB was generated from the pinned 1.0.12 Circuit JSON and 27 downloaded OBJ models using the companion exporter, with metadata for all 38 components. Hidden enclosure meshes are excluded from hover registration so parts underneath remain reachable.

This adds library support; switching tscircuit.com previews to use published GLBs is separate consumer work.

Live assembly demo: https://3d-viewer-git-feat-prerendered-glb-tscircuit.vercel.app/iframe.html?id=prerendered-glb--fidget-counter&viewMode=story

The GLB is served from `/prerendered-glb/fidget-counter.glb` on that deployment.

title: Adopt skew-tolerant pin 1 analysis for two-pad footprints
description: Adopts skew-tolerant pin 1 analysis for two-pad footprints to ensure accurate orientation detection in LED and diode components.
body:
Imported LED and diode footprints can contain two pads that are intended to form a horizontal row but differ by a few micrometers in Y. With the previous `@tscircuit/circuit-json-util` analyzer, Core could not infer that row, leaving `pcb_component.pin1_location` unset. Supplier analysis could also continue returning an older cached `null` result after the analyzer was updated.

This adopts `@tscircuit/circuit-json-util@0.0.128`, advances the supplier-orientation cache namespace, and adds a Core regression using a slightly skewed two-pad LED footprint. The supplier cache fixture now uses the same kind of skew so both local and supplier orientation paths exercise the published analyzer behavior from tscircuit/circuit-json-util#220.

This PR is stacked on the upstream `repro/footprint-origin-4628` branch because that branch already adopts util 0.0.127 and refreshes the snapshots changed by that release. Keeping this dependency explicit leaves this PR focused on the 0.0.128 pin-1 behavior. Retarget it to `main` after the base branch lands.
