title: Assembly Explosion Rendering
description: Adds a core implementation of assembly.explosion.stage and assembly.explosion.move, including multi-target moves and rendered constrained-assembly examples. The upstream props and PoppyGL changes are merged. This PR uses their published npm releases.  Multiple targets targetRefs accepts either a comma-separated string or an array: tsx assembly.explosion.move targetRefsshade, collar offZ60mm  assembly.explosion.move targetRefsshade, collar offZ60mm   Props trims and normalizes either form to targetRefs: string. Existing targetRef remains a single-target input alias; supply exactly one selector prop. Core resolves and validates every target before evaluating progress, then moves the union of the selected subtrees using one displacement in the stage owners frame. Duplicate references and overlapping parentchild selections move each part and reference surface only once. Each distinct selected target gets its own guide, anchored before the instruction moves any target. Model-less container centroids include prior independent movements of their children. All targets share the instructions progress, and evaluation leaves assembled Circuit JSON and props unchanged. !Comma-separated and array targets, shared progress, and legacy compatibility(https:raw.githubusercontent.comtscircuitcoreb16362715bac0d1e544dc2b51eb785e44770bb66testsassembly__snapshots__assembly-explosion-target-refs-annotated.snap.png)  Staged rendering getAssemblyExplosion(circuit,  throughStageRef?, stageProgress? ) derives an immutable CAD view after mounting constraints resolve. Stages use a stable topological sort with authored order as fallback; missingambiguous references, cycles, duplicate stages, and invalid move targets produce named diagnostics. Parent movement carries descendant CAD and reference-surface centers. Repeated evaluation and backward scrubbing reconstruct the assembled starting state. Existing examples lift an intact constrained cover, move it aside, and then remove its cap in the displaced subassembly frame. Frame tests cover upright, inverted, and tilted mounts against emitted reference directions, with guide endpoints checked against emitted GLTF translations. Run bun scriptsrender-assembly-explosion.tsx workassembly-explosion-preview to export those four PNGGLBJSON states.  Dependencies tscircuitprops: 0.0.707 in dev dependencies and overrides, including the merged stagemove API and targetRefs normalization. poppygl: 0.0.36, including the merged explosion guide and arrow APIs. Updated with main and resolved the package conflict. The existing dependency check is preserved and passes with these registry versions. The compatibility refresh also removes the unsupported write: false option from the existing Bun browser-bundle test; it continues to inspect the returned bundle without an output directory.  Validation 69 assembly regressions and 4 namespaced assembly regressions pass (73 total), using Bun 1.4.0 and the published npm packages. Three new tests cover stringarraylegacy selectors, shared progress, overlap and duplicate handling in a mounted frame, reference-surface translation without orientation changes, pre-move centroids, and validation of later-stage targets. Both new annotated visual snapshots were inspected and pass on comparison. Full CI is green on the updated branch: all ten test groups, full typecheck, dependency check, distribution smoke tests, package preview build, and deployment. Local package build (including declarations), 73 assemblynamespaced regressions, browser-bundle regression, changed-TypeScript formatting, and feature diff checks pass. Behavior and approval tracking are documented in docsassembly-explosion.md. This prototype supports mechanical CAD translations and rejects PCBcable-containing targets. Swept-path collision verification remains unimplemented (collisionCheckStatus: not_implemented); diagrams do not certify assembly clearance.
body:
Adds a core implementation of `assembly.explosion.stage` and `assembly.explosion.move`, including multi-target moves and rendered constrained-assembly examples.

The upstream props and PoppyGL changes are merged. This PR uses their published npm releases.

## Multiple targets

`targetRefs` accepts either a comma-separated string or an array:

```tsx
<assembly.explosion.move targetRefs="shade, collar" offZ="60mm" />
<assembly.explosion.move targetRefs={["shade", "collar"]} offZ="60mm" />
```

Props trims and normalizes either form to `targetRefs: string[]`. Existing `targetRef` remains a single-target input alias; supply exactly one selector prop. Core resolves and validates every target before evaluating progress, then moves the union of the selected subtrees using one displacement in the stage owner's frame. Duplicate references and overlapping parent/child selections move each part and reference surface only once.

Each distinct selected target gets its own guide, anchored before the instruction moves any target. Model-less container centroids include prior independent movements of their children. All targets share the instruction's progress, and evaluation leaves assembled Circuit JSON and props unchanged.

![Comma-separated and array targets, shared progress, and legacy compatibility](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/core/b16362715bac0d1e544dc2b51eb785e44770bb66/tests/assembly/__snapshots__/assembly-explosion-target-refs-annotated.snap.png)

## Staged rendering

`getAssemblyExplosion(circuit, { throughStageRef?, stageProgress? })` derives an immutable CAD view after mounting constraints resolve. Stages use a stable topological sort with authored order as fallback; missing/ambiguous references, cycles, duplicate stages, and invalid move targets produce named diagnostics. Parent movement carries descendant CAD and reference-surface centers. Repeated evaluation and backward scrubbing reconstruct the assembled starting state.

Existing examples lift an intact constrained cover, move it aside, and then remove its cap in the displaced subassembly frame. Frame tests cover upright, inverted, and tilted mounts against emitted reference directions, with guide endpoints checked against emitted GLTF translations. Run `bun scripts/render-assembly-explosion.tsx work/assembly-explosion-preview` to export those four PNG/GLB/JSON states.

## Dependencies

- `@tscircuit/props`: `^0.0.707` in dev dependencies and overrides, including the merged stage/move API and `targetRefs` normalization.
- `poppygl`: `0.0.36`, including the merged explosion guide and arrow APIs.
- Updated with main and resolved the package conflict. The existing dependency check is preserved and passes with these registry versions.

The compatibility refresh also removes the unsupported `write: false` option from the existing Bun browser-bundle test; it continues to inspect the returned bundle without an output directory.

## Validation

- 69 assembly regressions and 4 namespaced assembly regressions pass (73 total), using Bun 1.4.0 and the published npm packages.
- Three new tests cover string/array/legacy selectors, shared progress, overlap and duplicate handling in a mounted frame, reference-surface translation without orientation changes, pre-move centroids, and validation of later-stage targets.
- Both new annotated visual snapshots were inspected and pass on comparison.
- Full CI is green on the updated branch: all ten test groups, full typecheck, dependency check, distribution smoke tests, package preview build, and deployment.
- Local package build (including declarations), 73 assembly/namespaced regressions, browser-bundle regression, changed-TypeScript formatting, and feature diff checks pass.

Behavior and approval tracking are documented in `docs/assembly-explosion.md`. This prototype supports mechanical CAD translations and rejects PCB/cable-containing targets. Swept-path collision verification remains unimplemented (`collisionCheckStatus: "not_implemented"`); diagrams do not certify assembly clearance.

title: fix: preserve polygon plated-hole rotation
description: Fixes the issue where polygon plated holes did not retain their rotation during Circuit JSON reconstruction, ensuring correct rendering and alignment with the chips rotation.
body:
Polygon plated holes now emit their existing `finalRotationDegrees` as `ccw_rotation`, and Circuit JSON reconstruction restores that value as `pcbRotation`. The copper pad follows the chip's rotation and fits inside its silkscreen outline.

The production fix is two field assignments. Removes `.failing` from the test in #4830 and updates the same PCB snapshot; no regression assertions are added here. Each chip has one polygon pad with a centered drill and a surrounding outline, labeled by angle and layer. Current core already includes the renderer support from tscircuit/circuit-to-svg#869, so the snapshot visibly shows the correction without a dependency change.

Validation: all 44 focused plated-hole and Circuit JSON import tests pass, and the package build including declarations passes. The fixed regression covers nine orientation checks. Removing only the import assignment makes the imported rotations reset to zero and fails the test. Before and after snapshots were rendered and visually inspected.

Fixes #3647. Reworks the closed #4804 as the second PR in native GitHub stack #4832, based on #4830. Related prior proposal: #4727.

title: repro: snapshot polygon plated-hole rotation loss
description: Reproduces a bug where polygon plated-hole pads do not retain correct rotation, leading to copper misalignment with the silkscreen outline.
body:
At 90° and 270°, a polygon plated-hole pad stays horizontal while its chip rotates. The copper sticks outside the rotated silkscreen outline. This captures #3647 before the fix from the closed #4804.

Adds one test file and one PCB snapshot covering 0°, 90°, 180°, and 270° on both layers. Each chip has one polygon pad with a centered drill and a surrounding outline. The image explains the expectation: copper should fit inside the outline.

The `test.failing` case checks pad orientation against the emitted silkscreen outline and checks rotation preservation when reconstructing Circuit JSON. The snapshot runs in `beforeAll`, so visual failures still fail CI normally. Production code is unchanged.

Validation: the repro passes as an expected failure. Running it as an ordinary test fails at the visible 90° mismatch: expected 90°, received the default 0°. The snapshot was rendered and visually inspected.

First PR in native GitHub stack #4832. #4831 adds the small fix, removes `.failing`, and updates this snapshot.

title: Use platform autorouterThreads for local Pipeline9 workers
description: Updates props to 0.0.706 and consumes platform.autorouterThreads for local Pipeline9 routing, enabling worker-backed solveAsync for routing with counts above one, while retaining existing paths for counts of one or omitted.
body:
Stacked on #4810.

Updates props to 0.0.706 and consumes `platform.autorouterThreads` for local Pipeline9 routing. Counts above one use `solveAsync(runtime)` with the requested Node/Bun worker pool. Omitted counts and `1` retain stepped routing; browsers, cloud routing, and other algorithms retain their existing paths. `solveSync()` remains synchronous and inline even with threads configured.

Workers are disposed before completion/error events. Stopping suppresses late events, cleans workers during loading or solving, and prevents a concurrent restart until cleanup finishes. Native adapters load only on supported server runtimes; browser bundles exclude Node worker imports. Test, snapshot-test, and preview-install Bun versions move to 1.4.2 to support real workers.

Validation: 10 focused tests passed (63 assertions) on Bun 1.4.2, including actual dispatch, exact traces/full-output/iteration/statistics parity, inline/cloud/legacy behavior, failures, cancellation, and browser bundling. Native Node worker routing also matched `solveSync()` output. Focused TypeScript checks passed locally. Fresh-dependency CI preview/package build and package smoke tests passed on the functional commit; CI is rerunning after the snapshot-workflow version update.

title: fix: preserve explicit bus minLength and maxLength
description: Fixes the omission of bus minLength and maxLength from source_bus and router input, ensuring proper routing constraints are applied.
body:
Bus `minLength` and `maxLength` were accepted by props but omitted from both `source_bus` and the router input. For example, a declared 19–20 mm bus reached the solver without either bound.

Serialize absolute and relative bounds, resolve `longest_manhattan` references against placed pads, and intersect explicit bounds with the `targetLength`/`lengthTolerance` window. Reject an empty resolved interval with the bus name before routing.

Validation: 11 focused bus/routing tests pass, including an end-to-end captured SRJ and a routed 19–20 mm snapshot; relative subsets, independent bounds, zero/clamped minima and incompatible resolved windows are covered. Typecheck and package build pass. Existing target-length routing remains covered.

title: Add directional variants for the default Zener diode
description: Add directional variants for the default Zener diode, including right, up, left, and down orientations, while keeping legacy symbols unchanged.
body:
Default-size Zener diodes only provide horizontal and vertical symbols, so core selects the same symbol for opposite rotations. Add `zener_diode_right`, `_up`, `_left`, and `_down` so 90° and −90° render in opposite directions.

Reuse the existing Zener artwork and rotation helper, with `1`/`pos`/`anode` and `2`/`neg`/`cathode` aliases. Keep the legacy `_horz` and `_vert` symbols unchanged. Place REF and VAL using the box-resistor convention in every direction. Add the four generated exports and visual snapshots, check annotation placement, extend the existing polarity test, and remove the default-Zener fallback from the size-variant tests.

Validation:
- The extended tests fail before the new symbols are added.
- All 38 tests pass; build, type checking, formatting, and snapshot validation pass.
- A separate TSX smoke test with unmodified core 0.0.2196 and this local package verifies all four symbol names and emitted terminal directions. No core change is required.

Metadata-enabled GLBs retain component hiding and schematic navigation.

title: fix: pin repair03 overlap guard on current main
description: Fixes solar-chargerGame Boy quality regression caused by rolling back an entire board for one new pad contact by pinning the high-density-repair03 to the latest merged main commit, preventing new trace-to-obstacle copper overlaps while preserving independent improvements.
body:
Pin `high-density-repair03` to latest merged `main` commit `d003ab47f05b2fa4c0715ac235a54870ffdb732c` from https://github.com/tscircuit/high-density-repair03/pull/174. The repair guard prevents new trace-to-obstacle copper overlaps while preserving independent improvements: it restores only implicated connections, rechecks the complete mixed geometry, and retains the complete safe checkpoint if that candidate is unsafe or does not improve DRC.

This fixes the solar-charger/Game Boy quality regression caused by rolling back an entire board for one new pad contact. The dependency retains the geometry/via-span changes merged in repair03 #177 and the USB fix. Repair03 passes all 137 tests, typecheck, and formatcheck in CI.

Controlled relaxed-DRC comparison against the exact merged repair03 main (`fb345bc`):

| Fixture | Main | Updated pin |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| bugreport68-41562e | 6 | 6 |
| Solar charger | 3 | 3 |
| Game Boy | 27 | 26 |
| Board 1726 (macOS/Linux) | 0 | 0 |

All four boards solve. The earlier guarded pin produced 22 solar errors and 49 Game Boy errors; those regressions are resolved. Changed SVG snapshots reflect the resulting routes. Board 1726 still passes both its zero relaxed-DRC and zero declared-rule-DRC assertions. No solver assertion, timeout, or snapshot threshold was relaxed.

Validation:

- Local affected routing tests pass without snapshot update mode; physical trace-width and DRC-cache tests pass (247 assertions on the final pin).
- Local typecheck passes. Installed repair03 sources were verified byte-for-byte against the pinned commit; CI installs dependencies cleanly.
- Changed snapshots were visually inspected. Linux snapshots come from the actual CI output for this exact dependency pin.
- All 9 test jobs pass on `58b8dfc`: **875 passed, 0 failed**, 65 existing skips, and 63,458 assertions ([run](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/39718243088)). Build, typecheck, format, dependency checks, code checks, and Vercel checks also pass.

Fresh same-machine Blacksmith comparisons use base `f9ea920` and PR `96f7ed0`; later changes update SVG snapshots and fix final debug visualization in repair03 (`3411627` → `a756bcf`), without changing routing or DRC acceptance:

- [dataset01](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3174#issuecomment-6331720074): 85/85 solved and DRC-clean on both revisions, zero outcome regressions; P50 8.8s → 8.1s, P95 26.9s → 26.9s.
- [SRJ18](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3174#issuecomment-6331720851): 15/16 solved and DRC-clean on both revisions, zero outcome regressions; P50 108.9s → 110.5s, P95 303.2s → 305.0s. `sample015` fails on both with the identical missing-via transition (`z=3` → `z=0`) for `source_trace_117__source_net_117_mst3`. This existing failure is not introduced by the pin. Memory P50 increased 7.5% and P90 increased 8.5% in this run; these results establish outcome parity, not a universal performance improvement. Timing and memory results are from one paired run.

The upstream stack has landed on repair03 `main`. The merged commit `d003ab47f05b2fa4c0715ac235a54870ffdb732c` has the identical Git tree (`82db2704d0d64e3c69d4a4ae442a6db413a10793`) as the previously validated pin `a756bcfe5d18be3c2c7194bc590ef503340f0bc1`. This final update changes only the dependency reference in `package.json`; local JSON validation confirms no other manifest changes. The test and benchmark results above were collected on the previous pin's identical sources; the full suite was not rerun locally for this hash-only update.

title: Render orthographic outline views with hidden edges and hatched sections
description: Render outline illustrations of glTFGLB models with renderStyle: outline including hidden edges and hatched sections, while preserving existing shaded rendering defaults.
body:
Render outline illustrations of glTF/GLB models with `renderStyle: "outline"`: white opaque surfaces, black visible boundary/crease edges and view-dependent silhouettes, plus optional dashed hidden edges. Existing shaded rendering defaults are unchanged.

Adds orthographic projection with automatic camera-space fitting or an explicit vertical span. Planar sections clip in world/glTF coordinates, cap closed cut rings with diagonal hatching and preserve cavities. Open chains remain uncapped; the exported section helper reports their count. Sections currently support outline style only, and primitives are capped independently.

```ts
await renderGLTFToPNGFromURL(modelUrl, {
  renderStyle: "outline",
  showHiddenEdges: true,
  section: { axis: "x", offset: 5, keepSide: "less", hatchSpacing: 1 },
})
```

The author-facing TSX specification is in https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/951. Core registration, drawing-sheet layout and TSX-to-renderer integration remain follow-up work. These are tessellated raster illustrations, not CAD/B-rep vector output.

Validation: all 90 tests pass; TypeScript, package build and formatting pass. Six new tests cover orthographic scale/framing, hidden edges, cylinder silhouettes, cavity cap area, transformed sections, tangencies/open surfaces and identical output from GLB bytes and GLB URLs. title: Speculative explosion guide lines with optional arrows
description: Adds opt-in explosionLines for assembly diagrams, including optional arrowheads that show the direction a part moves, enhancing the visual representation of exploded views in the rendering engine.
body:
Adds opt-in `explosionLines` for assembly diagrams, including optional arrowheads that show the direction a part moves. Callers supply scene-space polylines and move the geometry themselves; guides respect scene depth without writing to the depth buffer.

Set `arrow: true` on a guide to add a solid open arrowhead at its final authored point. Arrows follow the final nonzero-length segment, remain solid on dashed shafts, and keep a consistent size of up to 10 output pixels under supersampling. Arrows default to off. Off-screen and behind-camera endpoints do not acquire arrowheads at clipping boundaries.

## Lamp example

The lamp shade, collar, and spokes lift **60 mm along +Y**, while the base, hollow blue stem, and bulb stay fixed. Two dashed guides with upward arrowheads join corresponding lower-rim points. Cosmos provides separate **Lift shade**, **Show dashed guides**, and **Show arrows** controls. The assembled and exploded snapshots use the same camera, with deterministic local geometry.

[Interactive lamp preview](https://poppygl-git-speculative-explosion-lines-tscircuit.vercel.app/?fixture=%7B%22path%22%3A%22site%2Fexamples%2Fexplosion-lamp.page.tsx%22%7D)

![Assembled lamp and shade lifting 60 mm with upward arrows](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/poppygl/cded660c40e52a2012a95a505b50e28517005b4f/tests/render/__snapshots__/explosion-lamp.snap.png)

## Rendering

Guide points contribute to automatic camera framing, and segments are clipped to the camera frustum before rasterization. The exported `ExplosionLine` type and README document coordinates, optional arrows, and dashed or solid shafts. Guide and arrow stroke widths use the `lineWidth` option from #52. Omitting guides preserves existing output.

This remains a **speculative draft awaiting API and implementation approval**, supporting the staged assembly proposals in [props#936](https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/936) and [core#4631](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4631). The PR package preview workflow allows the core draft to pin this implementation before a release.

## Validation

- `bun test`: 84 passed, including visual snapshots for the lamp and arrow directions, plus clipping, occlusion, repeated endpoints, and supersampling regressions.
- TypeScript, library build with declarations, Cosmos site build, and formatting passed.
- Updated with merged #52.

title: Add configurable hidden edges and thicker strokes
description: Adds render-wide controls for visible and hidden mesh edges, plus configurable stroke widths, allowing ordinary GLB files to display thick solid visible edges and faint dashed occluded edges without editing node metadata.
body:
Adds render-wide controls for visible and hidden mesh edges, plus configurable stroke widths. An ordinary GLB can now show thick solid visible edges and faint dashed occluded edges without editing its node metadata.

```ts
await renderGLTFToPNGFromGLB(glb, {
  showHiddenEdges: true,
  edgeWidth: 2.5,
  lineWidth: 2,
  hiddenEdgeOpacity: 0.35,
  supersampling: 2,
})
```

- `showEdges` enables visible boundary/crease edges alone. `showHiddenEdges: null` (the default) retains model flags; explicit `false` suppresses them.
- Widths use final output pixels and scale once with supersampling. Ordinary glTF LINES and finite grids use `lineWidth`; extracted mesh edges use `edgeWidth`.
- Wide strokes use antialiased screen-space coverage and frustum clipping in the existing software renderer. Per-pixel depth testing preserves occlusion; source-face depth sampling keeps visible sloping edges solid without a broad depth bias.
- Retains the legacy single-raster-pixel path. Edge overlays do not write geometry depth.
- Includes an interactive lamp example, deterministic lamp/cube visuals, and regressions for width across orientations, fractional alpha, dashes, supersampling, near/eye clipping, extreme endpoints and a close foreground occluder.

The lamp fixture is adapted from core's reference-surface lamp. Its collar, spokes and mounting details are visible through the shade in the right panel.

![Lamp with visible and hidden 2.5 px edges](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/poppygl/f49ffec8849a9af3d475be5c3a8c493c402de21b/tests/render/__snapshots__/edge-styles-lamp.snap.png)

Open `site/examples/edge-styles-lamp.page.tsx` in Cosmos for shaded/visible/hidden modes and the width slider.

This PR targets main independently of the speculative explosion guide-line PR #49. Edge extraction retains the existing boundary/30-degree crease behavior; it does not add smooth-surface silhouettes. The procedural infinite grid retains its own styling.

Validation:
- `bun test`: 77 passing, 0 failing.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`, `bun run build`, `bun run build:site`, `bun run format:check`, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Browser smoke: mode and width controls render correctly; no console errors.

title: Fix missing inner artwork in box schematic symbols
description: Restores the USB logo and socket outline inside the basics06-usb-c-connectors KiCad symbol.
body:
Restore the USB logo and socket outline inside `basics06-usb-c-connector`’s KiCad symbol.

The dependency/snapshot refresh in #723 exposed an earlier exporter regression in #491 (`720bc59`): component-level artwork handling was restricted to `is_box_with_pins === false`, removing the previous box-plus-artwork path. USB-C is a box component, so its seven paths and two circles were discarded. The exact versions from #723, tscircuit 0.0.2210 and 0.0.2984, produce identical artwork JSON (seven paths and two circles, with the same coordinates, styling, and component ownership). Passing those inputs through the historical converter revisions, with exporter dependencies held constant, gives:

| Converter revision | Input from 0.0.2210 | Input from 0.0.2984 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Before #491 (`63138ee`) | 7 artwork paths + 2 circles | 7 artwork paths + 2 circles |
| After #491 (`720bc59`) | Artwork missing | Artwork missing |
| Before #723 (`9ffdbb4`) | Artwork missing | Artwork missing |
| After #723 (`7463bb1`) | Artwork missing | Artwork missing |
| This fix (`e2e9c91`) | 7 artwork paths + 2 circles | 7 artwork paths + 2 circles |

Counts exclude the outer box, which is present in every case. The PNG had not been refreshed between the original connector support in #281 and #723, so #723 recorded the existing regression rather than introducing a new primitive format.

Reuse `buildSymbolDataFromSchematicPrimitives` to include component-owned artwork in generic box symbols. The box, artwork, and ports use the component coordinate system and the existing drawing transform handles placement. This preserves the existing pin/field handling and uses the shared shape, fill, and stroke converters without USB-specific logic.

Add direct assertions for the USB connector’s seven artwork paths, two circles, and sixteen pins, plus a nonzero-origin regression checking placement, fills, strokes, component isolation, and exclusion of field text. Both regressions fail before the fix. Refresh only the USB-C schematic PNG; the PCB snapshot is unchanged. The missing artwork occupies just 0.163% of the PNG, below the matcher’s tolerance, so the structural assertions prevent this from silently regressing.

Validation:
- Targeted regressions and native KiCad 10.0.1 rendering pass; visually inspected the restored artwork.
- The USB test also passes with current latest tscircuit 0.0.3003 in an isolated install, without changing repository dependencies.
- Typecheck, build, and formatting pass.
- [Full hosted test suite](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-kicad/actions/runs/39754927761), CI typecheck, CI formatting, and Vercel all pass.
- Local schematic suite: 78 pass / 28 fail; unchanged main: 77 pass / the same 28 failures (snapshot/environment failures). No new failures.
- Before/after comparison confirms identical box and pin definitions; only the inner artwork is added.

![USB-C artwork restored in KiCad](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-kicad/e2e9c91a2bfd0045e50789270440415109b36ecb/tests/sch/basics/__snapshots__/basics06-usb-c-connector.snap.png)

title: Fix automatic inline net labels using local KiCad labels
description: Fixes connectivity issues in KiCad by converting trace-backed text into local electrical labels, ensuring proper connections between components.
body:
Automatic inline labels currently export as plain text, so matching `SIGNAL` wire stubs remain disconnected in KiCad. This PR converts trace-backed text into local electrical labels using core's supplied attachment position, removing nearest-wire detection.

Updates `tscircuit` from `^0.0.2984` to `^0.0.2991` in this fix PR; `tscircuit-latest` stays unchanged. The repro keeps main's dependency range. Stacked on #692 and uses the merged [core](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4811) and [solver](https://github.com/tscircuit/schematic-trace-solver/pull/1339) fixes.

**Inline-label evidence**

Repro27 checks KiCad's native netlist: `R1.2` and `R2.1` change from separate nets to one `/SIGNAL` net. Both sides use the same TSX, including the section divider. The netlist proves connectivity.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: disconnected inline text](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-kicad/a97a3ffd03da9987be46d3be2a171618970ba5d6/tests/sch/repros/__snapshots__/repro27-inline-net-label-connectivity.snap.png) | ![After: electrically connected local labels](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-kicad/c3b52192d7675b2dd6e854c0fcfc6d5acf8f6845/tests/sch/repros/__snapshots__/repro27-inline-net-label-connectivity.snap.png) |

**Why `AddLibrarySymbolsStage.ts` changed**

The TB67 test exposed a separate bug: J1 reused J4's symbol because their pin numbers matched, despite different pin positions and names. This placed J1's pins on the wrong side, away from their wires. Comparing complete symbol definitions fixes that reuse. This change is independent of inline-label conversion and should be split into its own PR.

![TB67 connector J1 before and after the symbol-reuse fix](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-kicad/db8eea5fd0629f05843b19389ac75c7d0854783d/tb67-symbol-reuse-before-after.png)

Same circuit input; only `AddLibrarySymbolsStage.ts` differs. Native connection checks improve from **19/34 to 34/34**.

**Validation and limitations**

- Native KiCad connectivity checks, typecheck, and formatting pass locally.
- Older Circuit JSON with off-wire text positions needs regeneration with updated core.
- KiCad uses its normal above/left label placement, which can differ from core's chosen side.

References #549 and #552.

title: Reproduce disconnected inline net labels in KiCad

body:

title: fix: rotate polygon plated-hole copper, drills, and soldermask
description: Fixes the issue where rotating a component with polygon plated holes does not rotate its copper, drill offsets, and soldermask openings, ensuring they align correctly in the 3D viewer.
body:
Rotating a component with polygon plated holes leaves its copper, drill offsets, and soldermask openings in the original orientation. Circuit2Canvas supplies these textures to the 3D viewer, which currently needs a workaround for this missing support.

Add `center` and `rotation` to `drawPolygon`, following the existing rectangle, oval, and pill renderers' `save` / `translate` / `rotate` / `restore` pattern. Extend the existing polygon-path helper with the same center and CCW-angle options used by the rounded-rectangle and pill path helpers, so soldermask openings and margin rings rotate together.

Plated-hole copper and covered-pour openings pass rotation to these drawing primitives. Filled polygons reuse the existing polygon-path helper, and soldermask rings draw their outer and inset outlines through one loop.

Oval and pill drills use their existing rotation options; their local offsets are rotated into board coordinates. SMT pads and traces share the existing plated-hole drill calculation. Reuse the existing pill-path helper and build oval cutouts without changing the surrounding compound path's transform.

The repro's assertions stay unchanged: remove `test.failing` and update its one PNG snapshot so the 90° example has a vertical pad and slot with the correctly rotated drill offset. The 0° control stays unchanged.

Validation:

- `bun test`: 208 passing tests.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` and `bun run build`.
- `bun run format:check` passes for the full repository.
- An additional local rendering audit passed 1,120 comparisons against independently rotated canvas output, covering all four drill shapes, both layers, seven rotation inputs, four soldermask settings, and five rendering paths. The audit script is not included in the PR.

This is the second PR in a native GitHub stack, based on the repro PR.

title: repro: polygon plated holes ignore CCW rotation
description: Fixes rendering issue where polygon plated holes ignore counter-clockwise rotation, affecting both 2D and 3D views.
body:
Polygon plated holes ignore `ccw_rotation`, so a component rotated by core still renders its polygon copper and offset drill horizontally in Circuit2Canvas. This also affects the textures generated by the 3D viewer.

Add one example test and one PNG snapshot showing the same asymmetric polygon pad at 0° and 90°. The snapshot records the current bug: both pads have the same orientation. Pixel assertions expect the rotated copper, drill offset, and vertical slot; `test.failing` records that regression while keeping the repro test suite passing.

Include formatter-only corrections to the existing README example and the test workflow's final newline so the repository-wide format check passes with the currently resolved Biome version.

This is the first PR in a native GitHub stack; the next PR fixes rendering, removes `.failing`, and updates this same snapshot.

title: Reuse regional geometry and owned route metadata
description: Optimizes routing by reusing regional geometry and metadata during selective rerips, reducing unnecessary computations and improving performance.
body:
Port-point routing repeated static neighbor checks throughout each owned search, and selective rerips rebuilt intersection geometry even in untouched regions. Reuse both forms of stable state while preserving the selected paths, ordering, routing work, and invariant checks.

<!-- visual-optimization-snapshots -->
### Visual snapshots

PNG previews of the checked SVG regression snapshots, generated from the live reference and optimized test observations.

**Regional metadata reuse.** The port heatmap records 1,447 → 82 hop-ID evaluations over 50 paired steps with identical state and stats.

![Visual snapshot: Regional metadata reuse](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/tiny-hypergraph/2d5c9f01bb3dd540bdc654f801697384de64c2dc/tests/__snapshots__/owned-regional-hop-metadata-cache-visual.preview.png)

[SVG snapshot](https://github.com/tscircuit/tiny-hypergraph/blob/2d5c9f01bb3dd540bdc654f801697384de64c2dc/tests/__snapshots__/owned-regional-hop-metadata-cache-visual.snap.svg) · [Snapshot test](https://github.com/tscircuit/tiny-hypergraph/blob/2d5c9f01bb3dd540bdc654f801697384de64c2dc/tests/owned-regional-hop-metadata-cache.test.ts)

**Selective region rebuilding.** Ripping route 0 changes only region 0: rebuild one segment instead of five while retaining the same committed copper.

![Visual snapshot: Selective region rebuilding](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/tiny-hypergraph/2d5c9f01bb3dd540bdc654f801697384de64c2dc/tests/__snapshots__/selective-rerip-unchanged-region-cache-visual.preview.png)

[SVG snapshot](https://github.com/tscircuit/tiny-hypergraph/blob/2d5c9f01bb3dd540bdc654f801697384de64c2dc/tests/__snapshots__/selective-rerip-unchanged-region-cache-visual.snap.svg) · [Snapshot test](https://github.com/tscircuit/tiny-hypergraph/blob/2d5c9f01bb3dd540bdc654f801697384de64c2dc/tests/selective-rerip-unchanged-region-cache.test.ts)

The SVGs are regression-tested; the PNGs above are rendered from those exact checked-in SVGs for inline display.
<!-- /visual-optimization-snapshots -->

- Reuse intersection caches when a selective rerip removes no segment from a region. Refresh their scores with the current geometry and cost parameters; continue validating every committed port owner.
- Lazily cache successful section, incidence, hop-ID, assignment, and reservation checks inside the existing opt-in `OWNED_REGIONAL_HOP_FRONTIER` contract. Live closure, best costs, congestion, penalties, and scoring still run for each candidate. Lazy preparation preserves early-goal and exception order.
- Invalidate retained metadata when the heap, closure epoch, route, net, goal, best-cost generation, or neighbor-array identity changes. The existing ownership contract requires fixed ordinary metadata within an epoch; the default and opt-out search paths are unchanged.

The neighbor metadata idea is adapted from [#208](https://github.com/tscircuit/tiny-hypergraph/pull/208). This patch isolates cache reuse; it excludes that PR's owner-floor, dominance-pruning, and tie-order changes.

Validation with snapshot regression coverage (production unchanged from benchmarked `bee74730028acc3fe72a1132bef3ef89df0238d7`):

- All 152 tests pass with 2,889 assertions; TypeScript and changed-file formatting checks pass.
- Differential tests compare working state, subsequent output and iterations, native closure, queue replacement, best-cost resets, route/net/goal boundaries, neighbor replacement, no-op and selective rerips, shared endpoints, recommits, and loud ownership errors. Existing malformed-incidence, early-goal, and scoring-error cases preserve the exact exception order and messages.
- A work-count replay of the actual current autorouter's SRJ18 sample 6 retains the exact port-output SHA-256 `b6d233e9f40324bacc9393ce4038ec8ec155cc91433b083d49a392546681e860`, every non-timing solve-graph metric, all 2,000,000 inner iterations, and all 5,683,414 frontier expansions.
- In that replay, hop-key evaluations fall from 355,788,254 to 28,854,609 (91.89% fewer), port-reservation checks from 351,821,820 to 28,855,122 (91.80% fewer), and region-reservation checks from 338,725,099 to 15,758,401 (95.35% fewer). The 330,211,264 best-cost checks and 79,581,560 scoring calls remain identical. This omits 972,867,041 repeated static helper calls.

SRJ18 regional port pathing takes 5.97% less time overall and 13.43% less on sample 6 in the combined consumer benchmark. The combined consumer patch is benchmarked in [tscircuit-autorouter #3160](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3160): 107 scenarios on paired Blacksmith ARM runners, unchanged effort/search limits, all 106 completed route SVGs byte-identical, and no new completion or DRC failures. The five completed selected SRJ28 cases take 19.26% less total time (3.15% including the unchanged timeout); the heaviest completed case is 39.16% faster and reproduces a 37.01–44.80% speedup in a four-pass order control. Dataset01 is 2.92% faster in one paired run, while SRJ18 total time is effectively flat. These end-to-end figures measure the combined solver changes; they are not isolated attribution to this PR. Peak RSS is mixed and variable, including a 19.24% increase for sample 37 in the primary run that does not consistently reproduce in the order control. No uniform RSS reduction is claimed. Full per-case results, quality checks, memory quantiles, limitations and workflow links are in the consumer PR.

Snapshot regression coverage now records both optimizations with the original behavior as the live oracle:

- [Owned-metadata snapshot](https://github.com/tscircuit/tiny-hypergraph/blob/3399475ae8c84d988bbf918311c433b8cfcf78f9/tests/__snapshots__/owned-regional-hop-metadata-cache.test.ts.snap): 1,447 → 82 hop-ID evaluations in the uninterrupted case, plus explicit queue-clear, best-cost-reset and neighbor-replacement cases. Every compared routing step still has equal state and stats.
- [Selective-rerip snapshot](https://github.com/tscircuit/tiny-hypergraph/blob/3399475ae8c84d988bbf918311c433b8cfcf78f9/tests/__snapshots__/selective-rerip-unchanged-region-cache.test.ts.snap): ripping route 0 rebuilds one segment instead of five, identifies reused geometry regions, and retains the same committed routes. The test also checks subsequent routing, scalar cost refreshes and ownership errors.

These follow-up commits change only tests and checked-in deterministic snapshots. Production code and dependency pins are unchanged from the benchmarked revisions. The snapshots record operation counts rather than elapsed time. All four dependency solver suites (500 passing tests), all five repository type checks, and the autorouter goal regression pass locally.


Visual follow-up validation: all 500 dependency solver tests pass locally with four existing skips; all five repository type checks and the autorouter visual regression pass. Solver production code and runtime dependency pins are unchanged. The existing local formatter is pinned to Biome 2.5.15 for reproducible CI checks.


Formatting reproducibility: the floating Biome range began resolving 2.6.2, which introduced Markdown/YAML formatting failures in unchanged files. Pinning the locally validated 2.5.15 retains all format checks and keeps this PR focused on the solver and visual tests.

title: Add JLCPCB physical stackups through 8 layers
description: Expands the physical FR-4 stackup catalog from one construction to 83: five 2-layer, 28 4-layer, 25 6-layer, and 25 8-layer constructions, enhancing the stackup definitions and supporting additional layer counts and thicknesses.
body:
Expands the physical FR-4 stackup catalog from one construction to 83: five 2-layer, 28 4-layer, 25 6-layer, and 25 8-layer constructions. Shared copper, prepreg, and core builders keep the definitions readable and avoid repeating full layer objects. All named constructions are exported through the existing entry point.

`getJlcStackup` now supports the added layer counts and thicknesses, prefers ordinary JLC templates where available, and preserves the existing JLC04161H-3313 result for 4-layer 1.6 mm boards. Multilayer entries use 1 oz outer / 0.5 oz inner copper; retained 2-layer entries use the source's 1 oz construction. Ambiguous 2-layer copper variants and incorrectly reused 2.5/3.2 mm cores are excluded.

Data was independently checked against the [official JLCPCB calculator template API](https://jlcpcb.com/api/jlcTools/impedance/selectPageImpedanceDefaultTemplate) and [stackup reference](https://jlcpcb.com/impedance). The 1.8 mm and 3.2 mm 8-layer nominal thicknesses follow the named constructions and displayed finished thicknesses, correcting conflicting API filter metadata. Individual physical layer dimensions remain as published, including multi-sheet dielectrics and the asymmetric 3.2 mm construction.

Validation: `bun test` (5 passing tests, one per file), `bun run typecheck`, and `bun run format:check`. An independent comparison matched all 83 exported physical layer sequences and numeric values to official API records. Coverage includes legacy lookup identity, supported and unsupported constructions, unique exports, copper order, and representative source values.

- Sample006 and metadata/identity tests pass. USB still completes all six phases, publishes no new pad overlaps, and retains 0.1 mm terminal-via clearance. No snapshot or assertion tolerance was relaxed for this follow-up.

Consumer validation and exact dependency pin: https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3174. Final fixture results and benchmark evidence are recorded there.

Stacked on #173, targeting `techmannih/repro-sample006-pad-overlap`, and retaining the physical-width, rotated-pad and through-via changes merged in #177. This diff changes the repro's `test.failing` to a normal passing test. Merge this into the repro branch, then merge the repro into main.

description: GlobalDrcForceImproveSolver introduces two different-net SMT-pad overlaps when given the captured Pipeline9 sample006 input immediately after trace-width assignment. The input has no physical pad overlap; the output crosses pcb_smtpad_6 and pcb_smtpad_11 by approximately 0.0450793 mm. This reproduction runs repair03 alone with the original stage options, canonicalized routes, locked terminals, and connectivity map. The checked-in fixture records its source, capture boundary, and hashes. It does not install or run the complete autorouter. Only the final no-overlap assertion uses test.failing; setup, input-clearance, solver-success, and route-count checks run in beforeAll, where failures fail CI normally. An unexpected pass will fail the regression until the fix restores a normal test. The physical-overlap check offsets the engines 0.005 mm epsilon and filters negative copper gaps. A separate test verifies detection at -0.002 mm and -0.000001 mm and accepts touchingseparated copper. The complete capacity-autorouter 0.0.990 pipeline repairs these contacts in a later stage. This PR isolates the intermediate solver regression rather than claiming that the final pipeline output remains shorted. Validation: GitHub CI at ca648e9  full test suite (Bun 1.3.1, Ubuntu), typecheck, and formatcheck all pass. Repro and physical-threshold tests  2 pass. The repro is an expected failure only at the final no-overlap assertion (0 input overlaps, 2 output overlaps). Verified on CIs Bun 1.3.1 that a thrown beforeAll setup error exits with failure even when the test uses test.failing. bun run typecheck  passes, including the USB fixture project. bun run formatcheck and git diff --check  pass. Stacked fix: 174, targeting this reproduction branch. The fix restores this regression to a normal passing test and includes the verified USB routing snapshot update. Both branches can run CI successfully independently; the stack can be merged by merging the fix into this branch, then this PR into main.
body:
`GlobalDrcForceImproveSolver` introduces two different-net SMT-pad overlaps when given the captured Pipeline9 `sample006` input immediately after trace-width assignment. The input has no physical pad overlap; the output crosses `pcb_smtpad_6` and `pcb_smtpad_11` by approximately 0.0450793 mm.

This reproduction runs repair03 alone with the original stage options, canonicalized routes, locked terminals, and connectivity map. The checked-in fixture records its source, capture boundary, and hashes. It does not install or run the complete autorouter. Only the final no-overlap assertion uses `test.failing`; setup, input-clearance, solver-success, and route-count checks run in `beforeAll`, where failures fail CI normally. An unexpected pass will fail the regression until the fix restores a normal `test`.

The physical-overlap check offsets the engine's 0.005 mm epsilon and filters negative copper gaps. A separate test verifies detection at -0.002 mm and -0.000001 mm and accepts touching/separated copper.

The complete capacity-autorouter 0.0.990 pipeline repairs these contacts in a later stage. This PR isolates the intermediate solver regression rather than claiming that the final pipeline output remains shorted.

Validation:
- GitHub CI at `ca648e9` — full test suite (Bun 1.3.1, Ubuntu), typecheck, and formatcheck all pass.
- Repro and physical-threshold tests — 2 pass. The repro is an expected failure only at the final no-overlap assertion (0 input overlaps, 2 output overlaps).
- Verified on CI's Bun 1.3.1 that a thrown `beforeAll` setup error exits with failure even when the test uses `test.failing`.
- `bun run typecheck` — passes, including the USB fixture project.
- `bun run formatcheck` and `git diff --check` — pass.

Stacked fix: #174, targeting this reproduction branch. The fix restores this regression to a normal passing `test` and includes the verified USB routing snapshot update. Both branches can run CI successfully independently; the stack can be merged by merging the fix into this branch, then this PR into `main`.

title: Preserve physical clearances, rotated pads, and via drill spans
description: Updates autorouter to restore physical-clearance and via-layer behavior, ensuring correct handling of rotated pads and via spans, while maintaining regression guards for previous functionality.
body:
Updating autorouter from its production repair03 pin to main drops physical-clearance and via-layer behavior. This restores those guarantees on top of main so https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3165 can keep its original regression guards.

- Use each trace's actual radius and each via's actual diameter for pad repulsion, including the spatial search radius.
- Preserve rotated rectangular pad geometry in indexed DRC and circuit-json conversion. This restores zero remaining DRC errors for autorouter's SRJ18 sample010 case.
- Restore `allowBlindAndBuriedVias`: vias drill through the board by default; partial spans require opt-in. Apply the same span to DRC, exports, and repair geometry, and verify cache invalidation when the option changes.
- Add width, spatial-bucket boundary, rotated-pad, and via-span regression coverage while retaining explicit-layer and reversed-span cases.
- Use flat named parameter objects for the changed via helpers, their callers, and the test reference helper. Preserve the `ccwRotationDegrees` name throughout pad conversion.
- Format the four Markdown files flagged by the repository check; document content is unchanged.

Validation at `19fc80a`: [Linux tests](https://github.com/tscircuit/high-density-repair03/actions/runs/39661228720), [both typecheck projects](https://github.com/tscircuit/high-density-repair03/actions/runs/39661228820), and [the full format check](https://github.com/tscircuit/high-density-repair03/actions/runs/39661228930) all pass. All 12 focused width/via/rotation/cache tests pass locally. Autorouter's physical-clearance, minimum-width stability, cache, and sample010 zero-DRC/snapshot tests also pass with the reviewed source, as do its typecheck and build.

Local Apple Silicon reproduces an existing contact-tie floating-point equality failure on unchanged main; the complete Linux repair suite passes.

title: Preserve via-in-pad policy in regenerated TI samples
description: Preserves imported board via-in-pad permissions in the published TI routing samples, ensuring routers receive the source policy by updating the samples to include the allowViaInPad field and validating it against the Circuit JSON boards policy.
body:
**Motivation:** Preserve imported board via-in-pad permissions in the published TI routing samples so routers receive the source policy.

**Actual:** Samples 021–026 were generated with core `0.0.2165` and omit `allowViaInPad`, including four boards whose Circuit JSON explicitly permits vias in pads. The public declaration and validator also omit this policy.

**Expected / fix:** Pin released core `0.0.2188`, update its required props peer to `0.0.705`, and regenerate samples 021–026 from the SHA-256-verified Altium sources. Samples 021, 022, 024, and 025 now emit `true`; samples 023 and 026 emit `false` for an unspecified source policy. Add `allowViaInPad?: boolean` to the public declaration and generator template, and require each TI sample's policy to equal `pcb_board.is_via_in_pad_allowed ?? false` in the existing validator. The type remains optional for the older KiCad samples.

**Validation:**

- `bun install --frozen-lockfile`
- `bun run generate:ti --source-root ../regen-ti-sources`
- `bun run test`: all 26 samples and 858 through-hole obstacles pass.
- All 18 negative checks reject missing, inverted, or string-valued policies across the six TI samples.
- TypeScript consumer checks and the actual declaration generator round trip pass.
- `bun run build`

Regeneration adds only the policy field to each SRJ; the Circuit JSON and comparison SVGs are byte-identical.

**Related:** Uses the released fix from [tscircuit/core#4689](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4689).

title: Index fixed obstacle geometry for exact B01 collision checks
description: Adds spatial indexing for fixed obstacle geometry to optimize exact collision checks in B01 routing.
body:
B01 exact collision checks scanned every fixed trace, via, and rectangular obstacle for each candidate move. Build static spatial indexes during setup and query only geometry whose bounds can touch the move. The existing exact collision predicates, layer/root exclusions, endpoint handling, search order, and routing budgets remain unchanged.

<!-- visual-optimization-snapshots -->
### Visual snapshots

PNG previews of the checked SVG regression snapshots, generated from the live reference and optimized test observations.

**Obstacle candidates around the same routed copper.** One real trace query returns 185 → 3 candidates; the completed fixture returns 229,683 → 2,187 candidates across all obstacle types. The routed copper is identical.

![Visual snapshot: Obstacle candidates around the same routed copper](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/high-density-b01/8dd0815b18f766603e1688196a6d92ec5f16f96c/tests/b01/__snapshots__/obstacle-spatial-index-routing-visual.preview.png)

[SVG snapshot](https://github.com/tscircuit/high-density-b01/blob/8dd0815b18f766603e1688196a6d92ec5f16f96c/tests/b01/__snapshots__/obstacle-spatial-index-routing-visual.snap.svg) · [Snapshot test](https://github.com/tscircuit/high-density-b01/blob/8dd0815b18f766603e1688196a6d92ec5f16f96c/tests/b01/obstacle-spatial-index-routing.test.ts)

The SVGs are regression-tested; the PNGs above are rendered from those exact checked-in SVGs for inline display.
<!-- /visual-optimization-snapshots -->

Validation: the full suite on this exact final revision passes (70 tests, 2 existing skips, 68,270 assertions), along with TypeScript checks. Differential tests compare every grid move for mixed/rotated obstacles and compare complete routing steps, queue state, outputs, iterations, rip events and penalties on 12 real obstacle fixtures. Those fixtures examine less than half as many exact geometry candidates.

This branch is based on the consumer's exact e651cab pin so the consumer can test the isolated change.

The combined consumer patch is benchmarked in [tscircuit-autorouter #3160](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3160): 107 scenarios on paired Blacksmith ARM runners, unchanged effort/search limits, all 106 completed route SVGs byte-identical, and no new completion or DRC failures. The five completed selected SRJ28 cases take 19.26% less total time (3.15% including the unchanged timeout); the heaviest completed case is 39.16% faster and reproduces a 37.01–44.80% speedup in a four-pass order control. Dataset01 is 2.92% faster in one paired run, while SRJ18 total time is effectively flat. These end-to-end figures measure the combined solver changes; they are not isolated attribution to this PR. Peak RSS is mixed and variable, including a 19.24% increase for sample 37 in the primary run that does not consistently reproduce in the order control. No uniform RSS reduction is claimed. Full per-case results, quality checks, memory quantiles, limitations and workflow links are in the consumer PR.

[Obstacle-candidate snapshot](https://github.com/tscircuit/high-density-b01/blob/ce509fe8ec4287721992347708b8c576bd77ea5f/tests/b01/__snapshots__/obstacle-spatial-index-routing.test.ts.snap) records both live full-scan and indexed candidate counts for each of 12 real routing fixtures. For example, the first fixture returns 229,683 candidates before indexing versus 2,187 afterwards, with the same 2,145 queries, solved routes, iterations and rip count. These count candidates offered to the unchanged geometry loops before their filters and early exits, not exact predicate executions. The test compares routing steps, absolute iteration counts and full output against the original full-scan behavior in every run. The snapshot records zero iteration difference from that live oracle across all 12 fixtures, avoiding an unrelated platform-specific absolute-iteration golden.

These follow-up commits change only tests and checked-in deterministic snapshots. Production code and dependency pins are unchanged from the benchmarked revisions. The snapshots record operation counts rather than elapsed time. All four dependency solver suites (500 passing tests), all five repository type checks, and the autorouter goal regression pass locally.


Visual follow-up validation: all 500 dependency solver tests pass locally with four existing skips; all five repository type checks and the autorouter visual regression pass. Solver production code and runtime dependency pins are unchanged. The existing local formatter is pinned to Biome 2.5.15 for reproducible CI checks.


Formatting reproducibility: the floating Biome range began resolving 2.6.2, which introduced Markdown/YAML formatting failures in unchanged files. Pinning the locally validated 2.5.15 retains all format checks and keeps this PR focused on the solver and visual tests.

title: Reduce eleven-sample routing time by 30.6% with identical outputs
description: The eleven-placement benchmark spends substantial time rescanning unchanged copper, comparing distant curve chords, and rebuilding sparse compaction constraints. Add spatial broad phases, request-local conflictgeometry reuse, early dominance pruning, in-place Pareto label compaction, and sparse constraint cleanup. An explicit existing return type also fixes portable declaration generation.
body:
The eleven-placement benchmark spends substantial time rescanning unchanged copper, comparing distant curve chords, and rebuilding sparse compaction constraints. Add spatial broad phases, request-local conflict/geometry reuse, early dominance pruning, in-place Pareto label compaction, and sparse constraint cleanup. An explicit existing return type also fixes portable declaration generation.

Measured with the unchanged benchmark harness and fixtures:

| Measurement | Base | PR | Time reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| All 11: solver time | 2,371.601s | 1,646.858s | **30.56%** |
| All 11: worker time including fixture loading and validation | 2,431.766s | 1,704.913s | **29.89%** |
| `control-inner1` | 1,081.560s | 487.520s | **54.92%** |
| `outer-layers` | 581.543s | 535.792s | **7.87%** |

All **11 complete ordered output JSONs and iteration counts are identical** to the base. Every case routes **47/47 signals**, preserves all **161 fixed power dogbones**, and passes connectivity, combined copper DRC, full-copper bus/pair length matching and coupling. Search budgets and physical tolerances are unchanged.

[Full per-sample runtime and per-bus copper-length-skew report](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/blob/938a96720de827040d88629c522a99541bcad3fa/docs/benchmark-performance/README.md), [input/output hashes](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/blob/938a96720de827040d88629c522a99541bcad3fa/docs/benchmark-performance/comparison.json), and [eleven completed, visually inspected routed snapshots](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/blob/938a96720de827040d88629c522a99541bcad3fa/docs/benchmark-performance/README.md#routed-snapshots) are committed with the raw baseline and PR reports.

Validation: `./benchmark.sh` completed all eleven cases on both revisions; GitHub Actions passed **496 tests**, formatting and typechecking; `bun run test:package` passed isolated Node, browser and TypeScript consumers. Added randomized first-conflict ordering coverage and long sampled-path self-clearance regressions.

Timing methodology: one full run per revision on the same macOS arm64 host, Bun 1.3.2 and the same dependencies. Each revision runs cases serially in fresh processes; the two revisions overlapped. This is a single-run comparison and timings can vary with host load. Base: `81256f9`; detailed reproduction commands are in the report.

CI validation: the [fresh Blacksmith base/head comparison](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/actions/runs/39717903716) **passed**, pinned to base `13a1c5d` and head `938a967` (Bun 1.4.0, 3,600-second per-solver/sample budget). All eleven route jobs and the `AM3352 benchmark (11/11)` acceptance check are green; the aggregate log confirms **Fresh head acceptance: 11/11**, including connectivity, DRC, matching, coupling and fixed-copper preservation. Raw paired reports and `am3352-comparison` are retained as CI artifacts. The 30.56% timing figure above remains the separately documented local comparison against `81256f9`; it is not a claim about the CI timing comparison.

title: Reject jointly incompatible escape sites before native carrier search
description: This PR implements early rejection of incompatible native escape domains in the AM3352 hard-length surface routing, preventing unnecessary carrier negotiation on incompatible pair seeds.
body:
Native hard-length surface routing can spend its carrier-search budget on individually reachable escape sites that have no compatible joint assignment. In the AM3352 case, DDR_D13/D11/D9/DQM1 each have choices, but all 1,344 combinations conflict. This reuses bounded arc-consistency pruning on escape copper and full-stack drill compatibility before carrier negotiation. Proven-incompatible pair seeds return immediately; unsupported choices are removed. Exhausting the support-check budget keeps unproven choices and continues routing. The check is enabled for the hard-length native surface policy; the established unbounded legacy search remains intact. Manufacturing limits, supplied copper and final acceptance are unchanged. The regression fixture is derived entirely from the existing public full-DDR input, with geometry-derived native length limits and runtime-generated pair/CK repair geometry. No captured intermediate route dump or manual copper is added. Validation: two new integration tests pass (14 assertions); typecheck and diff checks pass. The negative control remains searching under the previous policy while the updated bounded policy rejects before 5,000 yields; a feasible four-signal control with generated DQS0 released still produces a candidate and preserves the other pairs/input. ## Benchmark effect **Complete: fresh Blacksmith base 11/11 and head 11/11; all checks green on the final production revision.** Same Linux x64 4-CPU / 16-GiB workspace, Bun 1.4.0, sequential base/head, JSC RAM setting 2 GiB and heap growth 1.05. Each policy receives the same cloned native state, options and 250,000-yield cap. Shared fixture generation took 33.126 s and is excluded. | Targeted case | Base | Head | | --- | --- | --- | | Four-signal incompatible seed | Rejected in 172.002 s / 247,179 yields | Rejected in 1.965 s / 402 yields | | Full forty ordinary signals | Still searching at 255.997 s / 250,000-yield cap | Rejected in 34.808 s / 48,178 yields | Inputs remained unchanged for every run. This is a single paired measurement of earlier dead-end detection, not a completed-board routing speedup. The full-forty base did not finish, so its final rejection time is unknown. All 503 tests pass in CI (0 failures, 172 files); typecheck, formatcheck and both package checks pass. - Base: `13a1c5d378028be3152fa8804510a2b884f53b6d`. - Head: `b6e5ac361636a652f851723f3d9d9b7da42e763b`. - The normal PR workflow measures all eleven canonical placements freshly on Blacksmith, paired sequential base/head per runner with equal one-hour budgets, and fails unless all eleven head samples independently pass. - `bun scripts/benchmark-am3352-collective-escapes.ts output.json` measures time to reject the four-signal and full-forty-signal incompatible seed under equal 250,000-yield budgets, excluding shared runtime fixture generation. This measures earlier failure detection, not time to finish a board. [Reproduction, method and all eleven inspected reference snapshots](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/blob/b6e5ac361636a652f851723f3d9d9b7da42e763b/docs/collective-escape-pruning/README.md). Remaining scope: this skips impossible pair seeds early. It does not regenerate DQS0 around a multi-signal conflict group, deduplicate equivalent repairs across seeds, or claim a completed native AM3352 board. Those remain follow-up solver work. ## Fresh canonical benchmark analysis Run: https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/actions/runs/39724746187 All eleven samples freshly solved on both revisions: 47/47 connections per sample, combined DRC valid, whole-copper bus and pair matching/coupling valid, and fixed FanoutSolver copper/input preserved. Every paired fixture hash, solver iteration count and complete validation object is identical. No lost completions, failures, timeouts, or missing reports. The canonical inputs use the established unbounded search; this guard targets the separate hard-length native case. Aggregate solver time was 2,276.534 s base versus 2,238.672 s head (-1.7%); P50 49.690 → 48.257 s and P95 773.114 → 764.298 s. Three individual samples were slower: control-inner1 853.066 → 870.621 s (+2.1%), right 17.441 → 17.759 s (+1.8%), and above 25.834 → 26.593 s (+2.9%). These single-run timing differences do not establish a canonical solver speedup; the search counts and validation results are unchanged. The targeted rejection results above establish the intended effect. Reproduction uses the pinned base harness on Blacksmith `blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404`, Bun 1.4.0, JSC RAM setting 2 GiB / growth 1.05. Install both revisions before timing; for each declared sample run the following, alternating sequential base/head order on the same runner, with the same 3,600-second budgets: ```sh bun base/scripts/pr-benchmark/run-pair.ts \ --sample "$SAMPLE" --timeout-seconds 3600 \ --main base/lib/index.ts --pr head/lib/index.ts \ --main-sha 13a1c5d378028be3152fa8804510a2b884f53b6d \ --pr-sha b6e5ac361636a652f851723f3d9d9b7da42e763b \ --controller-sha 13a1c5d378028be3152fa8804510a2b884f53b6d \ --output "results/$SAMPLE.json" ``` The workflow artifacts retain raw per-case reports/logs for 30 days. The generated comparison below is copied into this PR for lasting provenance.

title: Reproduce native AM3352 ordinary escape failures after pair planning
description: Reproduces failures in the native AM3352 surface search related to ordinary escape domains, adding tests for specific scenarios without altering existing routing behavior.
body:
The native AM3352 surface search can now select all three differential pairs, but the next stage rejects ordinary escape domains. This adds two deterministic reproductions: DDR_D13 has a legal expanded-site candidate that the current surface policy misses; DDR_CSn0 remains blocked until the generated CK corridor is removed, while removing either strobe pair does not help.

The loader derives everything from existing public repository fixtures and generates pair copper at runtime. No additional captured board data, intermediate route snapshots, or production routing changes are included. The tests record current behavior and diagnostic controls, not a completed or length-matched board.

Validation: 2 tests / 19 assertions pass; verifies input immutability, byte maximum length and 0.30 mm drill / 0.50 mm land vias. CI is green.

## Benchmark effect

Base `81256f907408004329344fd4731bfe29f8d47534`; head `f965d0041703021d851728b29fc0f6c71be8d805`. This PR changes no production solver code, existing benchmark inputs, acceptance checks or benchmark entry points; expected routing results and search behavior are unchanged. It adds a separate runtime-generated diagnostic fixture loader and two tests, increasing test work, not benchmark solver work. This is a source-scope assessment, not a measured full-suite runtime comparison; no speedup is claimed.

The behavior-changing stacked fix is #71; its benchmark analysis separately records the targeted gains, initial full-suite caps and the outstanding final-revision fresh base/head comparison. Reproduction controls do not count as solved or length-matched benchmark boards.

title: fix: avoid starvation in native shared-pair planning
description: Native AM3352 shared-surface routing could spend minutes searching individual differential pairs without offering a compatible joint corridor. Independent candidates could all conflict, while alternate allowed layers were deferred behind every preferred-layer variant. Try the direct corridor first, consider allowed layers in the same joint search, and make bounded repair attempts routing a pair around compatible neighboring choices. Restrict the new policy to fresh-surface planning; retain the established inner-layer policy and guard its complete legacy route in CI. Existing child budgets, length ceilings, inputfixed-copper preservation and final pipeline acceptance checks remain in force. The captured 46-signal  1,144-obstacle regression offers no plan on the baseline within 20,000 yields, and a six-conductor seed after 12,286 yields with this fix. Added bun run benchmark:shared-pairs, exact capture provenance, and a CI regression checking shared-section spacing, pair skew, allowed layers, length ceilings and inter-pair clearance. Validation: 494 tests pass, including complete inner-left routing; typecheck, format and package-consumer validation pass. All 1111 legacy placements have successful 4747 routes independently revalidated for DRC, total-copper matching, pair coupling and all 161 fixed power dogbones. Regenerated PNGs and trace arrays exactly match the prior proof; every image was visually inspected. Full proof, runtimes, revision provenance and completed snapshots(https:github.comtscircuitbus-lanes-solverblobfixam3352-shared-pair-searchdocsnative-shared-pair-planningREADME.md). Pins the validated formatter version to prevent CI dependency drift from introducing unrelated MarkdownYAML formatting failures. The new native regression certifies a planning seed, not a fully routed real SBC, final exterior coupling or full-bus length matching. Those remain mandatory downstream checks. Related independent core constraint-conversion fix: https:github.comtscircuitcorepull4833.
body:
Native AM3352 shared-surface routing could spend minutes searching individual differential pairs without offering a compatible joint corridor. Independent candidates could all conflict, while alternate allowed layers were deferred behind every preferred-layer variant.

Try the direct corridor first, consider allowed layers in the same joint search, and make bounded repair attempts routing a pair around compatible neighboring choices. Restrict the new policy to fresh-surface planning; retain the established inner-layer policy and guard its complete legacy route in CI. Existing child budgets, length ceilings, input/fixed-copper preservation and final pipeline acceptance checks remain in force.

The captured 46-signal / 1,144-obstacle regression offers no plan on the baseline within 20,000 yields, and a six-conductor seed after 12,286 yields with this fix. Added `bun run benchmark:shared-pairs`, exact capture provenance, and a CI regression checking shared-section spacing, pair skew, allowed layers, length ceilings and inter-pair clearance.

Validation: **494 tests pass**, including complete inner-left routing; typecheck, format and package-consumer validation pass. All **11/11 legacy placements** have successful 47/47 routes independently revalidated for DRC, total-copper matching, pair coupling and all 161 fixed power dogbones. Regenerated PNGs and trace arrays exactly match the prior proof; every image was visually inspected. [Full proof, runtimes, revision provenance and completed snapshots](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/blob/fix/am3352-shared-pair-search/docs/native-shared-pair-planning/README.md).

Pins the validated formatter version to prevent CI dependency drift from introducing unrelated Markdown/YAML formatting failures.

The new native regression certifies a planning seed, not a fully routed real SBC, final exterior coupling or full-bus length matching. Those remain mandatory downstream checks. Related independent core constraint-conversion fix: https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4833.

title: Archive stall testing process, recordings and homing outcomes
description: Preserves the NEMA17 stall experiment in stall-testing for auditing purposes, including original training trials and validation recordings, while documenting fixture procedures and outcomes.
body:
Preserve the NEMA17 stall experiment in `stall-testing/` so its fixture procedure, labels, source recordings and mounted-gantry results can be audited from the repository.

Includes the original 24 accepted training trials and two fresh validation recordings in compressed archives, a trial index and checksums, validation/update reports, screenshots, and an offline verifier. Documents the discarded fixture batch and clearly records that mounted XY homing remains unverified, with no saved bounds. Links the archive from existing documentation and keeps it out of dashboard deployment uploads.

Validation: `python3 stall-testing/verify.py` passes all 12 file hashes and 26 continuous 4,096-bin traces. Re-exporting the stored calibration using archived recordings reproduces `stall_model.h` byte-for-byte (NumPy 2.5.4). `git diff --check` passes. No hardware was operated and the full training search was not rerun for this archival update.

title: Add verbose diagnostics to macOS release signing
description: Add verbose diagnostics to the macOS release signing process, capturing detailed logs and artifacts for better troubleshooting of notarization failures.
body:

This uses the current release flow, including the 30-minute wait and single verification attempt, so it can be tested before #26.

title: Assess received-DQS timing and make pipeline installs portable
description: DQ eyes currently fold only on the transmitted stimulus clock and cannot assess receiver timing. Add opt-in modeling.ddrAssessments to align complete DQ windows to received differential-DQS crossings, interpolate AC setupDC hold, and report explicit voltagetiming limits and per-edge margins in HTML and CSV. Quiet, ambiguous or incomplete strobe observations remain unevaluated. Successful checks without characterization remain illustrative; finite simulation never claims DDR compliance. Existing probeseyes and stimulus-clock folds remain supported. An independent raw-waveform audit checks crossings, capture times, AC acquisition, continuous DC validity and folded interpolation. Pin the immutable prepared archive from ibis-to-spice 1. Remove the sibling-mutating postinstall builder, declaration rewriting and its esbuild dependency. The converter needs no install-time build approval. Keep a stable executable entry for Bun Git installs. Default native tools to a shared cache outside project paths so spaces in the checkout do not break wxWidgets. Browser inspection exposed an offline report bug: source-mode Function.toString() included a transpiler closure helper without its definition, disabling controls. Emit standalone browser JavaScript from the packaged typed source and add a regression check. Waveform and eye interaction were verified in Chrome. Canonicalize the TSX config path for macOS path aliases and keep temporary test projects outside the hashed source tree. Validation: an archive of exact public HEAD cd1e7db4384bdd599c29002a49aa91680659d449 passes both TypeScript checks and all 150 tests in parallel. Packaging commit 644d55f01d83379c0cac26bb3e63daf28447b770 additionally passed fresh-cache and warm frozen Bun 1.3.14 installs, fresh-store and warm frozen pnpm 11.25.0 installs, build, rootTSX APIs, both CLIs, converter parserloaderconversion and byte-identical artifactslocks. Pipeline consumers pass strict NodeNext with skipLibCheck enabled; converter declarations separately pass with it disabled. The board project with the final public pin passes its four tests, typecheck and all five builds. The separate native routed-copper FastHenry repair remains outside this PR. These changes do not establish complete full-board extraction convergence or hardware DDR compliance.
body:
DQ eyes currently fold only on the transmitted stimulus clock and cannot assess receiver timing. Add opt-in `modeling.ddrAssessments` to align complete DQ windows to received differential-DQS crossings, interpolate AC setup/DC hold, and report explicit voltage/timing limits and per-edge margins in HTML and CSV.

Quiet, ambiguous or incomplete strobe observations remain unevaluated. Successful checks without characterization remain illustrative; finite simulation never claims DDR compliance. Existing probes/eyes and stimulus-clock folds remain supported. An independent raw-waveform audit checks crossings, capture times, AC acquisition, continuous DC validity and folded interpolation.

Pin the immutable prepared archive from [ibis-to-spice #1](https://github.com/tscircuit/ibis-to-spice/pull/1). Remove the sibling-mutating postinstall builder, declaration rewriting and its esbuild dependency. The converter needs no install-time build approval. Keep a stable executable entry for Bun Git installs. Default native tools to a shared cache outside project paths so spaces in the checkout do not break wxWidgets.

Browser inspection exposed an offline report bug: source-mode Function.toString() included a transpiler closure helper without its definition, disabling controls. Emit standalone browser JavaScript from the packaged typed source and add a regression check. Waveform and eye interaction were verified in Chrome. Canonicalize the TSX config path for macOS path aliases and keep temporary test projects outside the hashed source tree.

Validation: an archive of exact public HEAD `cd1e7db4384bdd599c29002a49aa91680659d449` passes both TypeScript checks and all 150 tests in parallel. Packaging commit `644d55f01d83379c0cac26bb3e63daf28447b770` additionally passed fresh-cache and warm frozen Bun 1.3.14 installs, fresh-store and warm frozen pnpm 11.25.0 installs, build, root/TSX APIs, both CLIs, converter parser/loader/conversion and byte-identical artifacts/locks. Pipeline consumers pass strict NodeNext with skipLibCheck enabled; converter declarations separately pass with it disabled. The board project with the final public pin passes its four tests, typecheck and all five builds.

The separate native routed-copper FastHenry repair remains outside this PR. These changes do not establish complete full-board extraction convergence or hardware DDR compliance.

Exports SVG pages with embedded raster view renders. Preserves physical scale, clips viewports, maps CAD +Z-up coordinates to glTF +Y-up, and validates page references, dimensions, duplicate title blocks and raster allocation before resolving geometry. Raw PCB-to-model conversion and core TSX emission remain follow-ups.

Validation: 8 test files, each with exactly one test and one SVG visual snapshot; 553 assertions, typecheck, format, and visual inspection of the title block.
