title: Add resolved drawing dimension lines
description: Adds drawing_dimension_line as a resolved drawing primitive, allowing core precomputation of line placement and measurement text before serialization.
body:
Adds `drawing_dimension_line` as a resolved drawing primitive. Core will precompute the line placement and measurement text before serialization.

```ts
{
  type: "drawing_dimension_line",
  drawing_dimension_line_id: "bore_width",
  drawing_part_view_id: "tube_end",
  start: { x: -17, y: 18 },
  end: { x: 17, y: 18 },
  text: "34.0",
  edge_ref_start: { x: -17, y: 10 },
  edge_ref_end: { x: 17, y: 10 },
  edge_ref_name: "inner_top",
}
```

`start`/`end` are distinct finite page-centered paper coordinates in mm (+X right, +Y up). `edge_ref_start` and `edge_ref_end` independently attach optional witness lines to the measured feature in the same coordinate space. `edge_ref_name` preserves optional exact nonblank model-feature metadata. Required preformatted `text` preserves the model measurement independently of the paper span.

Replaces the unreleased `drawing_dimension` schema and its exports/registration. Removes target inference, owner/name lookup, `width_of_view`, `height_of_view`, `orientation`, `offset`, and `precision` from Circuit JSON. Width/height authoring intent remains in props; core resolves native geometry and emits the final drawing coordinates. No native model edge/topology schema is introduced. Core emission remains follow-up work.

Validation: all 503 tests (2723 assertions), typecheck, ESM/DTS build, Zod lint, snake_case, generated docs, and changed-file formatting pass locally. The single visual schema test covers scaled paper span versus model text, independent witness points, exact text/name preservation, finite points, distinct endpoints, and old-schema removal.

Related: [props #953](https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/953), [exporter #3](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-drawing/pull/3), [Fiber #142](https://github.com/tscircuit/jscad-fiber/pull/142), and [JSCAD #504](https://github.com/tscircuit/jscad-electronics/pull/504).

title: fix: preserve SVG sweep direction for semicircular NPTH cutouts
description: Fixes incorrect SVG rendering of semicircular NPTH cutouts by preserving the correct sweep direction, ensuring accurate representation of the cutouts in PCB designs.
body:
C5815189's NPTH locator is imported as an inward-pinched **0.7999984 × 0.7099808 mm** polygon because the shared arc helper reverses exact SVG semicircles. This makes sweep=1 follow increasing source angles and samples semicircle midpoints, producing the source's convex **1.5099792 × 0.7099808 mm** capsule.

**Stacked on #608. Merge order: #608 → this PR.** This PR targets the reproduction branch and changes the **same three existing PCB SVG snapshots** from pinched to convex, using `convertCircuitJsonToPcbSvg` and `toMatchSvgSnapshot`. The raw fixture, board sizes, and snapshot filenames are unchanged. The expected-failing source-arc assertion becomes an ordinary passing regression.

Eight generic direction tests cover both sweep flags, both large-arc flags, and semicircular/non-semicircular arcs. Four angular-span cases independently accumulate signed angles between consecutive radial vectors: the radius-2, chord-2 fixture must travel 60° for a minor arc and 300° for a major arc, in both sweep directions. The existing semicircle-tolerance and silkscreen arc tests remain passing. The C7203002 inline TSX snapshot is updated for the same correction in five fabrication-note paths. The five other affected inline snapshots and C41430893 PCB SVG are also regenerated through their canonical test helpers after inspecting the arc changes.

**This was not caused by #605.** The arc helper and NPTH walker are byte-identical before and after that PR. The affected source route was introduced by #593; #605 handled the separate dimensioned `pcb_hole` generator branch.

**Supplier discrepancy remains separate:** GCT drawing A2 specifies **1.01 × 0.71 mm**. The captured EasyEDA source itself specifies a **1.5099792 × 0.7099808 mm** capsule. This generic converter fix preserves source geometry; it does not hard-code the part's drawing dimensions. Round-hole diameter and relative center spacing remain Ø0.7099808 mm and 7.999984 mm.

### Validation

- [GitHub Actions tests](https://github.com/tscircuit/easyeda-converter/actions/runs/39859378968): **365 pass, 0 fail** across all three shards, on head `49f62e1711f1db65d43a056ebde3d34b1068f4d6`.
- [Type check](https://github.com/tscircuit/easyeda-converter/actions/runs/39859379013), [format check](https://github.com/tscircuit/easyeda-converter/actions/runs/39859378978), and [preview package build/publish](https://github.com/tscircuit/easyeda-converter/actions/runs/39859379000) all pass. Preview publishing initially returned an upstream HTTP 500; its retry succeeded.
- Focused arc/reproduction suite: **24 pass, 0 fail**, 109 assertions. Angular-span cases assert 60° minor arcs and 300° major arcs in both sweep directions.
- Against the original helper, the new strict regressions produce **6 failures**; with the fix all pass.
- Six CI snapshot failures were reproduced with network access and repaired. Earlier sandboxed model-download failures prevented those snapshot assertions from running locally. No checks were skipped or weakened.
- Also verified source → TSX → native output in latest **tscircuit 0.0.3004**: polygon points preserved exactly, width/height match the source within 1e-7 mm.
- All three regenerated C5815189 PCB snapshots and the C41430893 SVG change were visually inspected.

| Reproduction (#608) | Fixed |
| --- | --- |
| ![Inward-pinched locator](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/easyeda-converter/852738cd6b0950c8b68b7b00062e043bbc6571c6/tests/__snapshots__/c5815189-locators.snap.svg) | ![Outward capsule](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/easyeda-converter/a68f733d46c6133b32fd017e9925af8b7e55f96b/tests/__snapshots__/c5815189-locators.snap.svg) |

[Intermediate PCB snapshot diff](https://github.com/tscircuit/easyeda-converter/compare/codex/repro-c5815189-cutout-sweep...codex/fix-c5815189-cutout-sweep#diff) · [Native PCB after fix](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/easyeda-converter/a68f733d46c6133b32fd017e9925af8b7e55f96b/tests/__snapshots__/c5815189-native.snap.svg)

title: test: reproduce C5815189 inward-pinched NPTH cutout with native PCB snapshots

body:
C5815189's actual EasyEDA `SOLIDREGION npth` becomes an inward-pinched polygon before TSX generation. This captures the live raw response and reproduces its **0.7999984 × 0.7099808 mm** cutout, while verifying that footprint TSX and native PCB rendering preserve the polygon exactly.

This **predates #605**: the arc helper and path walker are byte-identical on that PR's parent and merged result. #593 introduced the NPTH cutout route; #605 only handled dimensioned `pcb_hole` generation.

The actual supplier path describes a **1.5099792 × 0.7099808 mm** convex capsule. Drawing A2 specifies **1.01 × 0.71 mm**, so the supplier-width discrepancy must remain separate from correcting arc direction. Round locator Ø0.7099808 mm; horizontal center spacing 7.999984 mm.

title: fix: synchronize footprint polarity with component pin labels
description: Fixes the mismatch between electrical anodecathode labels and footprint artwork for diodes, LEDs, and capacitors, ensuring consistent polarity representation in generated footprints.
body:
A diode/LED can connect its electrical anode to pad 2 through `pinLabels` while footprinter still draws its positive artwork beside pad 1. Resolve polarity before generating the footprint so the electrical terminals and fabrication/silkscreen artwork use the same mapping.

For example, `<led footprint="led0805" pinLabels={{ pin1: ["cathode", "neg"], pin2: ["anode", "pos"] }} />` now generates the footprint with `anodepin2_cathodepin1`, without modifying user props or numeric pad identities. Explicit footprint polarity options must agree with the labels; contradictory inputs produce a readable error.

Also forwards capacitor `polarized` to footprinter, selecting capacitor geometry for bare chip sizes when needed. Explicit capacitor `positivepin`/`negativepin` options and the cathode-first defaults of DO-219AD/SOD-323HE now initialize unambiguous electrical aliases instead of attaching both positive and negative aliases to each pin. Capacitor `pinLabels` are not added here; that API is not accepted by the current capacitor props schema.

### Reproduction and snapshots

`bun test tests/components/normal-components/footprinter-polarity-labels.test.tsx` fails on unchanged main: the positive annotation lies on the opposite side of the body from its emitted electrical anode (dot product −2.59875, expected positive). It passes with this fix. Additional board regressions cover matching/conflicting options, input immutability, cathode-first defaults, capacitor controls, rotation and bottom-layer mirroring.

![Default and reversed polarity, including transformed bottom-layer parts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/core/734c8a9e/tests/components/normal-components/__snapshots__/footprinter-polarity-labels-pcb.snap.svg)

![Positive capacitor terminal 1, terminal 2, and nonpolarized control](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/core/734c8a9e/tests/components/normal-components/__snapshots__/footprinter-capacitor-polarity-pcb.snap.svg)

### Footprinter integration

Related marking PRs: https://github.com/tscircuit/footprinter/pull/926 and https://github.com/tscircuit/footprinter/pull/927. title: fix: recognize trace endcap copper touching a pad
description: Fixes the issue where a constant-width trace was incorrectly reported as not connected to a pad when its round copper endcap physically overlaps the pad, even if the endpoint center is outside the pad.
body:
A constant-width trace can physically contact a pad through its round copper endcap even when the endpoint center is outside the pad. Contiguity previously reported that connection missing; this fix recognizes positive copper overlap on a matching layer.

Stacked on the focused repro #472 (merge the repro first). Its snapshot shows two named pads, one trace, the endpoint center, and the measured 0.029 mm copper overlap. In this PR that same snapshot changes from red `Connectivity errors: 1` with the missing-connection message to green `Connectivity errors: 0` / `No missing connections.` The copper geometry is identical before/after. A control moves the endpoint back to create a real 0.071 mm gap and still requires the missing-connection error. The existing motor-controller regression and snapshot update remain.

Use the existing shape-aware pad clearance geometry, the width of the adjacent nondegenerate segment, and cached pad bounds to reject distant candidates before the exact contact check. Interpolated traces remain conservative; tangency, gaps, and contact on the wrong layer are not accepted. No production code changes were needed for the new focused visualization.

Needed by the terminal trace-pair repair in https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3178.

Validation: main reports the reproduced error; the fixed checker returns none for the same geometry. All 62 focused contiguity/repro tests pass (100 assertions), including the real-gap control and the existing motor-controller regression. Focused TypeScript and formatting checks pass. Both snapshot versions were rendered and visually inspected.

The focused snapshot uses the standard `convertCircuitJsonToPcbSvg` rendering directly: default PCB colors, native error markers, and PCB notes for the actual error count/message. No custom SVG banner or wrapper.

body:
Two pads on the top layer are physically connected by a 0.15 mm trace, but contiguity reports a missing connection because the trace endpoint center is outside the receiving pad. Its round copper endcap overlaps that pad by 0.029 mm.

This minimal repro captures the current false positive in a readable snapshot: two named pads, one trace, an endpoint marker, measured overlap, and the actual checker count/message (`Connectivity errors: 1`). Moving the endpoint back creates a real 0.071 mm gap, which is checked separately as a control.

The focused snapshot uses the standard `convertCircuitJsonToPcbSvg` rendering directly: default PCB colors, native error markers, and PCB notes for the actual error count/message. No custom SVG banner or wrapper.

title: fix(cli): prevent complete source JSON overwrite during Gerber export
description: Fixes a bug where exporting Gerber files would overwrite the entire source JSON file, leading to data loss.
body:
Running `circuit-to-gerber board.json` or exporting an extensionless `board` without `--output` currently **truncates the entire source file and replaces all of its JSON contents with ZIP bytes**, while reporting success. The whole original board JSON is lost from that path. Recovering that JSON requires another copy, such as Git history or a backup.

The default path uses `input.replace(".circuit.json", ".gerbers.zip")`. When the suffix is absent, the output equals the input: the CLI reads the JSON, then `createWriteStream` truncates that same file. A directory name containing `.circuit.json` can also be rewritten instead of the filename.

### Result after this fix

Derive the archive path from the filename's suffix, preserving its directory, and reject an explicit output that resolves to the input path before conversion or writing.

| Input | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `board.circuit.json` | Writes `board.gerbers.zip` | Same behavior |
| `board.json` | Replaces the whole source JSON with ZIP data | Preserves JSON; writes `board.gerbers.zip` |
| `board` | Replaces the whole source JSON with ZIP data | Preserves JSON; writes `board.gerbers.zip` |
| `project.circuit.json/board.json` | Rewrites the directory name | Preserves JSON; writes `project.circuit.json/board.gerbers.zip` |

For example, `circuit-to-gerber board.json --output ./board.json` now exits with an explanatory error and leaves the source bytes unchanged. Valid custom output paths continue to work.

### Validation

- 11 actual CLI subprocess tests use the existing USB-C flashlight board fixture, including its real components, pads, and traces. They verify byte-identical input, ZIP CRCs, Gerber/drill contents, uppercase suffixes, directory names containing `.circuit.json`, custom outputs, and resolved same-path rejection. On upstream `34b217c`: 3 pass, 8 fail. With the fix: 11 pass, 0 fail.
- `bun test --timeout 30000`: 203 pass, 0 fail. The initial default five-second run had six rendering timeouts.
- Built Node CLI: six smoke checks pass, including source preservation and same-path rejection.
- Package build, TypeScript check, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. The full formatter reports the existing oversized `blinkByddy.json` fixture warning and exits successfully.

This is limited to the CLI bug and regression coverage; it changes no Circuit JSON schema or public library API.

Built on NOyu015's #182 with the original author commits preserved. The JSON-suffix handling follows iprasen's #178, credited in the follow-up commit.

Fixes #169.

title: Fix CDN static sites with the standalone viewer and embedded circuit data
description: Fixes CDN static sites that reference outdated JavaScript files, ensuring they use the latest version of the RunFrame library and properly embed circuit data in the generated HTML.
body:
Static sites built with `--use-cdn-javascript` currently reference `tscircuit/dist/browser.min.js`. Its embedded evaluation worker pushes recent releases past jsDelivr's 50 MiB file limit, leaving deployed pages stuck at the loader.

Resolve the latest `@tscircuit/runframe` release from npm at build time and write its concrete, versioned `dist/standalone.min.js` CDN URL into the generated HTML. Each build checks npm again; already-built sites keep the version they were built with. Registry errors fail the build clearly.

The existing multi-circuit command and viewer remain supported:

```sh
tsci build --site --use-cdn-javascript
```

This keeps the file picker, circuit gallery, File/View menus, PCB/schematic/3D views, hash navigation and configured custom tabs. Multi-circuit sites keep their separate JSON files and thumbnails.

For a single-circuit CDN site, embed Circuit JSON safely in the existing HTML template and expose it through a Blob URL in `TSCIRCUIT_RUNFRAME_STATIC_FILE_LIST`. The standard standalone viewer consumes this through its existing static-file interface. Only `dist/index.html` needs deploying when the remaining assets use external URLs. Automatic gallery thumbnails are skipped for these builds; explicitly requested image outputs still work.

Explicit local JS CDN bundling remains supported, while CDN mode avoids implicitly copying a standalone CLI distribution's local cache. No new CLI flag or preview entrypoint is introduced. Viewer scripts, external CAD models and iframe tabs still load from their external URLs; local model URLs, explicit `--bundle-jscdn` and local `--jscdn-base-url` settings require deploying those assets.

Validation:
- 31 tests passed across 9 files, including fresh npm lookups across releases, registry HTTP/connection failures, invalid metadata, deterministic CLI builds, JSON round-tripping and escaping, concurrency 1 and 2, gallery references/thumbnails, custom tabs and explicit image/JS CDN outputs.
- TypeScript checks, CLI build, formatting, targeted Biome checks and `git diff --check` passed.
- A live CLI build resolved RunFrame `0.0.3059`; its standalone CDN bundle downloaded successfully at 28,932,717 bytes. Verified switching between two circuits and opening the gallery in the browser.
- Previously exported the deployed RP2040 motor-controller data into a 2,878,857-byte HTML file, confirmed all 5,186 embedded elements matched, and verified PCB, schematic and 3D views while serving only that HTML. The input's existing routing DRC error was preserved; export was checked with `--ignore-errors --ignore-warnings`.
- No Markdown files are changed.

title: Run PCB SPICE through the scoped Circuit JSON library
description: Adds pcb_spice support to tsci simulate analog, allowing a TSX simulation entry to run native PCB SPICE analysis and write reports while preserving existing ngspice behavior.
body:
Adds `pcb_spice` support to `tsci simulate analog`, allowing a TSX simulation entry to run native PCB SPICE analysis and write reports. Existing ngspice simulations retain their current behavior.

## Usage

```bash
tsci simulate analog ./simulation.tsx
```

To choose the report directory:

```bash
tsci simulate analog ./simulation.tsx --output ./runs/my-simulation
```

The TSX entry selects `spiceEngine="pcb_spice"` and supplies its modeling export. There is no separate `--modeling` file option. Native solvers are discovered through `PATH`: `fasthenry`, `FasterCap`, and `ngspice`. No solver-path configuration file is required.

By default, reports are written to `runs/simulation-<timestamp>`. A directory supplied with `--output` must not already exist.

## Implementation

- Renders TSX afresh for each simulation, preserving modeling exports and imported-board serialization. Saved Circuit JSON inputs are also supported.
- Loads local IBIS sources and runs the PCB SPICE pipeline with native solvers.
- Rejects mixed simulation engines in a single entry.
- Keeps build handlers and shared build-cache behavior unchanged.
- Updates the required core/schema dependencies and pins the prepared pipeline dependency to an immutable revision.

The diff contains no test or documentation-file changes.

## Validation

TypeScript checking, the CLI build, and the existing analog simulation, cache, and KiCad PCM tests pass (3 tests). The analog test emits an existing core autorouting warning while completing successfully.

title: Parallelize independent high-density force improvement nodes
description: Parallelizes the processing of independent high-density force improvement nodes in the autorouting pipeline, enhancing performance and efficiency during routing tasks.
body:
Current head `315499234a6e58e052a70d2ccca33cdd7a196127` is stacked on updated #3170 head `6945310`. Both retain version `0.0.1001`, trace-simplification `054d77`, repair04 `4273e94`, and combined repair03 `5760ca3`. This PR remains exactly 17 force source/test paths relative to its updated base. All applicable CI checks and Vercel pass on this head.

Current validation: fresh production ESM/DTS and both embedded workers pass with Bun 1.4.2; 14 focused runtime tests / 1,146 assertions pass. Packed direct and rebundled Bun/Node consumers pass using four routing workers, and browser synchronous use passes. Generated payloads remain build artifacts.

The historical benchmark and full-dataset quality results below apply to their explicitly recorded base `7eff946` and head `b1de497`. An updated-head benchmark is pending.

Pipeline9 force improvement processes independent nodes sequentially. Compute those nodes through the existing Bun/Node worker pool, then publish results in original sample order. The synchronous numerical step, output, statistics, iteration limits, visualization order and sync/async resume retain native behavior; later worker errors wait for their original position.

Stacked directly on #3170. Each task contains one assigned node, its routes, force settings and relevant colors, without full-board SRJ, obstacles or connectivity context. Register the task in Bun, Node and source-test workers.

The [completed `/benchmark --dataset 18 --threads 4` run](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3176#issuecomment-6333856545) compares base `7eff946` and head `b1de497` on the same 8-CPU ARM64 runner with Bun 1.4.2:

| Metric | Base | PR | Base (4T) | PR (4T) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| P50 time | 49.7s | 49.2s | 33.0s | 31.9s |
| P95 time | 195.3s | 183.8s | 134.2s | 123.9s |
| Completion / DRC pass | 16/16 | 16/16 | 16/16 | 16/16 |

All 64 attempts solve, with zero DRC issues or timeouts and unchanged average via/angled-trace counts. The four-thread force stage falls **26.408s → 15.268s (42.2% less time)**. Whole-board four-thread elapsed sums fall **789.5s → 776.8s (1.6% less time)**; matched-board median speedup is only **1.002×**. This is one fixed-order run, so the small overall difference is not evidence of a repeatable broad speedup.

PR synchronous → PR four-thread scaling is **1.393× matched-board median**, **1.394× aggregate** (1082.7s → 776.8s). The separate ratio of reported P50 times is 1.542×. Per-board ratios use log timings rounded to 0.1s. Serial passes use three concurrent samples; four-thread passes use one sample with four effective routing workers.

Four-thread memory P50 rises 1903.4 → 1925.4 MiB, and P80 rises 2452.5 → 2654.9 MiB. Joint DRC repair and port pathing still account for 56.9% of recorded PR four-thread stage time. **The 2× overall goal remains unmet.**

The cache experiment #3171 is excluded because its clean full-dataset comparison did not establish a repeatable benefit. Joint repair is restored byte-for-byte to #3170. Six prior-head complete-pipeline runs against that recorded cache-free base pass on samples 002, 014 and 015: byte-identical complete SRJs, identical iterations, all non-timing phase statistics/state/property order including physical DRC counters, and zero benchmark or declared board/continuity DRC errors. Only explicit clock fields are excluded.

Prior-head validation on `b1de497`: all applicable CI checks and Vercel passed. 27 local tests pass with 6,190 assertions. Production ESM/DTS, rebuilt embedded workers, packed Bun/Node direct and rebundled consumers, browser synchronous use and actual production Node four-worker jobs pass. Focused tests cover changed geometry, terminals/vias, unassigned routes, reverse completion, deferred failure, MAX0/MAX3 boundaries, absolute stop prefixes, resume, empty input and outer Pipeline9 budgets.

The earlier captured-input warm-pool AB/BA screen, without force-kernel prewarming, reduced the force stage by 46.0% on sample002 and 41.2% on sample014 while preserving complete output/state/statistics/order/input immutability and visualizations. Those are stage-only results, consistent with the full-dataset force-stage gain above.

title: Reduce repeated regional routing work and repair search allocations
description: Reduces repeated regional routing work by stopping unnecessary neighbor expansions after a goal is accepted, optimizing search allocations and improving solver efficiency.
body:
Regional routing repeatedly prepares fixed neighbor metadata, repair searches allocate replacement objects on priority decreases, and several collision paths rescan fixed geometry. This change pins four focused solver fixes and stops ordinary single-route search immediately after accepting its checked goal.

<!-- visual-optimization-snapshots -->
### Visual snapshots

PNG previews of the checked SVG regression snapshots, generated from the live reference and optimized test observations.

**Stop expanding after accepting the goal.** The frozen original step creates eight unused neighbor objects after success. The optimized step creates zero and preserves the full route and all ten iterations; both solver variants are checked.

![Visual snapshot: Stop expanding after accepting the goal](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/b1aeb3eaa1d362c150c33278f86c84b79dd152f1/tests/solvers/__snapshots__/single-route-stop-at-goal-visual.preview.png)

[SVG snapshot](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/blob/b1aeb3eaa1d362c150c33278f86c84b79dd152f1/tests/solvers/__snapshots__/single-route-stop-at-goal-visual.snap.svg) · [Snapshot test](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/blob/b1aeb3eaa1d362c150c33278f86c84b79dd152f1/tests/solvers/single-route-stop-at-goal.test.ts)

title: Fix custom symbol variants and pin connectivity (#663)
description: Fixes incorrect pin connectivity for custom symbols with the same name by ensuring distinct library IDs for different variants, resolving issues with disconnected wires.
body:
Same-named custom symbols currently reuse the first library definition even when their artwork or pins differ. In #663, a width-4 instance uses the width-2 definition, leaving its wire disconnected. This change shares complete matching symbol definitions and assigns distinct definitions unique library IDs through the existing component-to-library mapping.

Stacked on #738. Fixes #663 once both PRs reach main.

KiCad stores schematic coordinates in 0.0001 mm units. Derive local pin offsets from the rounded sheet origin and directly transformed source pin, so the placed pin meets the wire even at rounding boundaries. Drawing dimensions use that same native precision; text and pin identifiers remain unchanged. Reserve source symbol names and power-rail IDs before allocating variant suffixes. No net labels or dependencies are added.

The snapshot repro in #738 declares A1, A2, A3 and their resistor connections directly in TSX. This PR updates its PNG: A2 now has the correct width and joins R2. Native KiCad netlist checks verify all three connections, and the equivalent narrow instances still share one definition.

The five edge-case tests use explicit TSX components and traces, one test per file and no beforeAll. They cover artwork/fill/text differences, pin numbers and names, an explicitly named Shared_2 declared after a variant, power-rail name collisions, and fractional pin positions on all four sides, including adjacent native coordinates and a half-unit boundary. Circuit construction uses no case tables or hand-written Circuit JSON fixtures.

Existing repro22 and repro25 additionally check the previously disconnected J2/J4 and U3 pins against native netlists. Their two affected SVG snapshots are updated using verified KiCad 10.0.1 Linux output.

title: feat: make copper-pour opacity configurable
description: Adds a configurable opacity parameter for copper pours in the 3D viewer, allowing for a single rendering pass instead of eight.
body:
The 3D viewer currently needs **eight copper-pour drawing passes to compensate for Circuit2Canvas's hardcoded 50% opacity**. In [`createCopperPourTextureForLayer`](https://github.com/tscircuit/3d-viewer/blob/75d06ad913acd1549cd37f7380561b78be7d067e/src/textures/create-copper-pour-texture-for-layer.ts#L27-L30), `COPPER_POUR_OPACITY_COMPENSATION_PASSES = 8` makes the same pours and drill elements render repeatedly until the texture is effectively opaque and matches the traces and pads. Callers cannot currently request an opaque pour directly.

Add `copperPourOpacity` to `drawElements`, forwarded to the shared pour renderer's optional `opacity` parameter. This lets the viewer replace the eight passes with a single call after adopting the updated package:

```ts
drawer.drawElements(elements, {
  layers: ["top_copper"],
  copperPourOpacity: 1,
})
```

The default remains 0.5, preserving existing rendering. Pixel assertions and one combined PNG snapshot cover default, zero, fractional, and full opacity for rectangular, polygon, and BRep pours across top, bottom, and inner layers, including transparent BRep holes and restored canvas alpha. The snapshot places all four opacity settings side by side over a checkerboard. The explicit opacity cases fail against the previous renderer and pass with this change.

Validation: all 209 tests pass with existing snapshots unchanged and one new comparison snapshot; TypeScript, build, and format checks pass.

title: Reduce A01 queue writes and redundant node storage
description: Reduces the number of writes to the A01 heap by implementing hole-based sifts, eliminating unnecessary node priority storage, while maintaining existing array structures and behaviors.
body:
A01 swaps all three heap arrays at each sift level and also copies the heap priority into every private search node even though that copy is never read. Use hole-based sifts to move parent/child entries and write the queued item once, then remove the unused node priority field. The existing number arrays, separate sequence values, comparator behavior, search budgets, heuristic scores and routing policy remain unchanged. #103 also explores hole sifts; this PR keeps the current storage and tie ordering.

title: Refresh via and segment indices after force detours
description: Fixes incorrect routing behavior by refreshing via and segment indices when segment movement changes the routes point count, preventing validation failures in explicit-via scenarios.
body:
A segment force can insert a bend before a via. `applyDrcErrorForces` then reuses cached point indices later in the same error, moving the wrong points and splitting the via's layer endpoints. Dataset18 sample015 reaches this case and fails Pipeline9's explicit-via validation.

Rebuild the via and segment views immediately when segment movement changes the route's point count. This preserves the existing force sequence for moves without topology changes and retains the strict route validator.

Source commit `5760ca3cdd5bb3d0e29975a3225fd46730412173` incorporates main `d003ab47`, including its trace-obstacle overlap guard. The PR still changes exactly the index-refresh helper and its regression test relative to main. Current head `030252b278c06e0776c481a289e72fe83fa62e4f` is an empty CI retry with the identical source tree; the previous runner recorded successful tests but did not finalize its status. Consumers #3170 and #3176 retain the identical pinned source commit `5760ca3`.

Current validation: 15 focused tests / 80 assertions pass. GitHub tests, Typecheck (including the separately installed USB fixture), and formatcheck all pass on the current retry head. The complete test run records 138 passed / 0 failed / 26,387 assertions. Consumer production ESM/DTS, fresh Bun/Node workers and packed direct/rebundled four-worker parity pass with the combined dependency.

Prior-head validation on `6fb56fa`: the new five-point regression fails on the previous main and passes with this fix; seven focused tests pass with 21,785 assertions; strict TypeScript passes. The captured global stage no longer splits the affected via. Full consumer sample015 completes in both synchronous and four-worker modes with byte-identical SRJs, equal 2,456,774 iterations, equal non-timing Joint statistics, and zero benchmark and declared board/continuity DRC errors. title: Reduce repair search allocations and index junction anchors
description: Reduces memory allocations during repair searches by reusing queue entries and optimizing dense heap position updates, while indexing junction anchors for improved performance.
body:
Repair searches allocated a new queue entry on every priority decrease and routed dense heap position updates through closure adapters. Use scalar enqueues inside the searches to reuse pending entries, and access the existing dense position array directly during heap moves. The same comparisons, ties, costs, enqueue/pop order, and search accounting remain in use.

<!-- visual-optimization-snapshots -->
### Visual snapshots

PNG previews of the checked SVG regression snapshots, generated from the live reference and optimized test observations.

**Queue-entry reuse on a priority decrease.** A real queued entry changes priority 998 → 996. The original replaces the object; the optimized queue reuses it. Total allocations are 3,001 → 1,033 in both storage modes.

![Visual snapshot: Queue-entry reuse on a priority decrease](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/repair04/58a5f789df1d380f706bcdbfd4d64e7868182117/tests/__snapshots__/clearance-path-scalar-heap-parity-visual.preview.png)

[SVG snapshot](https://github.com/tscircuit/repair04/blob/58a5f789df1d380f706bcdbfd4d64e7868182117/tests/__snapshots__/clearance-path-scalar-heap-parity-visual.snap.svg) · [Snapshot test](https://github.com/tscircuit/repair04/blob/58a5f789df1d380f706bcdbfd4d64e7868182117/tests/clearance-path-scalar-heap-parity.test.ts)

The SVGs are regression-tested; the PNGs above are rendered from those exact checked-in SVGs for inline display.
<!-- /visual-optimization-snapshots -->

Compatibility follow-up for autorouter #3160: merge `4273e9455084b7b35ebc860ebe4483b9d19692ea`, the fixed-collar via correction already used by autorouter main, into this optimized branch. Revision `792d6ab1b034d95e63621b03624463cf003a231e` retains both changes. All 170 tests and the type check pass; the allocation snapshot and its visual remain unchanged. The historical performance measurements below use the original isolated optimization pin and do not benchmark this later correctness merge.

Public object enqueues retain the supplied object's identity and ownership. A queue receiving an object enqueue stops reusing its pending objects until it empties; popped objects remain unchanged when a state is reinserted. Internal scalar enqueues use ordinary `{ id, cost, priority }` entries with the same field order.

Junction preservation also scanned every same-net/layer anchor for every route segment and via. Index the immutable anchor disks by net and layer, query conservative local bounds, and retain the exact geometry and connectivity checks. Candidates retain insertion order so epsilon-based junction deduplication produces the same result.

Validation on this branch, including the visual regression:

- All 170 tests pass with 554,706 assertions; TypeScript and targeted formatting checks pass.
- Frozen-queue differential tests compare complete heap arrays, dense/sparse positions, and popped sequences across 8,000 operations, including decreases, ties, reinsertion, signed-zero IDs, and mixed object/scalar ownership.
- An independent replay of the saved SRJ18 sample14 right-via-cluster region preserves all 388,734 enqueue/pop events, routes, stats, and 2,962 solver steps. Queue-entry allocations decrease from 288,734 to 170,182: 118,552 fewer allocations (41.1%). All 100,000 heap pops and 94 search calls remain identical. The original dense queue performs 2,137,649 position-adapter calls in that replay; direct array access removes those calls.
- Junction-index regression coverage matches the original exhaustive output across traces, vias, aliases, full/cropped bounds, reversed insertion order, and epsilon tangencies.

The combined consumer patch is benchmarked in [tscircuit-autorouter #3160](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3160): 107 scenarios on paired Blacksmith ARM runners, unchanged effort/search limits, all 106 completed route SVGs byte-identical, and no new completion or DRC failures. The five completed selected SRJ28 cases take 19.26% less total time (3.15% including the unchanged timeout); the heaviest completed case is 39.16% faster and reproduces a 37.01–44.80% speedup in a four-pass order control. Dataset01 is 2.92% faster in one paired run, while SRJ18 total time is effectively flat. These end-to-end figures measure the combined solver changes; they are not isolated attribution to this PR. Peak RSS is mixed and variable, including a 19.24% increase for sample 37 in the primary run that does not consistently reproduce in the order control. No uniform RSS reduction is claimed. Full per-case results, quality checks, memory quantiles, limitations and workflow links are in the consumer PR.

[Queue allocation snapshot](https://github.com/tscircuit/repair04/blob/71e69da363e8b1461264501edf93c6bd0925b1d6/tests/__snapshots__/clearance-path-scalar-heap-parity.test.ts.snap) records 3,001 original object allocations versus 1,033 heap-owned scalar-entry allocations in each of the dense and sparse cases. It also records the preserved pop sequence boundaries and retained popped objects; the live frozen-queue comparison checks all heap state and popped values, including ownership after reinsertion.

The earlier snapshot follow-up commits change only tests and checked-in deterministic snapshots. Those snapshot commits left production code and dependency pins unchanged; the compatibility merge above additionally retains the upstream fixed-collar via correction. The snapshots record operation counts rather than elapsed time. All four dependency solver suites (500 passing tests), all five repository type checks, and the autorouter goal regression pass locally.


Earlier visual follow-up validation: all 500 dependency solver tests pass locally with four existing skips; all five repository type checks and the autorouter visual regression pass. Solver production code and runtime dependency pins are unchanged. The existing local formatter is pinned to Biome 2.5.15 for reproducible CI checks.


Formatting reproducibility: the floating Biome range began resolving 2.6.2, which introduced Markdown/YAML formatting failures in unchanged files. Pinning the locally validated 2.5.15 retains all format checks and keeps this PR focused on the solver and visual tests.

title: Preserve fixed collar vias during clearance negotiation
description: Fixes autorouter failure by preserving existing fixed collar vias during clearance negotiation, preventing them from disappearing when their layer transition is outside the crop.
body:
Clearance negotiation rebuilt each cropped route's vias only from local layer transitions. A fixed via whose transition was outside the crop disappeared, so autorouter board109 failed with `repair04 merge rejected a changed via in the boundary collar` even though the route points were unchanged.

Preserve existing vias outside the mutable bounds when they belong to the reconstructed fragment, while still rebuilding mutable vias from the resulting layer transitions. Apply this to both negotiation implementations; the merge invariant remains unchanged.

Validation: 167 Bun tests pass, TypeScript and formatting checks pass. The new fixed-collar regression fails on the original code. Autorouter board109 passes with zero relaxed DRC errors using this change and the rectdiff outline fix (tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter#3144).

title: fix: try native DDR pair seeds with larger continuation budgets
description: Attempts to fix routing issues by trying native DDR pair seeds with larger continuation budgets, allowing for improved routing around prior-byte copper.
body:
Stacked on #85. The shared native planner can miss a valid DQS0 route around prior-byte copper: its 6,000-yield handoff attempts neither offer the original zero-via native endpoints nor allow the 24,086 yields needed by the reproduced native route. Try a native pair seed on its allowed original pad layer for up to **60,000 yields**, then retain all existing generated-handoff/layer alternatives. Eligibility requires prior copper, exactly one pair in a hard-length bus, unconnected native component pads and a common globally/bus-allowed layer. Supplied copper stays fixed. Native surface pair repair receives **300,000 yields**; ordinary negotiation around the new seed receives **2,000,000** instead of 250,000. Other pair/ordinary search budgets are unchanged. Final connectivity, copper DRC, bus maximum/skew and pair skew/coupling acceptance remains mandatory. Validation: the native-seed regression passes 20 assertions, including a valid completed pair beyond 6,000 yields, forbidden global/bus layer controls, no-prior/no-bound/supplied-own-copper rejection, input immutability and actual pipeline dispatch to the helper. A second 11-assertion regression freshly generates the collective conflict and recovers pair repair after **201,522 pair yields / 202,047 including its computed ordinary candidate**. The recovered pair passes absolute length, skew/coupling and combined copper DRC including that ordinary candidate; inputs remain unchanged. The previous 60,000-yield repair cap missed it. Both targeted tests pass (31 assertions total), and TypeScript passes. The gated completed-pair snapshot is inspected and validated. **This completes the pair reproduction; complete second-byte or SBC routing is not yet claimed.** A separate 1,200-second diagnostic continuation with an even larger 600,000-yield repair budget recovered the same valid pair but remained incomplete in ordinary carrier negotiation (1,432,652 total steps; input unchanged). This exploratory control is separate from the final-revision benchmark. Increasing budgets alone has not demonstrated a full byte. Full CI on this revision: **517 tests passed, 0 failed**; formatting, typecheck, package validation and preview pass. ### Benchmark effect The [fresh final-revision Blacksmith comparison](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/actions/runs/39868623860) passes **11/11 on both base and head**. Every sample connects 47/47 signals, passes fixed/combined copper DRC, whole-copper bus/pair matching and coupling, preserves all 161 fixed power fanouts and leaves input unchanged. Validation objects and solver iteration counts are identical for all eleven samples. No completions lost or gained. Aggregate solve time: base **2405.258 s**, head **2506.658 s** (**+4.22%**). Single-run timing differences with identical algorithmic work do not establish a solver speedup or regression. This legacy comparison is separate from the native reproduction/repair controls above and does not establish full native BYTE0/SBC completion. All raw reports were independently checked, including revision/runtime provenance, input hashes, fixed copper and pair coupling.

title: fix: report collective escape conflicts to generated-pair repair
description: Fixes the omission of reporting proven empty domains during collective escape pruning, allowing for generated-pair repair to be attempted.
body:
Stacked on #83. When collective escape pruning proves a domain empty, report its connection through the same callback used for individually empty domains. `routeSurfaceOrdinarySignals` can then invoke generated-pair repair rather than silently skipping it. Support-check exhaustion retains unproven choices and emits no failure callback. Input domains, candidate references, prior copper and native routing input remain unchanged. This fixes repair feedback; it does not claim a complete native second DDR byte or SBC route. Validation: 10 targeted tests pass, including the real four-domain callback and a caller-level control verifying that pair repair is invoked, propagated/initial emptiness, inconclusive budget exhaustion and immutable inputs. Full CI on this revision: **515 tests passed, 0 failed**; formatting, typecheck, package validation and preview pass. ### Benchmark effect The [fresh final-revision Blacksmith comparison](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/actions/runs/39865194561) passes **11/11 on both base and head**. Every sample connects 47/47 signals, passes fixed/combined copper DRC, whole-copper bus/pair matching and coupling, preserves all 161 fixed power fanouts and leaves input unchanged. Validation objects and solver iteration counts are identical for all eleven samples. No completions lost or gained. Aggregate solve time: base **2943.266 s**, head **2794.593 s** (**-5.05%**). Single-run timing differences with identical algorithmic work do not establish a solver speedup or regression. This legacy comparison is separate from the native reproduction/repair controls above and does not establish full native BYTE0/SBC completion. Pinned base/controller `61554bbfd5724aba86d82433b5a2757a703171bc`; head `0590aed072a39821a3809bcb687c89938efd0766`. Same fixtures/harness, Bun 1.4.0, Blacksmith 4 vCPU and 3,600 seconds per solver/sample. All raw reports were independently checked, including revision/runtime provenance, input hashes, fixed copper and pair coupling.

title: repro: collective escape rejection skips generated-pair repair
description: Fixes the omission of necessary signal callbacks in collective escape pruning, preventing skipped generated pair repairs.
body:
Collective escape pruning proves a domain empty, but `negotiateSignalSites` returns null without its `onBlockedConnection` callback. `routeSurfaceOrdinarySignals` requires that callback to invoke generated-pair repair, so it skips a useful repair path. This reproduction freshly generates the public native DDR pair state, verifies the four-domain rejection and records the missing feedback while checking input immutability. Production behavior is unchanged. The stacked fix will require feedback for a proven empty domain, without treating support-check exhaustion as infeasibility. Validation: the targeted reproduction passes (one test, four assertions). Full CI: **511 tests passed, 0 failed**; formatting, typecheck, package validation and preview pass. ### Benchmark effect The [fresh final-revision Blacksmith comparison](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/actions/runs/39864902569) passes **11/11 on both base and head**. Every sample connects 47/47 signals, passes fixed/combined copper DRC, whole-copper bus/pair matching and coupling, preserves all 161 fixed power fanouts and leaves input unchanged. All validation objects and solver iteration counts are identical across all eleven samples. Aggregate solve time: base **2675.849 s**, head **2902.166 s** (**+8.46%**). This PR changes no production or fixture code. Single-run timing variation with identical algorithmic work does not establish a solver regression or speedup. No completions lost or gained. Pinned base/controller `5a6c0b9419c5fba7ea149152554ce24f5d5cdc8d`; head `61554bbfd5724aba86d82433b5a2757a703171bc`. Same fixtures/harness, Bun 1.4.0, Blacksmith 4 vCPU and 3,600 seconds per solver/sample. All raw reports were independently checked, including revision/runtime provenance, input hashes, copper preservation and pair coupling.

title: fix: recover collective DDR escape assignments around fixed prior copper
description: Fixes allocation failure for the second DDR byte when routing around previously completed copper, allowing for successful routing of the second byte.
body:
Stacked on #80 after repro #79. The second native DDR byte failed local escape assignment around the first byte's completed copper. The fallback moved nets that failed individual site probes, but could not recover when individually feasible choices conflicted collectively. After the existing fallback fails, try eligible native-pad cohorts individually, then cumulatively, with at most two trials per eligible cohort. Ordinary cohorts precede differential pairs; pair partners stay together. Global/bus layer restrictions, existing handoffs and supplied copper remain fixed. Successful initial allocations retain their existing path. Failed allocations now report the number of cohort trials. Validation: **508 tests passed, 0 failed across 175 files**; TypeScript, formatting, package validation and package preview checks pass. Three reduced geometry tests cover individually feasible but collectively conflicting sites, differential partners falling back together, and forbidden-layer rejection. The real sequential test freshly solves BYTE1, passes its exact 11 traces to BYTE0, and obtains 18 generated dogbones with independent native copper DRC while preserving inputs, caller target maps and prior copper. **Scope:** this fixes the reproduced escape-allocation failure and allows the second byte to enter routing. A separate 600-second continuation did not finish the second-byte interconnect. Full second-byte and SBC completion are not claimed; later pair/site search experiments are excluded from this PR. ### Benchmark effect The final-revision [Blacksmith acceptance check](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/actions/runs/39830585705) passes **11/11 on both base and head**. Every case connects 47/47 signals, passes combined copper DRC, total-copper bus/pair matching and coupling, and preserves all 161 fixed power dogbones and input data. Full validation objects and solver iteration counts are identical for all eleven samples. Aggregate solve time: base **3686.365 s**, head **3702.699 s** (**+0.44%**). The outer-layer case was slower (780.419 → 904.024 s); other cases were faster, including control-inner1 (1785.917 → 1746.475 s). These single-run differences with identical iterations/validation do not establish an algorithmic speedup or regression. Pinned base/controller: `a1452929b5aee4ddfd1e959c2c005a9277de3da3`; head: `68e2a3a60d7f46d0289b9ba7379fb6326f51f758`. Identical fixtures and harness, Bun 1.4.0, Blacksmith 4 vCPU, and 3,600 seconds per solver/sample. All raw base/head reports were checked independently; exact per-case timing, skew and input provenance follow.

title: repro: second DDR byte cannot escape around completed first phase
description: Fixes routing failure for the second DDR byte when attempting to assign dogbones around a freshly routed first byte.
body:
Stacked on #78. Freshly solves DDR_BYTE1 from the public fixture and supplies its exact 11 traces to DDR_BYTE0. The second phase reproduces the four-step local dogbone assignment failure and proves inputs/prior copper remain immutable. No saved route is a test input. #80 adds diagnostics; #81 fixes the collective allocation failure and replaces the failure assertions with independently DRC-checked successful allocation. Full second-byte interconnect completion is separate. Validation: targeted regressions, full CI unit suite, TypeScript, formatting and package checks pass. Fresh Blacksmith base/head comparison: **11/11 accepted on both revisions**, all 47/47 signals connected, combined copper DRC and total-copper bus/pair matching/coupling pass, and all 161 fixed power dogbones are preserved. Full validation objects and solver iteration counts are identical for every sample. Aggregate solve time across the eleven cases: base **2845.447 s**, head **2860.889 s**. Per-case timings, including slower cases, appear below. These single-run differences with identical iterations/validation do not establish an algorithmic speedup or regression. The pinned base harness uses identical fixtures and 3,600-second per-solver/sample budgets, Bun 1.4.0 and Blacksmith 4 vCPU. See the complete report for exact revisions and input hashes. ### Native reproduction snapshot Completed scoped BYTE1 route used by this stack's sequential reproduction. **11/11 BYTE1 connections** pass independent native copper DRC, whole-copper bus maximum/skew and pair skew/coupling. The snapshot represents this completed scoped byte, not the complete SBC. title: fix: use surface planning for a single hard-length native bus
description: Fixes routing logic to allow a single native bus with a hard maximum length to qualify for the existing surface planner, ensuring proper validation and connection checks are maintained.
body:
Stacked on #75. A single native bus with a hard maximum now qualifies for the existing surface planner. Other dispatch guards and final copper/timing validation remain intact. The repro becomes a normal passing test: 11 connections finish in 25,329 steps, with input immutability and bus/pair matching checked. #81 separately fixes the next phase's collective escape allocation; full SBC routing remains incomplete. Validation: targeted regressions, full CI unit suite, TypeScript, formatting and package checks pass. Fresh Blacksmith base/head comparison: **11/11 accepted on both revisions**, all 47/47 signals connected, combined copper DRC and total-copper bus/pair matching/coupling pass, and all 161 fixed power dogbones are preserved. Full validation objects and solver iteration counts are identical for every sample. Aggregate solve time across the eleven cases: base **3397.608 s**, head **3468.482 s**. Per-case timings, including slower cases, appear below. These single-run differences with identical iterations/validation do not establish an algorithmic speedup or regression. The pinned base harness uses identical fixtures and 3,600-second per-solver/sample budgets, Bun 1.4.0 and Blacksmith 4 vCPU. See the complete report for exact revisions and input hashes. ### Native reproduction snapshot Completed scoped BYTE1 route used by this stack's sequential reproduction. **11/11 BYTE1 connections** pass independent native copper DRC, whole-copper bus maximum/skew and pair skew/coupling. The snapshot represents this completed scoped byte, not the complete SBC. [Audit and exporter](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/blob/68e2a3a60d7f46d0289b9ba7379fb6326f51f758/docs/native-ddr-sequential/README.md). ![Completed scoped DDR_BYTE1, top and bottom](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/68e2a3a60d7f46d0289b9ba7379fb6326f51f758/docs/native-ddr-sequential/byte1-completed.png)

title: repro: single hard-length native DDR bus skips surface planning
description: Reproduces a native 11-connection DDR_BYTE1 phase being excluded from joint surface planning due to containing only one bus, with an expected-failure test under a 35,000-step budget.
body:
Reproduces a native 11-connection DDR_BYTE1 phase being excluded from joint surface planning because it contains only one bus. The desired completion/matching assertion is an expected-failure test under a 35,000-step budget. #78 supplies the fix; #79 → #80 → #81 cover the subsequent sequential allocation failure. No production solver changes in this PR. Validation: targeted regressions, full CI unit suite, TypeScript, formatting and package checks pass. Fresh Blacksmith base/head comparison: **11/11 accepted on both revisions**, all 47/47 signals connected, combined copper DRC and total-copper bus/pair matching/coupling pass, and all 161 fixed power dogbones are preserved. Full validation objects and solver iteration counts are identical for every sample. Aggregate solve time across the eleven cases: base **3562.874 s**, head **3437.216 s**. Per-case timings, including slower cases, appear below. These single-run differences with identical iterations/validation do not establish an algorithmic speedup or regression. The pinned base harness uses identical fixtures and 3,600-second per-solver/sample budgets, Bun 1.4.0 and Blacksmith 4 vCPU. See the complete report for exact revisions and input hashes. ### Native reproduction snapshot Completed scoped BYTE1 route from the stacked fix, rather than the failing base. **11/11 BYTE1 connections** pass independent native copper DRC, whole-copper bus maximum/skew and pair skew/coupling. The snapshot represents this completed scoped byte, not the complete SBC. title: Fix dependency installation in the publish workflow
description: Fixes the dependency installation failure in the publish workflow caused by the order of steps when using Bun 1.4.4.
body:
The publish workflow fails at dependency installation with Bun 1.4.4 because setup-node routes every @tscircuit dependency to GitHub Packages, where public npm dependencies return 404 ([failed run](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-webgpu/actions/runs/39880923880/job/120177831212)).

Move the existing bun install step before GitHub registry configuration. Publishing retains its existing registry and authentication setup. This changes only the order of one workflow step.

Validation: fresh dependency installation with Bun 1.4.4, followed by typecheck, all 106 unit tests, and build with the GitHub scope registry configured; git diff --check passed.

title: fix: rotate polygon plated-hole copper and drill offsets
description: Fixes the rotation of polygon plated-hole outlines and drill offsets around the pad anchor to ensure consistent ccw_rotation application across copper, slots, board cutouts, and soldermask openings.
body:
GitHub stack #75: [Repro #73](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-webgpu/pull/73) → [Fix #74](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-webgpu/pull/74).

Rotate polygon plated-hole outlines and drill offsets around the pad anchor using the existing `rotate` helper. This makes copper, slots, board cutouts and soldermask openings follow the same `ccw_rotation`.

The production change is confined to the existing compiler: rotate the polygon vertices and remove the special case that kept polygon-pad drill offsets in board coordinates. No new production function or file is needed.

Promotes the repro's seven failing geometry tests and GPU correctness test to passing tests. Updates `tests/snapshots/jae-shell-pad-90.png` from the broken rendering committed in #73 to the corrected rendering. The independent camera-rotation assertion and comparison tolerance are retained. Two older tests are updated to stop asserting the incorrect unrotated behavior.

![Corrected JAE shell-pad rendering](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-webgpu/codex/polygon-rotation-fix/tests/snapshots/jae-shell-pad-90.png)

`package.json` and workflow files are unchanged. Run browser checks directly with `WEBGPU_SOFTWARE=1 bun test --timeout 60000 ./tests/polygon-pad-rotation.browser.ts`.

Validation: 106 passing unit tests, both GPU checks, type checking and formatting. The compiler change also passed the existing 25 visual snapshots and build. GPU verification uses Chromium SwiftShader; unit discovery uses Bun 1.4.4.

Related to [pcb-viewer #980](https://github.com/tscircuit/pcb-viewer/issues/980) and the compatibility code in [pcb-viewer #1113](https://github.com/tscircuit/pcb-viewer/pull/1113).

title: test: reproduce polygon plated-hole rotation with a JAE shell pad
description: Reproduces a rendering bug where rotating a hole with a polygon pad leaves its copper outline and drill offset unrotated, adding tests to verify the issue and its resolution.
body:
GitHub stack #75: [Repro #73](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-webgpu/pull/73) → [Fix #74](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-webgpu/pull/74).

Rotating a `hole_with_polygon_pad` leaves its copper outline and drill offset unrotated, even though the slot itself rotates. This reproduces the mismatch using an original ground land for the JAE DX07S024JJ2 shell slot, also used in [pcb-viewer #1112](https://github.com/tscircuit/pcb-viewer/pull/1112).

Adds seven `test.failing` geometry regressions and a `test.failing` GPU comparison against an independently rotated camera view. The committed PNG records the current broken rendering; the fix PR updates that same file to the corrected rendering. A separate passing snapshot assertion checks that the recorded PNG matches the actual output.

![Current broken JAE shell-pad rendering](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-webgpu/codex/polygon-rotation-repro/tests/snapshots/jae-shell-pad-90.png)

Only test files are added. `package.json`, workflows and production code are unchanged. Run the browser checks directly with `WEBGPU_SOFTWARE=1 bun test --timeout 60000 ./tests/polygon-pad-rotation.browser.ts`. To regenerate the recorded rendering, add `UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1` to that command.

Validation: unit regressions and both GPU checks pass with the known failures marked `test.failing`. GPU verification uses Chromium SwiftShader and Bun 1.4.4.

Related: [pcb-viewer #980](https://github.com/tscircuit/pcb-viewer/issues/980) and [pcb-viewer #1113](https://github.com/tscircuit/pcb-viewer/pull/1113). Component dimensions: [JAE drawing, page 3](https://atta.szlcsc.com/upload/public/pdf/source/20221019/45408AD208B5AA4B3A1B5FD9AD1181E7.pdf#page=3); the copper land is original test artwork.

title: Derive PCB SPICE modeling from Circuit JSON
description: Derives PCB SPICE modeling directly from Circuit JSON records, allowing for simulation without an external modeling object and enhancing the integration of simulation settings.
body:
A TSX-declared PCB SPICE channel now drives `runPipeline` without an external modeling object. Derive lanes, extraction settings, passive scope, and via/profile settings from raw `simulation_experiment.pcb_spice_channel` records. Explicit modeling still overrides the circuit declaration; incompatible experiments fail clearly.

The ImportedBoard bridge accepts simulation-only voltage supplies, binds their terminals to saved-board ports, discards their temporary physical records, and remaps source-component/source-port ID arrays. IBIS models use their existing direct asset paths; existing explicit modeling options retain their behavior.

Uses published `circuit-json@0.0.534` and development `@tscircuit/props@0.0.709`, containing the merged schema/API changes from https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/pull/923 and https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/954. Compatible peer minimums remain unchanged.

body:
Importing the pipeline previously loaded a project runner, React, native setup, file output and runtime report compilation. Replace that boundary with `@tscircuit/pcb-spice-pipeline`: Circuit JSON, explicit modeling, supplied IBIS bytes and an injected solver callback go in; validated matrices, waveforms, probe-bound Circuit JSON graphs, eyes/DDR assessments and artifact strings come back.

```ts
const result = await runPipeline({ circuitJson, modeling, ibisSources, runSolver })
const reportFiles = generateReport(result)
```

The main entry performs no implicit filesystem, network, subprocess, environment, clock, console or source-loading actions. `/node` explicitly opts into installed solver execution, local model loading and output writing; `/tsx` exposes the saved-board bridge and serializer using optional host React/core peers. Remove the standalone CLI, installer/download paths, duplicate pipeline and install-time `prepare`. Ship compiled ESM/declarations and build the report client ahead of time.

Keep the existing matrix/convergence and model-hash checks. Reject nonzero solver exits and incomplete recordings, accept recovered ngspice operating-point warnings only with complete finite transients, and replace old graphs on reruns. Reports also work without Node's `Buffer` global.

Validation: both typechecks, all **145 tests**, packed Node/Bun runs, NodeNext consumer declarations, and a cold import/full run with host actions denied pass. Real CMOS and differential extractions reproduce every reference R/L/C entry and all 129,803/75,088 adaptive waveform samples exactly using the same installed binaries. A real saved-board DDR strip run also passes five extraction stages and two six-probe experiments (45,786/163,305 samples and four eyes). Browser waveform/eye controls were exercised. The historical routed AM3352 FastHenry numerical failure remains a separate limitation.

Consumers use an immutable prepared archive built from this source while the scoped package awaits npm publication. The archive contains the packed JavaScript/declarations and requires no preparation scripts. No npm publication or merge is performed here. Merge this API before the coordinated [CLI #5541](https://github.com/tscircuit/cli/pull/5541) and [DDR consumer #19](https://github.com/0hmX/am3352-ddr-eye/pull/19).

title: Render resolved dimension lines and optional gray edge names
description: Renders resolved drawing_dimension_line records using caller-supplied paper-space startend and preformatted text. Optional edge_ref_start and edge_ref_end independently attach witness lines. Optional edge_ref_name records the native feature name. The exporter preserves the supplied line endpoints and text. Arrow direction and readable text rotation follow those endpoints. There is no dimension orientation, offset, precision, model target lookup, or inferred-view measurement in the exporterCircuit JSON contract. Core will perform native geometry interpretation, measurement, projection and layout before emitting these records. Widthheight intent remains in props. showEdgeNames: true adds small gray feature names. With only resolved dimension metadata, labels use the witness points (or the line midpoint). Optional resolveModelEdges(view, input) enumerates all native named features, even without dimensions. Its runtime samples remain outside Circuit JSON and use the same camera as the part raster. Duplicate names are deduplicated, coincident labels are separated, and dimension text is reserved. Labels are disabled by default; their model callback is never invoked in that mode. The rounded tube demonstrations use the actual collected JSCAD solid and native extrusion outlines, with a shared indexed mesh converter. Test-only upstream preparation emits 34.0 mm bore, 40.0 mm outer width, 20.0 mm height and 80.0 mm length at explicit 1:1 scale. Native model geometrytopology stay with their readers. Validation: all 14 tests pass (665 assertions), with exactly one test and one visual SVG per test file. Typecheck and formatting pass. Coverage includes horizontalverticaldiagonalreversed lines, independent witnesses, supplied text versus paper span, movedscaled views, sections, XML escaping, input immutability, page bounds, default-off callbacks and native edge labels without dimensions. Real modeldrawing snapshots were visually inspected. !Tube resolved dimension lines(https:raw.githubusercontent.comtscircuitcircuit-json-to-drawingfeatnamed-edge-dimensionstests__snapshots__named-edge-dimensions.snap.svg) !Optional gray feature names(https:raw.githubusercontent.comtscircuitcircuit-json-to-drawingfeatnamed-edge-dimensionstests__snapshots__show-edge-names.snap.svg) Related: props 953(https:github.comtscircuitpropspull953), Circuit JSON 922(https:github.comtscircuitcircuit-jsonpull922), Fiber 142(https:github.comtscircuitjscad-fiberpull142), and JSCAD 504(https:github.comtscircuitjscad-electronicspull504).
body:
Renders resolved `drawing_dimension_line` records using caller-supplied paper-space `start`/`end` and preformatted `text`. Optional `edge_ref_start` and `edge_ref_end` independently attach witness lines. Optional `edge_ref_name` records the native feature name.

The exporter preserves the supplied line endpoints and text. Arrow direction and readable text rotation follow those endpoints. There is no dimension orientation, offset, precision, model target lookup, or inferred-view measurement in the exporter/Circuit JSON contract. Core will perform native geometry interpretation, measurement, projection and layout before emitting these records. Width/height intent remains in props.

`showEdgeNames: true` adds small gray feature names. With only resolved dimension metadata, labels use the witness points (or the line midpoint). Optional `resolveModelEdges(view, input)` enumerates all native named features, even without dimensions. Its runtime samples remain outside Circuit JSON and use the same camera as the part raster. Duplicate names are deduplicated, coincident labels are separated, and dimension text is reserved. Labels are disabled by default; their model callback is never invoked in that mode.

The rounded tube demonstrations use the actual collected JSCAD solid and native extrusion outlines, with a shared indexed mesh converter. Test-only upstream preparation emits 34.0 mm bore, 40.0 mm outer width, 20.0 mm height and 80.0 mm length at explicit 1:1 scale. Native model geometry/topology stay with their readers.

Validation: all 14 tests pass (665 assertions), with exactly one test and one visual SVG per test file. Typecheck and formatting pass. Coverage includes horizontal/vertical/diagonal/reversed lines, independent witnesses, supplied text versus paper span, moved/scaled views, sections, XML escaping, input immutability, page bounds, default-off callbacks and native edge labels without dimensions. Real model/drawing snapshots were visually inspected.

![Tube resolved dimension lines](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-drawing/feat/named-edge-dimensions/tests/__snapshots__/named-edge-dimensions.snap.svg)

![Optional gray feature names](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-drawing/feat/named-edge-dimensions/tests/__snapshots__/show-edge-names.snap.svg)

Related: [props #953](https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/953), [Circuit JSON #922](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/pull/922), [Fiber #142](https://github.com/tscircuit/jscad-fiber/pull/142), and [JSCAD #504](https://github.com/tscircuit/jscad-electronics/pull/504).
