title: Add assembly drawing dimension authoring props
description: Adds assembly.drawing.dimension with exactly one authoring target: a model-defined edgeRef, widthOfView, or heightOfView, plus optional stable name.
body:
Adds `<assembly.drawing.dimension>` with exactly one authoring target: a model-defined `edgeRef`, `widthOfView`, or `heightOfView`, plus optional stable `name`.

Models declare native outlines directly on `ExtrudeLinear` using `topOutlineName` and `bottomOutlineName`. The tube example selects `edgeRef=".tube > .inner_top"`; its actual bore spans 34 mm and outer outline spans 40 mm. Width/height flags remain authoring props.

Core will resolve the selected geometry, infer placement and measurement text, then emit a `drawing_dimension_line` with paper-space `start`/`end`, required preformatted `text`, optional `edge_ref_start`/`edge_ref_end` witness points, and optional `edge_ref_name`. Core generation is follow-up work. Native model geometry and topology stay in the model reader.

Removes the unreleased `orientation`, `offset`, and `precision` props. There are no layout defaults. Exactly one real selector or true view flag is required; false flags do not select a target. Exported types expose only the four authoring fields; runtime parsing strips unknown fields.

Validation: all 726 tests (7 snapshots), typecheck, ESM/DTS build, formatting, and all four required documentation generators pass locally. Tests cover conflicts, trimmed selectors, false flags, nested annotations, and the exact public/canonical props shape.

Related: [Circuit JSON #922](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/pull/922), [exporter #3](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-drawing/pull/3), [Fiber #142](https://github.com/tscircuit/jscad-fiber/pull/142), [JSCAD #504](https://github.com/tscircuit/jscad-electronics/pull/504).

title: Use configurable copper pour opacity
description: Changes copper-pour rendering to use a configurable opacity, reducing redraws from eight to one and adding regression tests for various pour types.
body:
Copper-pour textures currently redraw each group eight times to compensate for the renderer's default 50% opacity. Upgrade `circuit-to-canvas` from `0.0.135` to `0.0.139` and draw each group once with `copperPourOpacity: 1`, using the option added in https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-to-canvas/pull/317.

Add a real-canvas regression test covering rectangular, polygon, and BRep pours on both layers. It checks full copper color and opacity, transparent holes and background, exposed-pour filtering for relief masks, and one draw per covered/exposed group.

Validation:
- `bun test tests`: 213 passed, 0 failed.
- `tsc --noEmit` passed.
- Formatting and whitespace checks passed for the changed files.
- Confirmed the regression test fails when the opacity option is removed, the original eight-pass workaround is restored, or opaque pours are drawn repeatedly.
- Build and Node bundle loading passed for the renderer update.

title: Gracefully ignore reference annotations in unsupported adapters
description: Plans with named profiles, outlines or extrusion caps now execute on adapters that do not support references. Missing naming methods evaluate the wrapped shape once and return its geometry unchanged. Adapters without reference naming support receive ordinary extrusion options with cap names omitted, so strict option validation also works (including an empty references namespace).
body:
Plans with named profiles, outlines or extrusion caps now execute on adapters that do not support references. Missing naming methods evaluate the wrapped shape once and return its geometry unchanged. Adapters without reference naming support receive ordinary extrusion options with cap names omitted, so strict option validation also works (including an empty `references` namespace).

Adapters can implement either naming method independently. Reference-capable implementations retain their existing naming behavior and validation errors; geometry errors still propagate. Plans are not mutated, and the planner continues to expose both naming methods as required authoring APIs.

Validation: 37 Bun tests, 293 assertions; TypeScript, formatting and package build pass. Regression tests compare named and unnamed geometry after JSON roundtrips, check strict extrusion options, verify partial adapters and single evaluation, and preserve implementation errors.

title: Support native construction reference names and extrusion caps
description: Serializes references.name and references.nameOutlines as plan operations and accepts topOutlineNamebottomOutlineName in extrudeLinear options, enabling native construction references and maintaining compatibility with existing adapters.
body:
Serializes `references.name` and `references.nameOutlines` as plan operations and accepts `topOutlineName`/`bottomOutlineName` in `extrudeLinear` options. Executing a JSON-roundtripped plan with `@tscircuit/jscad` produces native construction references such as `top.bore`, including full transform placement. Legacy adapters reject requested reference operations explicitly; ordinary plans and existing attachment-plane extraction retain their behavior.

Integration tests now use the released package from jscdn: `https://jscdn.tscircuit.com/@tscircuit/jscad/0.0.2.tgz`. The archive was downloaded and its package name, version, source exports and reference implementation verified. JSCAD publishes through the handbook/plop GitHub Packages variant of `bun-pver-release.yml`.

Validation: 35 tests, 277 assertions; package build and TypeScript checks pass against the released archive. Tests cover JSON roundtrips, signed cap placement, actual hole boundaries, named profiles, unsupported adapters and existing plane extraction.

Paired Fiber integration: https://github.com/tscircuit/jscad-fiber/pull/142.

title: fix: preserve authored footprint origins for CAD placement
description: Fixes CAD placement by preserving the authored footprint origins for asymmetric footprints, ensuring that changes in copper geometry do not affect model positioning.
body:
Addresses the core portion of #4628.

An asymmetric footprint's copper bounding-box center can differ from its authored origin. Emit that origin as `pcb_component.footprint_origin` and use it for explicit object/child CAD model placement, so changing equivalent copper geometry does not move the model. Layout transforms move the origin alongside the pads. Bounding-box placeholder models retain their existing placement.

Chips and both jumper implementations also emit the origin because they override normal component rendering. Main's polygon-bounds implementation from #4818 is retained without duplicating it.

Prerequisites are merged and published: tscircuit/circuit-json#913 (`circuit-json ^0.0.531`) and tscircuit/circuit-json-util#256 (`@tscircuit/circuit-json-util ^0.0.128`). The existing circuit-json override uses the same published version. No preview dependencies or eval dependency changes.

Repro: f7864e67. Fix: #4807, merged into this branch. **Review this complete PR against main.** The KiCad consumer change is separate: tscircuit/circuit-json-to-kicad#712.

Validation:
- 19 focused regression/CAD tests pass, including both footprint-origin PCB snapshots, all quarter-turns on both layers, nested placement and packing.
- Browser autorouter bundling test passes; main now includes the correction to its unsupported build option.
- TypeScript, ESM/DTS build, distribution smoke tests, formatting and dependency checks pass locally.
- Refreshed 43 PCB snapshots for the published utility's silkscreen rotation fix (#263). All 44 affected tests pass. SVG comparisons confirm label rotation/font changes, trace ordering, and a small Arduino routing change that reproduces identically on unmodified main with util 0.0.127.
- Latest verification on 07bd3c3a: main's checks ^0.0.264 update and the footprint-origin utility ^0.0.128 are both retained. Nine focused footprint-origin, CAD and polarity tests pass locally. Hosted CI passes all 10 test shards, type checking, formatting/dependency checks, build/distribution smoke tests and previews. Both fixtures use ccwRotationDegrees per the handbook.

title: Add native drawing references using @tscircuit/jscad
description: Models declare named construction features directly through normal extrusion components, allowing for native geometry references and improved integration with the JSCAD kernel.
body:
Models declare named construction features directly through normal extrusion components:

```tsx
<ExtrudeLinear height={80} topOutlineName="top" bottomOutlineName="bottom">
  <Subtract>
    <Rectangle size={[40, 20]} />
    <Rectangle size={[34, 14]} />
  </Subtract>
</ExtrudeLinear>
```

The viewer-free `jscad-fiber/model` entry wraps the supplied kernel with `@tscircuit/jscad`, evaluates the existing host once, and collects references from the output geometry. Each reference retains its native planar profile and full model-space matrix. Bottom is local Z=0; top is signed height after the final twist angle in radians. Geometry readers can bake transforms without changing reference placement. References describe authored construction geometry and do not claim persistent B-rep identity after CSG.

This delegates reference propagation to the shared kernel and removes the separate Fiber matrix traversal, feature callbacks and cap collector. Named Rectangle construction planes use empty native geometry carriers. Ordinary Custom geometry remains supported; the proposed Custom naming/reference props are removed. Explicit solid repair preserves native reference metadata when rebuilding polygons.

Plans retain cap names inside standard extrusion options. The paired planner executes them with a compatible kernel and rejects legacy adapters explicitly. `@tscircuit/jscad` now uses the released jscdn archive `https://jscdn.tscircuit.com/@tscircuit/jscad/0.0.2.tgz`. The planner dependency pins the updated #22 preview (`31ab47d`). Both archive integrity values are updated in the lockfile.

Validation: 32 tests, 241 assertions and 4 snapshots; TypeScript, formatting and all four ESM/DTS entry builds pass against the released jscdn package and updated planner preview (full TypeScript validation runs in CI). Cap tests compare every outline point against actual cap vertices under signed height, twist, full placement and scaled native profiles.

Open paired planner PR: https://github.com/tscircuit/jscad-planner/pull/22.

JSCAD's release workflow and jscdn archive are published and verified. The existing electronics demo remains pinned to its previous Fiber preview.

title: Fix Gerber openings for pill-shaped NPTH slots
description: Fixes the omission of copper-pour clearance and solder-mask openings for pill-shaped NPTH slots in Gerber outputs, ensuring accurate fabrication.
body:
## Motivation

The merged reproduction in #190 shows a fabrication mismatch: an ordinary pill-shaped NPTH slot is present in the Excellon drill output, but its copper-pour clearance and solder-mask opening are missing from the Gerbers.

## Changes

- Reuse the existing pill rendering path for ordinary pill-shaped NPTH holes
- Define the matching aperture, including any solder-mask margin
- Turn the existing reproduction into a regression test and update its visual snapshot

| Output | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Drill | Pill slot is emitted | Unchanged |
| Copper pour | Pill clearance is missing | Pill clearance is emitted |
| Solder mask | Pill opening is missing | Pill opening is emitted |

![Pill NPTH Gerber regression snapshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GokulPandi-M/circuit-json-to-gerber/3be964ff79c456c830e25efbd252c1443603a67a/tests/gerber/__snapshots__/pill-npth-gerber-openings-repro.snap.svg)

## Validation

- bunx tsc --noEmit

- bun run format:check
- git diff --check

The full suite reports 223 passing tests and one unrelated macOS CLI output-path failure in tests/cli-output-path.test.ts; that same case also fails in isolation, and this patch does not touch CLI path handling.

title: repro: pill NPTH Gerber openings are omitted
description: Adds a reproduction test for the omission of non-plated pill mounting slots in Gerber openings, ensuring that the fabrication layers align correctly with the drill output.
body:
## Motivation

The [KH-SK22D07-G5 switch](https://github.com/tscircuit/boosters/blob/4b8b330cf06cee8109edab00d8bba5973925da76/boostxl-uln2003/imports/KH_SK22D07_G5.tsx) (JLCPCB C5274511) has two non-plated pill mounting slots. Circuit JSON preserves both slots and the NPTH drill output emits them as `G85`, but the Gerber exporter omits their copper and solder-mask openings.

This makes the fabrication layers disagree: the manufacturer receives the slot drills without the matching copper and mask clearance.

## Reproduction

| Output | Current result |
| --- | --- |
| Circuit JSON | Round control hole and two pill slots are present |
| NPTH drill | Both pill slots are emitted as `G85` |
| Inner copper | Only the round control hole is cleared |
| Front solder mask | Only the round control hole is opened |

![Circuit JSON input versus Gerber output](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GokulPandi-M/circuit-json-to-gerber/d0a86ccddc2846fabaa22c6bc7969aed9249bbae/tests/gerber/__snapshots__/pill-npth-gerber-openings-repro.snap.svg)

This PR adds only a focused reproduction test and visual snapshot; it does not change converter logic.

## Validation

- `bun test tests/gerber/generate-gerber-with-pill-npth-repro.test.ts`
- `bunx biome check tests/gerber/generate-gerber-with-pill-npth-repro.test.ts`

title: Fix: prevent empty supplier arrays and blank resolver data from erasing valid supplier part numbers
description: Fixes bugs in BOM export that caused valid supplier part numbers to be erased when empty supplier arrays or blank resolver data were present.
body:
## Summary
Fixes two related bugs in the BOM export's supplier part number extraction that caused valid data to be silently erased:
1. An empty array (e.g. `lcsc: []`) was treated as truthy and overwrote a valid value from another supplier array (e.g. `jlcpcb: ["C12345"]`).
2. When a part resolver returned blank supplier data, it wiped out valid `source_component` data because the fallback accepted the blank resolved column.

Both bugs share the same supplier-part-number extraction path, so they are fixed together.

## Problem
Before this change, a part with:
```json
"supplier_part_numbers": { "jlcpcb": ["C12345"], "lcsc": [] }
```
exported with a blank `JLCPCB Part #` column. The code checked `if (lcsc)`, and since `[]` is truthy, it overwrote the valid JLCPCB code with an empty string.

Similarly, if a resolver returned `{ supplier_part_number_columns: { "JLCPCB Part #": " " } }`, the exporter accepted the whitespace-only string and dropped the valid `source_component` data.

## Fix
- Added `getFirstSupplierPartNumber`, which scans supplier arrays, removes whitespace, and returns the first non-empty value.
- The extraction checks `lcsc` first, then `jlcpcb`, and omits the column if neither has a valid entry.
- The resolver fallback now validates that the resolved column is non-empty before using it. If blank, it falls back to the raw `source_component` data.
- No CSV columns were added or removed. DNP logic and footprint selection were not touched.

## Test
Added `tests/supplier-array-filtering.test.ts` with three cases:
- `jlcpcb: ["C12345"], lcsc: []` exports `C12345`.
- `jlcpcb: [" C12345 "]` exports `C12345` (trimmed).
- Resolver returns blank supplier data, so the exporter falls back to `source_component`.

Two of the three cases fail on `main`; all three pass with this fix. The whitespace-trimming case already passed before the fix and is kept as a regression guard.

## Verification
- `bun test`: 32 pass, 0 fail (29 baseline + 3 new).
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`: clean.
- `bunx biome check lib/index.ts tests/supplier-array-filtering.test.ts`: clean.

title: fix: include simple_inductor inductance in BOM Value
description: Fixes the omission of inductance values for simple inductors in the BOM, ensuring they are correctly extracted and displayed in the output.
body:
## Problem
`lib/index.ts` extracts values for `simple_resistor` and `simple_capacitor`, but not `simple_inductor`. Inductors therefore had no SI-formatted value: `Value` fell back to the JLCPCB/LCSC part number when one existed, and inductors without an MPN also had a blank `Comment`. In the 26-board `dataset-srj24` dataset this affected 42 inductors.

## Fix
Added `simple_inductor` to the existing `si()` extraction path (`lib/index.ts:128-129`), mirroring the resistor/capacitor branches:

```ts
if (source_component.ftype === "simple_inductor")
  value = si((source_component as SourceSimpleInductor).inductance)
```

`Comment` still falls back to `Value` when no MPN is available, a resolved manufacturer MPN keeps precedence, and CSV sanitization converts `µ` to `u`, matching resistor/capacitor behavior. Supplier columns, DNP handling, and `resolvePart` are untouched.

## Test
`tests/inductance-value.test.ts` covers a 10 µH inductor (`inductance: 10e-6`) plus the two precedence cases: a supplier part number no longer replaces the inductance in `Value`, and a resolved manufacturer MPN still takes precedence in `Comment`. All three tests fail on the pre-fix code.

## Validation
- `bun test`: 32 pass, 0 fail
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`: clean
- `bunx biome check lib/index.ts tests/inductance-value.test.ts`: clean

Before: `"L1","",""," "`
After:  `"L1","10u","10u"," "`

title: fix: expand disconnected MST candidate graphs
description: Fixes incomplete minimum spanning trees caused by disconnected candidate graphs in the autorouting algorithm by dynamically expanding the neighborhood during processing.
body:
## Issue

The fixed 10-neighbor candidate graph can split a net into disconnected groups, so Kruskal returns an incomplete tree.

## Fix

Increase the neighborhood only when the tree is disconnected, then rerun the existing KD-tree/Kruskal logic. Includes focused tests and the two real sample24 net SVGs.

## Rationale

Candidate pruning must not prevent the tree from connecting every terminal. Already-connected nets keep their existing pairs and ordering.

Stacked on #3196. Leaves #3209 unchanged.

title: Reduce four-thread Pipeline9 repair runtime on current main
description: Reduces the runtime of the four-thread Pipeline9 repair process by implementing a deterministic directional clearance search and optimizing various components of the autorouting algorithm.
body:
Derivative of #3194 targeting main `72d3d4c`. Apply deterministic directional clearance search, compact edge/query kernels, cached fixed connectivity, and revision-aware clearance projections through [repair04 #50](https://github.com/tscircuit/repair04/pull/50).

The new projection path skips repeated no-op constraints when all endpoint revisions are unchanged and uses conservative bounds rejection before exact contacts. Pad revisions are recorded before interior projections so moving interior contacts continue to run. Pair order, sweep count, step budgets, routing geometry, and counters are preserved.

Main's worker scheduling and dependency improvements remain intact. Search allowances and the validated 1,024-pop probe are retained; explicit custom budgets can still select one direction.

Validation:
- repair04: 184 tests, 602,903 assertions, type check pass locally. Thirteen captured clearance cases match the pre-optimization solver's exact output hashes, iteration counts, and statistics.
- A local sample15 comparison preserves byte-identical output, 2,480,804 iterations, and zero DRC issues; elapsed time 93.289 → 85.681s, joint repair 44.425 → 35.470s. Local timing is a screen, not the dataset claim.
- All nine consumer test shards passed before the latest projection dependency update; checks on the latest head are in progress.

Target: at least 15% lower arithmetic mean 4T board elapsed time across all 16 dataset18 samples versus main. The first [same-machine benchmark](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3225#issuecomment-6370587674) measured `185bc9b`: 54.285912 → 47.310198s average (-12.84995%), all 16 solved, zero DRC issues/timeouts. That result did not meet the target. A new `/benchmark --dataset 18 --threads 4` comment measures the projection update at `001ce25`; its result is pending.

title: Fix false off-board warnings for asymmetric PCB outlines
description: Fixes false off-board warnings for components inside asymmetric PCB outlines by using explicit outline coordinates for placement analysis.
body:
Stack: [#47 — reproduction](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-placement-analysis/pull/47) → this PR — fix.

Placement analysis reports a component inside an asymmetric flex tail as 10.28 mm outside the board because it reconstructs board edges from `center ± width/2`. Use the explicit outline's axis-aligned coordinate extents in both the summary and per-component reports, with the existing rectangular fallback for missing or invalid outlines. The reproduction's component is now correctly reported as 2.22 mm inside the right edge.

This PR adds the shared bounds resolver, updates the reproduction's expected result, and adds regressions for translated outlines, outline-only boards, real overhangs and rectangular fallback. The fixture and SVG are provided by the base PR. The original NEMA17 board's false off-board reports also disappear when analyzed with the built package.

Validation: all 52 tests pass; TypeScript, package build and formatting checks pass.

title: fix: respect existing copper during dogbone site assignment
description: Fixes existing-copper collision bug during dogbone site assignment by ensuring that immutable input copper is respected and blocking segments are correctly identified.
body:
Stacked on #5. Seed dogbone matching blockers from immutable `input.traces` before assigning sites. Include wire→wire, wire→via, and via→wire segments plus the physical layer span and copper diameter of each existing barrel. Explicit connection-name/source-trace ownership permits same-net reuse; anonymous or foreign traces remain blocking. Input copper is never edited.

The four expected-failure regressions in #5 become ordinary passing tests. The unblocked escape snapshot remains identical, and a new completed escape snapshot shows the solver moving clear of the fixed foreign barrel.

Validation: `bun test tests/regressions/existing-copper.test.ts`: 8 pass, 0 fail, 25 assertions; source-only TypeScript check passes. Tests independently check barrel/segment separation and input immutability. Both visual snapshots were rendered and inspected.

![Completed escape clear of fixed barrel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/dogbone-solver/astra/fix-dogbone-fixed-copper/tests/regressions/__snapshots__/existing-copper-cleared.svg)

Benchmark effect: on the focused identical fixtures, baseline violates all four foreign-copper checks; this head passes all four and preserves the no-existing-copper snapshot. No fresh paired pinned base/head 11-case Blacksmith run or statistically meaningful runtime comparison has been completed. Historical legacy 11/11 used smaller vias and does not cover this adapter/manufacturing case. This PR is draft, not merge-ready; required benchmark results must be added before merging. No whole-board DRC, skew, coupling, or speedup claim follows from this local fixture.

AM3352 remains unrouted: the latest native Core/CLI run solved the checked BYTE1 subset, then naturally exhausted BYTE0 search after 635.9 seconds. A staged planning conflict between strobe routing and remaining fanout sites is separately reproducible; this patch fixes the confirmed existing-copper collision bug, not that larger planning problem. No manual board routing or CircuitJSON postprocessing is introduced.

title: repro: dogbone assignment ignores existing traces and barrels
description: Fixes the issue where existing input traces are ignored when assigning dogbone sites, ensuring proper handling of foreign barrels and immutable copper during routing.
body:
Existing `input.traces` are ignored when assigning dogbone sites. A source-to-bottom-plane escape can place its through-via on a foreign barrel or across an existing inner-layer segment. This is especially relevant when an earlier routing phase has already produced immutable copper.

Adds a portable 2×2, 0.8 mm pitch source fixture with 0.30 mm drills / 0.50 mm lands. Four `test.failing` regressions cover a foreign barrel and wire→wire, wire→via, and via→wire segments. Passing controls cover the completed unblocked escape, same-net reuse, and input immutability. Run `bun test tests/regressions/existing-copper.test.ts`: 7 pass, including four expected failures on the current source. The stacked fix will turn those into ordinary passing tests.

Visual snapshot (successfully completed local escape, inspected):

![Completed unblocked dogbone escape](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/dogbone-solver/astra/repro-dogbone-fixed-copper/tests/regressions/__snapshots__/existing-copper-unblocked.svg)

Benchmark effect: this PR changes no solver code. The focused fixture reproduces the collision deterministically; it does not establish whole-board connectivity, DDR timing/coupling, or legacy benchmark performance. No fresh paired pinned base/head 11-case Blacksmith run has been completed. Historical bus-lanes 11/11 results use smaller vias and do not cover this adapter case. Keep this stack draft until the required benchmark evidence is reported; do not merge based on these scoped checks alone.

AM3352 status: latest Core 0.0.2202 / tscircuit 0.0.3012 / CLI 0.1.2406 reproduced a checked BYTE1 solve, then naturally exhausted BYTE0 search after 635.9 seconds. The DDR interface and SBC remain unrouted. This repro isolates one confirmed bug; it does not claim this bug alone explains the remaining route failure.

title: Retry transient Apple ticket validation network failures
description: Retries transient Apple ticket validation network failures up to three times with backoff, improving reliability during notarization processes.
body:
The [Intel release job](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-standalone/actions/runs/39980517887/job/120509438142) passed notarization and stapling, then failed validation when Apple's CloudKit connection dropped (`NSURLErrorDomain -1005`, exit 68).

Retry only transient stapler network failures up to three times, with 10/20-second backoff. Print each attempt and Gatekeeper failures inline. Invalid tickets and TLS trust errors still fail immediately; notarization is submitted once.

Validation: all 13 signing tests and Bash syntax checks pass, covering recovery, retry exhaustion, permanent failures and credential cleanup.

title: Add JSCAD-compatible native construction references
description: Adds tscircuitjscad, a small wrapper around the upstream 2.13.0 kernel with ordinary native geometry outputs.
body:
Adds `@tscircuit/jscad`, a small wrapper around the upstream 2.13.0 kernel with ordinary native geometry outputs.

`references.nameOutlines(profile, { outer, hole })` names actual post-CSG boundaries; `extrudeLinear({ topOutlineName, bottomOutlineName }, profile)` adds cap names and children such as `top.bore`. `references.get` returns a native planar geometry snapshot and full model-space matrix. Public transforms, CSG and shape operations carry authored construction references, including through geometry-reader transform baking. Ambiguous boundaries, duplicate names and missing references fail explicitly. This does not claim persistent B-rep edge tracking after topology changes.

Validation: TypeScript and formatting pass; 5 Bun tests with 27 assertions and 5 PoppyGL SVG snapshots cover backwards compatibility, holes, signed/twisted caps, transforms, CSG and construction datums. Runtime is browser-safe; rendering dependencies are development-only. CI checks and immutable package-preview publication pass.

Repository provisioned via https://github.com/tscircuit/create-repo/pull/101.

- Planner: https://github.com/tscircuit/jscad-planner/pull/22
- Fiber: https://github.com/tscircuit/jscad-fiber/pull/142
